### US-13 · Review before save
As a user, I review extracted values in a metric×date matrix (mirroring the live timeline), can edit any value (tagged `lab_import_edited`), and only what I confirm is saved.
- AC1: Dedup: documents on `sourceFileName`, lab values on `(metric, recorded_at)` — re-uploading the same file is a no-op, not an error or duplicate. **Widened 2026-09-04 (US-35 AC6):** a document is also already-imported when a live row carries the bytes' `contentHash` (`sha256-<hex>`) — ONE dedup key shared with the connector, so a rename defeats the name check but not the hash; a hash on a row WITHOUT a `fileRef` is the connector's metadata-only import, and uploading that same PDF on the website archives the blob into a new row and tombstones the metadata-only one. **Fixed 2026-09-07 (website read-back DEFECT B):** the review step offers Save even with every value already recorded when the bytes match such a row ("Nothing new to save. Save will archive the original PDF…", button "Save 1 Original") — `ReviewTable.archive.test.tsx`, `archive-payloads.test.ts` (`connectorOriginals`). Same day, widened to every document type: a clinic letter the connector filed is name-deduped to an UNSELECTED row, so it never reached the archive step; now a hash match on a `fileRef`-less row counts it as an original too, Save is offered, and `handleSave` files it with its reviewed content (`connectorDocumentEntries`) so the store tombstones the hash-only row exactly as for a lab PDF (`roadmap-store-data-safety.test.ts`, both types). Re-selecting the row saves it as a document instead, never both. **Fixed 2026-09-07 (DEFECT C, Sentry 7715862604):** a title with an em dash (or a macron, or an emoji) broke the Dropbox `Dropbox-API-Arg` header — now `dropboxApiArg()` escapes non-ASCII as `\uXXXX` for every content call (`dropbox.test.ts`, `dropbox-rest.test.ts`) — and a failed blob write behind a connector row no longer files a plain duplicate: the connector row stays live, `bulkSaveDocuments` returns `errorCount`, and the modal's "could not be saved" notice asks for a retry (`roadmap-store-data-safety.test.ts`).
- AC2: Edited-at-review values carry the edited source for audit.
- AC3 (added 2026-09-03 as US-32 AC24, restated here because it is this table's behavior): when the document carries a number for a `(metric, day)` an active row already holds, the review table shows the CONFLICT — record value, document value, and a Replace checkbox UNCHECKED by default — instead of dropping the document's number; equal values are context, not a conflict; Replace is written as a correction (`correctsId`, old row `entered-in-error`, original date). Nothing auto-supersedes on source rank. For a core metric, "equal" is the stored canonical value within float noise, not the displayed text (2026-10-13): Lp(a) in whole mg/dL rendered 124 and 125 nmol/L both as "50" (one decimal place since, 49.6 and 50.0), and in nmol/L 124.5 and 125 both render "125"; each pair crosses the Elevated line. A pair that rounds alike but differs now shows as a conflict, Replace unticked, so nothing is written unless asked. Comparing on canonical values also reaches older rounded rows of every core metric: an LDL of 3.4 mmol/L saved as 3.3876 through a US display (131 mg/dL) now raises a conflict when the report is re-imported. Replace stays unticked, so nothing is written; the cost is noise. Additional lab rows compare quantity, held SI against the printed unit, with health-core's `sameLabQuantity`, the connector's rule too (2026-10-16, US-35 AC6); before that they compared text, so 50 ng/mL over a held 50 nmol/L read as equal.
- AC4 (added 2026-10-13, with US-05 AC1): an untouched value saves exactly what was extracted, never a value re-derived from its rounded display (Lp(a) 124.5 nmol/L shows "125" in nmol/L; re-deriving would save 125, Elevated; in whole mg/dL, before 2026-10-13, 124 showed "50"). A cell counts as edited when its text differs from the extracted value shown in the unit it was typed in, so a unit toggle alone edits nothing. Its colour grades the value that will be saved: the extracted value while untouched, the typed number once edited. After a toggle an edited cell shows its typed value converted to the row's unit and grades that, so what it shows is what Save writes (typed "60" mg/dL, toggled to SI, shows "150" nmol/L, Elevated; before, it showed "60" beside nmol/L and graded Normal).
- AC5 (2026-10-19, PR #154 by @robertaustinbell): a selected core value outside the form's input bounds blocks Save for the whole review and shows an inline error. Correcting or clearing it lets Save through; an unticked Replace is not selected. Typed text is checked in the unit it was typed in, even after a unit toggle. An untouched extracted value is checked at its exact canonical value, not its rounded display, so rounding alone never marks a valid value invalid; the inline error and Save read the same result. Retyping the rounded display of an invalid extraction counts as a correction; retyping a valid one's display keeps its exact value. Additional lab tests get no bounds.
- AC6 (2026-10-22, redone from PR #152 by @robertaustinbell): a document's date is its own, reviewed apart from the blood-test column, and Save writes only what the card shows. Before, the card and Save read the file's report date, so a letter with no report date saved the 1st of this month while its screening box promised the extracted day, and editing the date left that promise stale. The extracted date is read as the connector reads it (`validDay`): a past calendar day is kept, a timestamp keeps its day, and anything else (junk, "2024-13-45", "15/06/2024", "2024-02-30", a future day) is unknown. Unknown saves `null` and shows "Date unknown" over an empty picker. A month alone ("2024-06", Brad 2026-10-19) leaves the day blank, "— Jun '24" over an empty picker, and saves `null` until the user picks a day, never the 1st by default; its screening update keeps the month ("2024-06"). A picked past day saves; a future pick is refused and not written; clearing the picker makes it unknown again, its month too, so the screening box has no date and writes nothing. The screening box names the date it will write, follows every edit, is disabled with no date, and an untick survives date edits. The archive-only path files what the review shows (`reviewed` in `onSave`): an unselected document behind a metadata-only row (US-13 AC1, US-14 AC4) takes the reviewed title and date, and a lab original's archive row takes the reviewed column day, or `null`, never the extracted string. Tests: `ReviewTable.document-dates.test.tsx`, `UploadModal.session.test.tsx` "US-13 AC6".
- AC7 (2026-10-22, from PR #153 by @robertaustinbell): changing a new column's date keeps the review. A corrected value saves on the new day as `lab_import_edited`, in the unit it was typed in; a cleared cell stays excluded, an additional lab's too; an untouched value keeps its exact extracted quantity; every file sharing the column moves with it. Main already does this since AC8's re-keying by the value's place in the extraction; the PR's cases now guard it. A Replace tick never follows the value: moved to an empty day it saves as a first row, moved onto another saved row's day it is a conflict with Replace unticked, and a tick there corrects that row. A move is never refused because the record holds some measurement on the new day (the PR refused any, a weight included). Decided (orchestrator call 2026-10-22, while redoing Austin's PRs at Brad's request; Brad to confirm): moving one upload column onto another upload column's day merges them, by design: one reading per (test, day), the loser named in the notice (US-12 AC14), and the merged column then moves as one. Tests: `ReviewTable.date-edits.test.tsx`.
- AC8 (2026-10-19, reproduced on main by roadmap-64): a new blood-test column counts as dated, and Save is allowed, only when its date is a calendar day that has happened (`validDay`, which uses `isCalendarDay`; no third rule). Before, a full-day report date that was impossible or in the future ("2024-15-06", "2027-03-15") saved with no click, since the check asked only whether a day existed; rows are append-only, so it stayed. Now Save stays disabled until the user picks a past day for every new column that will write a cell (a column whose cells are all cleared needs none), a valid day changed to a future one disables it again, and `handleSave` refuses an unset column too. Typed text, a cleared cell and the touched mark are keyed by the value's place in the extraction, not by its column, so an edit or a clear made before the day is picked survives the pick, which re-keys the column; an edit saves as `lab_import_edited`. A saved row on the cell's day is judged against the edited value, never the extracted one, so an edit is never hidden as already saved: equal to the saved row, it saves nothing and offers no Replace, and a tick it had is cleared; different, it is a conflict with Replace unticked (review, 2026-10-19). A Replace tick is keyed by that place and the saved row it replaces, so a day moved onto another saved row starts unticked (review 2026-10-19). A date with no real month ("2024-13", "June 2024", "2024-15-06") shows this month with no day, never "NaN"; an impossible day ("2024-02-30") shows its month with none. A date cell with no day (`DraftDateCell` with `needsDay`: a column with no past day, and the document card's date) shows "— Mon 'YY", or its `placeholder`, over a picker that starts empty: picking a prefilled picker's own day fires no change, so a printed month's 1st could not be chosen. There is no Use button. The header stays one element, so later headers stay over their values. A valid past day still saves with no click. Tests: `ReviewTable.column-dates.test.tsx` (cases from the PR #152 review rounds: 2024-13, 2027-03, June 2024, none, 2027-03-15, 2024-15-06, 2024-02-30 and 2024-06 each need a pick; a month's 1st can be picked; a valid day saves; a day moved to the future blocks; today counts; one header element per column; an edit before the pick survives it).
- AC9 (2026-10-19, review round 5: the undated-column notice threw while rendering and the whole widget went dead): a review that throws while rendering is never a dead widget. The upload modal wraps it in the shared `ErrorBoundary`, given a `fallback` and a `feature` tag: the user sees "Something went wrong showing these results. Your file was read; please try again." with Cancel, which discards the review as the review's own Cancel does. The error goes to Sentry tagged `feature: upload_review`, with no component stack or props, through `scrubEvent`'s strict branch, as `feature: upload` does (review round 6, 2026-10-19): breadcrumbs, extra, contexts and the request are deleted and the exception value is replaced, since a review's click breadcrumbs quoted its values (the Replace label named both until AC10). The rest of the tool keeps the whole-tool message. Tests: `UploadModal.review-error.test.tsx` (a throwing review shows the message, reports once with the tag only, and Cancel leaves it) and `sentry-scrub.test.ts` (the real `scrubEvent` on an `upload_review` event with numbers in its message, exception, tags, a ui.click Replace label, extra, contexts and request: no digit survives).
- AC10 (2026-10-19, privacy and accessibility): no aria-label, title or alt in the upload review holds a value. Session replay and error tools capture that text, and the Replace box's label read "Replace the saved hdl value 1.2 with 1.4". Labels name the test by the label the row shows, and the column by its date in words, so cells in one row read apart: "Replace the saved HDL Cholesterol value from 2 Sep 2025", "Albumin value from 2 Sep 2025" (core inputs too, which had no name), "Sep 2025" for a column with no day yet, and "from the undated previous results" for an undated column not yet picked. A label may hold the test's own name ("Vitamin B12", "HbA1c") and a date in words, never a value. A screen reader still hears the values through `aria-describedby`, which names text, never an input (screen readers differ on reading an input's value from a description): the Replace box is described by the saved value shown in the cell and a visually hidden line that mirrors the typed one ("new value 1.4"), and a lab input by its unit note and the value Save stores ("→ 40 g/L"). When a lab conflict's two units differ, both sides show their unit ("15 µmol/L" over "100 µg/dL"), so each is seen and heard with it; before, the saved side showed a bare number when its unit was the row's. A long saved value wraps in its cell. A cell's validation error describes its input instead of copying into a `title` (`NumericInputCell`, every caller). The blood pressure cell in `StartingInfoVitals` does the same: with both halves out of range it shows both errors, one line each, each describing its own input; one error for the pair (a clash) shows once and describes both, and when systolic has its own range error the clash line below it describes both halves too. An input's own value is not a label and stays. Tests: `ReviewTable.a11y.test.tsx` (a review with conflicts, context, converted and refused units, edits and a validation error: no number but a test's own name or a date in any aria-label, title, alt or aria-valuetext, by the shared `a11yTextWithDigits`, which strips the names the rows show and still catches a value beside a name or a date; a digit-named test (HbA1c, Vitamin B12) passes; a month-only report names "Sep 2025"; the Replace box named with its date and described by both values from text, following an edit, and by both units; a lab input described by its stored value; one test in three columns, the undated one in words; an error describes its input), `StartingInfoVitals.bp-error.test.tsx` (either half out of range, both at once, a clash shown once, and a systolic range error with the clash describing both halves), plus the label assertions moved to names and descriptions in `ReviewTable.units.test.tsx`, `ReviewTable.archive.test.tsx`, `ReviewTable.range.test.tsx`, `ReviewTable.screening.test.tsx`, `ReviewTable.slots.test.tsx`, `ReviewTable.undated.test.tsx` and `NumericInputCell.test.tsx`.
- AC11 (2026-10-20, issue #166): a core cell shows what the report printed ("Printed: 1.5 mg/dL", or "(no unit)") whenever the cell shows something else, a converted number or a guessed unit; the note describes the input. The extractor's `question` shows in the cell, and any question makes a `high` value `medium`, so the cell is highlighted. A creatinine above 500 µmol/L (D6, Brad's proposal; a display question, not a clinical threshold, so the three clinical files are unchanged) asks "Was this a blood test?". The connector's `import_documents` candidates carry the same question and confidence through the existing `question` field (D7b), including the "unit was inferred" question on a creatinine it inferred and stored in SI (US-12 AC15, D7a, Brad 2026-10-20); the tool text is unchanged. Tests: `ReviewTable.units.test.tsx`, `lab-extraction.creatinine.test.ts`, `mcp-tools.test.ts`.

It saves the thousands reading only when that is inside the test's input range and the decimal reading is below it; otherwise the cell asks "Did you mean 1234 or 1.234?" and blocks Save, as an out-of-range value does (AC5). ### US-14 · Document archive
As a user, my uploaded reports/letters become organized markdown documents (+ original file when my cloud can hold it) that I can reopen in a lightbox.
- Note (2026-09-04, US-35 AC8): a file imported through the connector lands here as a metadata-only row — `fileRef: ""`, `contentHash`, sniffed `mimeType`, `extractedText: ""`, `metadata.importedVia: "connector"` — with the original left where the user put it; a lab report's row takes the shape the website's upload writes (`pathology_report`, hidden from the Documents list), since 2026-10-23 with its `labArchive: true` flag too (US-35 AC8). The website archives the blob behind such a row on the next upload of the same bytes (US-13 AC1).
- AC1 (2026-10-20, PR #186 by @robertaustinbell; moved here from US-12): GitHub and WebDAV document reads and writes URL-encode each logical path segment once, preserving folder separators and literal `#`, `%` (including the text `%23`), spaces and Unicode. A lone UTF-16 surrogate, including one created by title truncation, keeps the URL boundary’s previous U+FFFD replacement instead of throwing; valid surrogate pairs and a leading U+FEFF are preserved. Stored document refs and title sanitization do not change. WebDAV keeps the configured base URL's escaping and optional trailing slash. GitHub keeps its default-branch and SHA retry behavior and its private-repository write guard. Legacy reads: before this change the raw ref was joined onto the URL, so a document whose ref holds `#` was stored under the name cut at the `#`, and literal `%xx` text was decoded by the server. A read that gets a 404 at the encoded URL, for a ref whose old raw-join URL differs, retries once at that old URL (fragment dropped) and returns those bytes; a plain ref makes one request. Writes always use the new encoding. Two titles that differed only after a `#` were saved to the same cut name before this change, so the later file overwrote the earlier one; that earlier file cannot be recovered. Tests: `storage/document-url.test.ts` (real adapters, mocked HTTP requests, including WebDAV collection creation; legacy reads seeded at the old location for `#` and literal `%20`, both providers); live-provider acceptance is not verified.
- AC2 (2026-10-20, security; adversary R2 on PR #186): a document's file path never leaves its folder. The date in a ref comes from the model reading the uploaded file (`reportDate`, `documentDate`, only `z.string().nullable()` in the extraction schema), so a crafted PDF could return "../../x" and point a WebDAV or GitHub URL outside the configured folder. `buildDocumentRef` takes the date only when it is a real calendar day (`isCalendarDay`); anything else, like a missing date, becomes today's local date. The row's own `date` field is unchanged. Tests: `document-path.test.ts` "US-14 AC2" (`../../x`, a date with a slash, `..`, an impossible day, a short date, empty, null and undefined all give today's date in one folder).
- AC3 (2026-10-20, security; found by an outside scanner, verified in code): an archived original never runs script on the app's origin. "View original file" opens a blob: URL, and a top-level blob: URL runs with the page's origin, beside the cloud tokens in localStorage; an archived SVG or HTML file could read them. (a) The viewer opens a file in a tab only when its ref's extension names a passive type (`.pdf`, `.png`, `.jpg`/`.jpeg`, `.heic`) and the stored bytes carry that type or none (Dropbox and GitHub return untyped bytes); it re-types the blob as that type before opening. Anything else, an SVG, HTML, XML, a `.docx`, a mismatch (`.png` bytes typed `image/svg+xml`), an unknown or missing extension, is re-typed `application/octet-stream` and downloaded under its ref's name, never opened. A stored type that is a non-standard alias (`image/jpg`, `image/pjpeg`, `application/x-pdf`, as WebDAV or Drive may return) is a mismatch too: the original downloads rather than opens, which fails safe. This covers SVGs already in users' archives. (b) The upload reads a photo only by allow-list: JPEG, PNG, HEIC or HEIF, by type or extension. Any other `image/*` (SVG, WebP, GIF) is no longer read as a photo; it gets the "Could not open it ... not a PDF, photo or .docx file" notice (US-12 AC9) and nothing is archived. Tests: `file-kinds.test.ts` and `image-resize.test.ts` "US-14 AC3"; `DocumentLightbox.test.tsx` (an SVG, a `.png` typed SVG and a `.docx` download, a PDF from untyped bytes opens as a PDF).
- AC4 (2026-10-22, redone from PR #164 by @robertaustinbell; AC1 was taken by PR #186): a document row whose blob write failed keeps its bytes' `contentHash`. Before, it was saved with an empty hash, so a later upload of the same bytes could not find it and the document was listed twice. Now the row is a pending original, as a connector row is (US-13 AC1): a later upload replaces it, a new row with the blob, every such row of its kind is tombstoned, but only once the blob lands. A second failure behind a held row, a connector's or an earlier failed save's alike, is a settled outcome, never an error, so an original that can never be stored (a size cap) does not loop on "Failed to save". The held details stay, unless the review changed the title or date: then a new metadata-only row (same hash, the reviewed title and date) replaces the held rows. Either way the done screen says "The original file couldn't be stored; its details are saved." (`unstored`), never a silent checkmark. The rows replaced are read inside the commit from the record as it then is, so a same-hash row merged in from another device during the upload goes too (orchestrator calls 2026-10-22, after review). A first failure still degrades to a metadata-only row as before. It is replaced only by an upload of its own kind (Brad 2026-10-19): a lab archive by a lab archive, a shown document by a shown document, read by `isLabArchiveDocument`, not by the document type, which is the model's per-run guess. Otherwise both stay live: rows merge with `deleted` OR-ed, so a letter tombstoned by a lab re-read of the same bytes would be gone for good. A deselected letter is archived only behind a shown-document row, never a lab-archive one. One helper (`pendingRowsFor`) picks these rows for the card and the store. The review card of a document that will replace them starts from the newest one's title and date (2026-10-22), a missing date staying unknown, so a retry shows the earlier edits, and the user can still change them; what the card shows is what is saved (US-13 AC6). Hashless rows saved before this cannot be matched and are not migrated. Accepted trade-offs (orchestrator call 2026-10-22): a held row's unknown date wins over a fresh extraction, so a date the user cleared stays cleared even when the new read has one; and older same-kind rows for the same bytes (say from another device) are replaced although the card shows only the newest. Tests: `roadmap-store-archive-retry.test.ts`, `roadmap-store-data-safety.test.ts`, `UploadModal.session.test.tsx` "US-14 AC4"; `ReviewTable.document-dates.test.tsx` "starts from the failed row" and "starts from the newest such row".
- AC5 (one save path, Brad 2026-10-22: "I don't like code sprawl"): saving uploaded documents lives in health-core (`document-save.ts` `saveDocuments`), called by the web's `RoadmapStore.bulkSaveDocuments` and by the iPhone (US-52 AC13d, 2026-10-22, with the lab-archive row's shape shared as `labArchivePayload`). The web's behaviour is unchanged: rows, field values, order, dedup on `contentHash` and `sourceFileName`, tombstoning a hash-only row and replacing it (US-13 AC1), blob before the record, the metadata-only fallback with its hash (AC4), the first write per folder alone then three at a time, telemetry and error texts. The hasher and the bytes' type are the caller's, so it runs in JavaScriptCore too. The shared Dropbox and Drive adapters (`dropbox-rest.ts`, `drive-rest.ts`) write and read documents only when built with `{ documents: 'write' }`; built bare, they refuse with the same words as before and call nothing, so the hosted MCP server, which builds them bare and is under OpenAI review, is unchanged. The browser's adapters now call the shared upload, download and find-or-create-folder functions, and their own copies are deleted. Two stated differences on the web, both a token fetched once where it was fetched twice within one call (a token counts only with 60 seconds left). Tests: `document-save.test.ts`, `dropbox-rest.test.ts`, `drive-rest.test.ts` (default refusal with no fetch, opt-in write and read, two concurrent first writes into a new folder make one folder, a failed lookup is not cached), `app/lib/mcp-documents-guard.test.ts` (the server builds its adapters bare and imports none of the shared document functions), and the web's store suites unchanged.
- Tests: ✅ document-path taxonomy; ✅ view-original type gate (AC3); ✅ failed-blob retry by kind (AC4); 🟡 archive-payloads synthesis; ❌ store deleteDocument/readDocumentFile. Deferred.

## Epic E — Chat

### US-15 · Ask about my plan
As a user, I can ask the assistant about my suggestions; it answers with my plan as context, cites Brad's content, and its name matches the store I'm on (Brad AI / MicroVitamin).

**Decided (Brad, 2026-09-10).** The blog chat bubble (`widget-src/src/site-chat.tsx`) and the chatbot embed (`widget-src/src/chatbot-embed.tsx`) both read the widget's cached inputs out of `localStorage` (`loadGuestInputs()`) and send them as context with every message, and neither bundle sets `VITE_LOCAL_FIRST`, so the server stores the whole transcript. Both open questions are answered. The cached values keep being sent: the answer is worse without them, and they are the person's own values, already stored in that browser (since AC10, 2026-09-26, that includes their saved measurements, which may have arrived by a lab import, another device or an assistant, not only what they typed). The transcripts join the 30-day purge, so the text does not outlive the audit that needs it (AC8). The README and the privacy addendum now say that.
- AC1: Server-proxied on Shopify surfaces; BYOK on Pages (chat reaches no Brad server there; the build itself still calls `api.google-token` for Google sign-in, `api.reminders-v2` if the user enrols, and Sentry for scrubbed errors).
- AC2: `chat_opened` now measures adoption.
- AC4 (2026-09-07): Main-LLM, router and classifier failure telemetry contains only bounded diagnostic categories and numeric timing/counts. User messages, assistant content, provider response bodies, author identifiers and arbitrary error strings never enter Sentry events or failure-path console logs. Conversation storage is unchanged.
- AC4b: Discord admits at most three active responses and ten waiting messages. Further eligible arrivals receive the busy reply. Completion, provider failure or a failed wait releases its reserved capacity. Tests: `discord-bot.queue.test.ts`.
- AC3: A transient upstream failure — a 5xx whose body is not our handler's JSON (the Shopify proxy / Fly edge answered, not our route) — is retried once before chat surfaces an error. The send POST is retried only within an existing conversation; a thread's FIRST message is never auto-retried (on the stored surfaces a retry could mint a ghost conversation). On the stored surfaces the server-side dedup absorbs an identical resend; on the widget (AC7, nothing stored) the client re-serves its own last reply when the resend is byte-identical to its last user turn, and otherwise a retry costs one more LLM call and no row. Added 2026-08-12 from Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-1M / -22 (sentry-fix loop; scoped per independent review); widget wording 2026-09-10.
- AC6 (2026-09-09): GET/POST/DELETE reject invalid conversation IDs before database use. Omitted/null POST IDs remain new conversations. Route error diagnostics, including detached failures, never include raw database errors or IDs. `api.chat-privacy.test.ts` checks SDK envelopes and console output.
- AC6a: A supplied stored-conversation ID on GET, POST or DELETE must belong to the authenticated principal, including a guest, before transcript reads, model work or deletion. Missing and foreign parents receive the same not-found response. A GET naming an id with neither a session token nor a customer answers not-found without creating a guest session. A guest is its session token plus its IP, so a guest whose IP changes no longer owns its thread: a guest's not-found carries that guest's own session token (one the changed IP may just have minted). When a guest's send answers not-found for the stored thread, the server has made no chat write or model call (a guest session may have been created), so the chat client keeps the handed-back session, sends the message once in a new conversation on it, shows that thread and drops the unreachable old thread from its list; the message is neither lost nor sent twice, and the restart mints no second session. A signed-in customer's not-found is shown, never forked into a new thread. The resend carries the handed-back token directly, so it works even when the browser refuses to store it. Opening or deleting a guest thread that answers not-found also keeps the handed-back session and drops that thread from the list. A sessionless GET's not-found carries no token. Tests: `api.chat-ownership.test.ts`, `chat-api.test.ts`, `useChatState.test.tsx`.
- AC7 (2026-09-10, Brad's decision): A turn from the main widget — the surface that sends the health record with every message, identified by `localFirst: true` in the POST body, which only the `VITE_LOCAL_FIRST` builds send — writes no `chat_conversations` row and no `chat_messages` row: not the question, not the reply, not a title (titles are the first words of the question). The widget sends that conversation's earlier turns in the request from its own `chat-history.json`; the server uses them for the prompt and discards them. What the server keeps is one `chat_match_events` row per answered turn: the question text verbatim (Brad, 2026-09-10 — a number scrub was built and then dropped as over-complication: an adversarial review found nine shapes still leaking through it, so a scrub good enough to trust needed a second round of rules, and routing is about topics, not magnitudes; the audit needs the real question), the prior-turn context the router saw (on the stored surfaces only — a widget row keeps just `platform: 'widget'`, so it can never hold a second question), the matched handles, classification, router timings, and the fallback flag and category, so article matching can be audited. Honest limits: a question can name a value ("my LDL is 4.2"), so this is "no reply and no record", not "no health information". **Narrowed 2026-10-15 (US-15 AC33 review, S2; Brad confirmed 2026-10-16):** the widget row now stores the question with every run of digits, in any script, masked to `#` ("my LDL is #"), so a value typed into the chat for `run_roadmap` never reaches the row. A closed list of topic names that hold a digit stays whole when it stands alone (HbA1c, B1 to B12, D2, D3, K1, K2, GLP-1, SGLT2, omega-3, CoQ10, PCSK9, T1DM, T2DM, type 1, type 2, Zone 2), so "HbA1c 41" is stored as "HbA1c #" and a glued "LDL4.1" as "LDL#"; `router_raw` and `router_error` get the same mask (third review, 2026-10-15). This narrows the verbatim-question decision above: the topic words stay for the article-matching audit, the numbers go. A number written in words ("four point one") still passes. **Amended 2026-09-10 (public-repo privacy audit):** the question text is now kept for 30 days, long enough to audit article matching, and then removed; the handles it matched stay on as counts, so the audit signal outlives the text. A daily cron does the removal on every platform (`app/lib/chat-purge-cron.server.ts`, lock `chat_text_purge`): past 30 days `message` goes null, `router_context.first`/`.recent` are dropped, and `router_raw` and `router_error` are blanked too (2026-09-10 — the router's raw output is the model's answer about the question and the error text can quote it), while `matched_handles`, `classification`, the timings and `is_fallback` stay forever. `guest_chat_sessions.ip_address` holds a salted HMAC of the address (`hashClientIp`, HKDF from the app-proxy secret — equal addresses still match, no address reads back) and the session's audit entry carries no address at all, so a retained question is no longer linkable to an IP. The blog chat bubble (`site-chat`), `chatbot-embed`, Discord and YouTube store messages exactly as before, for router optimisation. `router_context.platform` names the surface on every row (`widget` / `shopify` / `discord` / `youtube`); the `chat_match_events → chat_messages` and `→ chat_conversations` foreign keys are gone, so a user's delete no longer removes router telemetry. A widget row carries only a whitelisted set of columns (`redactForWidget`), so a reply or error text cannot ride along unseen. Usage signal: daily `chat_match_events` rows with `router_context->>'platform' = 'widget'` against the prior 7-day shopify total (widget and blog were one number before this change), `chat_opened` steady, Sentry "Chat sendMessage failed" flat. No new `product_events` name: `trackProductEvent` fires once per session per name, so a per-turn event cannot live there. **The history went with the decision (Brad, 2026-09-10):** the 266 widget conversations stored before it — 211 guest-owned plus 55 from before the local-first cutover — were deleted on 2026-09-10 (the statement lives in `supabase/rls-policies.sql`). The 8 profile-owned blog conversations were kept: that surface still stores transcripts, and Brad wants them for router optimisation.
- AC8 (2026-09-10, Brad's decision): The stored Shopify transcripts join the 30-day window AC7 built. The same daily cron (`app/lib/chat-purge-cron.server.ts`, lock `chat_text_purge`) runs two more passes under the predicate `platform in ('shopify','discord')`, reached from `chat_messages` through a PostgREST `!inner` embed so a message qualifies only on its own conversation's platform. Past 30 days by `created_at`, `chat_messages.content` goes null; past 30 days by `updated_at`, `chat_conversations.title` goes null, because a title is the first words of the question. A thread resumed after that shows as Untitled: the title is set on insert only and is not refilled. YouTube rows are never selected: those turns are public comments on a video, under their own retention. **Amended 2026-09-10 (evening), Brad's decision:** Discord joined the predicate. A question typed at the bot is as private as one typed into the bubble, so its transcripts are blanked on the same clock; only the platform list changed, not the passes. Discord user ids stay on the rows — the decision covers the text. The bot's own history load (`loadConversationHistory` in `app/lib/discord-bot.server.ts`) drops null-content rows before building context, the way the POST reload does, so a purged turn is never sent to the model and never dedups against a blank. What stays is the shape of the thread, not the words: the row id, `role`, `created_at`, `model`, the token counts, `is_fallback` and `failure_mode`, so the fallback and cost audits outlive the text exactly as the handle counts do. A blanked turn reads back as `PURGED_TEXT` = `[removed after 30 days]` in the GET messages response and in the audit renderer (`tools/chat-audit-pull.ts`); the POST history reload drops null-content rows instead, so a purged turn is never sent to the model and never dedups against a blank. `chat_messages.content` drops its NOT NULL in `supabase/rls-policies.sql`. The cached widget inputs keep being sent as chat context (the header decision above). Tests: `app/lib/chat-purge-cron.server.test.ts` (Shopify and Discord rows blanked, other columns kept, YouTube untouched, in-window untouched on both platforms, title only on stale conversations, idempotent, update error throws, no-progress guard throws) and `app/routes/api.chat-privacy.test.ts` (GET substitutes the placeholder; POST answers from the live turns only).
- AC5 (2026-09-07): Sentry accepts errors from the current Shopify main widget, lazy chunks, upload and chat bundles, and our Pages scripts. Unrelated scripts and misleading/rehosted URLs stay excluded. `sentry-bundles.test.ts` runs the real SDK filter with the production init options against the emitted build files.
- AC9 (2026-09-10, from Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-6E, sentry-fix loop): A `/api/chat` request without a valid app-proxy signature, once it reaches the proxy check, is answered with the 400 the Shopify library throws, never a 500, and is never a Sentry error (a bare GET with neither `logged_in_customer_id` nor `sessionToken` still takes the pre-existing empty-list return before any check runs — it reads nothing). `authenticate.public.appProxy` rejects by throwing a `Response`; the route's catch-alls re-throw a thrown `Response` so react-router returns it as-is, and only failures in our own code reach `reportChatError`. Before this AC two unsigned `curl` POSTs straight at the Fly host (2026-09-10 08:51Z) became "Chat: Action failed" events and 500s — the same issue id a real action failure would land under, and that message carries no cause by design (AC4/AC6). `api.chat.test.ts` pins both the POST and the GET path.
- AC10 (2026-09-26, Brad approved; wording corrected 2026-09-28 after adversarial review): The blog chat bubble and the chatbot embed send the saved record: the saved profile, the latest saved value of each measurement with its date, and the medications and screenings on record. Nothing typed but unsaved is sent. (The widget's own chat sends the same set, plus up to 24 dated values per measurement and what is typed on the page but not yet saved.) The unit system is the one the widget shows: a saved preference, else the detected one. After an erase the copy is emptied and the embed mutes (US-11 AC8). An erase made on another device reaches this copy only once the widget loads here. The copy of medications and screenings is refreshed from the store after each save, so a failed save leaves nothing behind. So a returning user, whose form fields are empty because the values are saved, gets answers with their numbers. The embed is not muted for a returning user with a saved weight, or with only blood tests. It reads the context when each message is sent, not when the page loads. The cached copy has one meaning, the saved record: HealthTool's medication and screening handlers no longer write unsaved form values into it. The context goes into the prompt only; nothing stores it (checked 2026-09-26: `api.chat.ts` and `chat.server.ts` write only the question, the reply and router telemetry). A reply can still quote the values, as AC8 and the privacy addendum already say.
- AC11 (2026-09-28, from the /simplify altitude review): The chat's plan counts the medications and screenings on record.
  - **The bug:** before this AC, the Shopify chat server read the medication and screening lists as flat objects. Both clients send lists, so the server got nothing, and it computed the plan as if none were recorded. Given rosuvastatin 40 mg and ApoB 1.0, the model was handed a "start a statin" suggestion. The Pages chat already converted the lists, so the two chats disagreed.
  - **Now:** one health-core builder feeds both. Every field is sanitized before it can reach the prompt:
    - medication keys are allowlisted;
    - numbers are bounded;
    - a screening date must be a real calendar date (month 01 to 12, and a day that exists in that month and year): `screeningsToInputs` drops any other, for the widget's plan, the chat, the reminder schedule and `get_plan`'s `due` list alike, so '2020-99' can no longer roll forward and read as "up to date", or schedule a reminder. A "last done" date (the six `_last_date` keys) must also fall in the current month or before it, as the form's own year and month lists do; the five `_followup_date` keys keep accepting future dates, because the form asks when a follow-up is scheduled;
    - strings are capped.
  - **Drug names:** a listed name passes through. An unlisted name still counts in the plan, exactly as the widget reads it, but the prompt shows it as "unlisted". The prompt never says "other", which is the form's own "Other GLP-1" choice and means something to the plan. An empty name is left out of the prompt, and a non-string name (null, a number or an object in a hand-edited file) drops its row, as `medicationsToInputs` does for the widget's plan. A name outside the character bound becomes a placeholder that means nothing to the plan. A test pins that no suggestion title carries a drug name, so an unlisted name never reaches the model.
  - **Doses:** the plan reads the raw dose, as the widget does. The prompt drops a dose outside its range.
  - **Data sent:** the browser sends only the fields the builder uses: no row ids and no timestamps.
  - **The values the model reads are the values the plan used** (Codex, 2026-09-28): `latestValues` come from the snapshot the plan was computed from, so an unsaved value the widget sends stands in for the saved one, and the dated series fills only the fields the snapshot lacks. Before, the saved series overwrote the snapshot, so the model could explain a plan built on 3.4 while being told 1.0.
  - **Both chats read the same context (round 3, 2026-09-28):** the Pages chat plans from the context the widget supplies, with unsaved typed values and lent drafts, as the Shopify chat does (AC10). Every chat on the page supplies that context, so the old fallback to the saved file was dead code and is gone.

- AC14 (2026-09-29, chat audit F2): a refusal (HTTP 200, `stop_reason: 'refusal'`) is a third outcome beside answer and fallback. The model's partial text is discarded; the user sees a fixed line: for `bio`, `general_harms` and unknown categories "I can't help with that here. Please raise it with your doctor or pharmacist."; for `reasoning_extraction`, `cyber` and `frontier_llm` "I can't help with that request." Web returns it as the reply with `isRefusal: true` and `isFallback: true` (the flag the widget's dedup reads; the widget stores it in the cloud chat history, so it holds after a reload); Discord posts it; no surface re-serves it on a duplicate send. On the streaming web surface, the partial text already shown is replaced by the refusal line when the refusal arrives; on the surfaces that post only a finished reply (Discord, YouTube) it is never posted. Rows carry `failure_mode = 'refusal'` with `is_fallback` false. Telemetry carries only the stop reason and the closed category (`chat_timing`, the Sentry warning tags), never text. A `max_tokens` stop keeps the answer, adds nothing the user sees, and logs its stop reason; a tool call it cut off mid-input is dropped, and a stop with no text is the fallback, logged with its stop reason (never a parse error). Tests: `anthropic.server.retry.test.ts`, `anthropic.server.stream.test.ts`, `chat.server.refusal.test.ts`, `api.chat-widget.test.ts`, `chat-dedup.server.test.ts`, `chat-api.local-first.test.ts`, `chat-history-store.test.ts`.
- AC15 (2026-09-29, chat audit F2): on YouTube a refusal skips the comment and keeps its claim, like SKIP_NO_REPLY; only a main-LLM failure is unclaimed for the next tick. - AC16 (2026-09-29, Brad's decision, chat audit F3): the web chat streams the answer. The widget POSTs `stream: true`; the route answers `application/x-ndjson`, one line per thinking or text delta, then a `done` line carrying exactly the JSON the unstreamed reply would have been. A refusal or fallback `done` line carries `isFallback: true`, and the client replaces what streamed with its content. The body decides the path, not the header: an `application/json` answer (an older server, an error status) takes the unstreamed path unchanged; any other 200 is read as NDJSON when its first line starts `{"type":`, so a proxy that rewrote the type still streams, and fails as before otherwise. Without `stream: true` the route is unchanged. Persistence and telemetry run after the stream completes; `chat_timing` adds `streamed` and `firstTokenMs`. Discord, YouTube and the Pages BYOK chat do not stream. `CHAT_STREAMING=false` on the server is the off switch: the route ignores `stream: true` and answers JSON, which the client reads unchanged (default on; docs/deploy-runbook.md). A stream cut off before `done` is reported as a network error and not retried, because the server finishes and persists the turn after a disconnect, so a retry would duplicate it on the stored surfaces; the pre-stream transient retry (AC3) is unchanged. Tests: `app/lib/anthropic.server.stream.test.ts`, `app/lib/chat.server.refusal.test.ts`, `app/routes/api.chat-stream.test.ts`, `widget-src/src/lib/chat-api.stream.test.ts`.

When the answer lands, the summary folds into a collapsed "Show how I approached this" toggle above it. Usage signal: `chat_thinking_opened`, fired once per answer when the toggle is opened (the client's per-tab-session throttle then keeps one per session). - AC26 (2026-10-04, Brad's decision; on 2026-09-27 two pasted analysis templates were stored at exactly 500 characters, cut mid-word before any lab value): a pasted lab report or "act as a doctor" template reaches the model whole. The web chat input and the server both take a message of up to 8,000 characters (`MAX_CHARS` in `useChatState.ts`, `MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH` in `chat.server.ts`); the old cap was 500, and the widget cut longer pastes silently. 8,000 is a ceiling against abuse and runaway cost on a public guest endpoint. A longer paste keeps its first 8,000 characters and the chat says "Your message was cut at 8,000 characters."; the next edit within the cap, or a send, clears the notice. The counter reads n/8000, and the server answers a longer message with a 400. No cut splits a surrogate pair: an emoji astride the cut is dropped (`cutText`). Earlier turns are bounded per path: the widget cuts each prior turn it sends at `MAX_HISTORY_TURN_CHARS` (8,000, never below the message cap); the stored surfaces' history is bounded by the server's token budget, and BYOK history by the 20-message count, with no per-turn cut on either. The router and classifier keep their own 2,000-character slice (`sanitizeForRouter`), unchanged: they need only the topic. The router telemetry row does not grow with the message: `chat_match_events` keeps at most the first 500 characters of the question, and of the earlier turns in its router context, on every web surface (`MATCH_EVENT_MESSAGE_CHARS` in `api.chat.ts`), as it did before; the router still reads 2,000. Accepted consequence, confirmed by Brad 2026-10-04: the stored surfaces (blog bubble, chatbot embed) now keep transcripts of up to 8,000 characters per message in `chat_messages` for the 30-day AC8 window, up from 500. Reply length is the chat prompt's business, not this AC's. Usage signal: `messageChars` on the `chat_timing` log line, the length as a number and no text, shows how often a message passes 500 and 2,000. Tests: `app/routes/api.chat-widget.test.ts` (7,999 and 8,000 accepted and passed to the model whole, 8,001 refused, the 500-char row, the `messageChars` signal), `app/routes/api.chat-stream.test.ts`, `app/lib/chat.server.test.ts`, `app/lib/chat-router.server.test.ts`, `packages/health-core/src/chat-history.test.ts`, `widget-src/src/hooks/useChatState.test.tsx` (the cap, the notice, the emoji cut).

- AC28 (2026-10-12, Brad approved; evidence: chat-health W41, `docs/loops/chat-health/2026-W41.md`): a router reply that corrects itself still routes. On 2026-10-07 the router sent a JSON object, then "Wait — correction", then a second object; the first-to-last-brace parse threw, and the turn got no handles and a `router_error`. Now, when that parse fails, the router takes the reply's top-level `{…}` objects (a brace inside a JSON string does not count) and uses the last one that parses and holds a `handles` list, so a trailing note or example object never overrides the answer. A reply the old parse accepted parses exactly as before; a reply with no such object fails with the same `router_error` as before. Known limit, accepted: when two handles objects are offered as alternatives, the later one wins, as a correction does. `extractJsonObject` is unchanged, since lab extraction shares it. The router harness (`tools/test-chatbot-matching.ts`) uses the same parser (`app/lib/router-reply.ts`) and counts a reply nothing parses, or one with no `handles` list, as an error, like an API error: printed, counted in `apiErrors`, and the run exits non-zero. Before, it scored that reply as a silent ∅. Tests: `app/lib/router-reply.test.ts`, `app/lib/chat-router.server.test.ts`, `tools/test-chatbot-matching.test.ts`.

- AC31 (2026-10-12, Brad, issue #135; reworked 2026-10-14, Brad: "when someone says analyse my numbers, we should run it through my roadmap algorithm"; this was AC29 until the merge with main, whose AC29 and AC30 came first): "analyse my data" reports the roadmap's own verdicts; the model does not compute them. The chat context (`buildChatContextJson`, health-core `chat-context.ts`) carries what the plan code already computes, and nothing new: each card's `description` (the text the user sees), `derivedValues` (BMI, BMI category, waist-to-height ratio, non-HDL cholesterol, eGFR; the BMI category and eGFR withheld for a known minor, as `plan.ts` withholds them) and `missingInputs` (the plan's gating inputs it lacks: `missingPlanInputs`, moved from `plan.ts` to `calculations.ts` and shared). The descriptions come from the plan run over the medications the prompt shows, so an unlisted drug name or an out-of-range dose never reaches the prompt (the Lp(a) card prints the statin's name and dose); a card that run lacks keeps its title and has no description. Payload for the OA1 profile: 3,187 to 7,603 bytes; 7,775 with AC33's `units` (re-measured 2026-10-15; the AC31 builder gives 7,615 on today's fixture). The rule, verbatim in `app/lib/chat-system-prompt.md` ("Your role"), 778 characters (677 until the AC33 review of 2026-10-15 replaced "what is on target", which invited the model to grade values the plan gives no card, with the no-card clause; the rule before AC31 had 1,190): **When asked to analyse or review their data with no topic named** ("analyse my data", "how am I doing?"), report what their roadmap already says: what needs work and their plan, urgent and attention cards first and the info cards in one sentence; for a value with no card or verdict in the data, say the roadmap raises no card for it rather than calling it on target. Take every verdict from the user data block (the cards and `derivedValues`); never judge a value against a threshold yourself. If the roadmap does not assess something or lacks a value (`missingInputs`), say so plainly; testing is for their doctor. With no profile, the roadmap cannot assess them yet: say it needs at least their sex and height, not that their data is empty (they may have entered other values), and do not build a plan. With no profile, values pasted into the message are no longer graded (the previous rule counted them). Why the no-profile sentence: production sends '{}' (`EMPTY_CHAT_CONTEXT`) whenever sex or height is missing, even when other values are entered (until AC36, 2026-10-18: now only for an empty form). Measured 2026-10-14, 3 runs each, through production `resolveChatContext`/`buildSystemBlocks` (`user_context` fixtures), arms production (origin/main prompt and builder) / previous (the 1,190-character rule) / shipped: OA1 3/3, 3/3, 3/3; OA2 3/3, 3/3, 3/3; E1 (empty profile) 6/6, 6/6, 6/6; X3 (values entered, no sex) 1/6, 5/6, 6/6 (production says "your health data is empty"; the first shipped wording, without "not that their data is empty", 4/6); X4 (values pasted, no profile) 2/3, 2/3, 1/3 (shipped: one reply was a pre-fill tool call with no text, one opened a numbered list with "To get your plan:", which the check's pattern counts; the first shipped wording 3/3). - AC33 (2026-10-14, Brad: when a user types values that are not in their profile, the bot runs the real algorithm code on the saved profile plus the stated values and answers from its output, never from its own reading of the algorithm document; saving stays the user's job; revised 2026-10-15 after a second adversarial review, below): the widget's chat and the Pages chat have a `run_roadmap` tool (health-core `run-roadmap.ts`). Its input is up to 20 stated values (`field`, `value`, `unit`, optional `date`; the form tool's field enum; the unit read through the shared unit table, so an unknown unit is rejected and the prompt keeps "ask, never guess") and an optional `sex`, `height` (`{ value, unit }`, cm or in, through the same unit table; feet and inches as total inches) and `age` (whole years), or a `birthYear` only when that is what the user said (2026-10-16: "born 1974" needs no arithmetic by a model that may not know today's date; age wins when both come and both are usable, and a refused age, not a number or out of range, falls back to a usable stated birth year (2026-10-18, Brad: a malformed age used to hide a valid birth year)). These make a plan for a user with no profile, and they also stand in for a saved profile's sex, height or birth year for this answer (adversary R9, 2026-10-16: the behaviour since the start, now written down). `runRoadmap` turns the age into a birth year from today's date, in January, so the plan's age is the stated one and the US-07 AC6 gate is exactly under 18: 17 is a minor, 18 is not (adversary R3, 2026-10-16: the model used to compute "this year minus age" without knowing the date). A stated age is rounded down (16.5 is 16), and an age or birth year sent as a numeric string is read, so a usable age is never refused: with no saved birth year a refused age leaves no age and so no minor gate (adversary rounds 3-4). A stated birth year is used as stated, without a month (a different year drops the saved month), so the gate keeps its conservative no-month reading. The tool's own description carries its usage rules: call it when the user states values not in their saved data and wants them assessed or analysed; use only the user's own values, not a family member's; pass exactly the stated values and units, and sex, height or age only if stated in this conversation; on an ambiguous unit ask first and grade nothing; answer only from the result; say nothing is saved; offer to pre-fill measurements, never sex or height, which go to the roadmap tool (2026-10-20, US-15 AC36). Neither prompt names the tool. It is offered only on a turn whose latest or previous user message holds a digit (health-core `chatToolsFor`, on the server and in the Pages chat; the form tools keep their rule): it reads only stated values, and offered on every turn it changed answers to questions it has nothing to do with (below); the previous message counts so that "Lp(a) 75", the unit asked, then "nmol/L" still runs it. Tools render before the system prompt, so the widget's chat has two prompt-cache shapes (the form tools, and the form tools plus `run_roadmap`), each cached on its own. `runRoadmap` lays the values over the request's own `guestInputs` (a stated value is the latest for this answer only; nothing is saved) and returns exactly `buildChatContextJson`'s output, the same anti-injection boundary as the user data block, beside `applied` (field names) and `rejected` (field names and fixed reasons, never a value or the model's own string). It refuses, each with a fixed reason, in this order: a date that is not a real calendar day, or is later than today anywhere on Earth (record-edits' `resolveRecordedAt` with `latestDayOnEarth`); a dated value older than the newest saved point for its field ("older than the saved value"; an undated value is today's), checked next, so a dated old value, usable or not, never touches a newer saved one; a missing or non-numeric value or unit ("value or unit missing or not a number"); an unknown unit ("ask the user which unit"); a number below US-36 AC4's unit-swap floors (`UNIT_SWAP_FLOORS`: LDL "3.4 mg/dL" is 0.09 mmol/L), or an HbA1c or creatinine under 20 stated in its SI unit (mmol/mol, µmol/L: "6.1 mmol/mol" is a percentage, "1.1 µmol/L" is mg/dL), again "ask the user which unit" (adversary R7, 2026-10-16: the band is for the SI unit only, so "HbA1c 3.9 %", 19.1 mmol/mol, is read); a value outside the input schema's range, with a reason by kind: blood pressure above ("treat it as a possible emergency and advise urgent medical care") or below ("treat it as possibly dangerous and advise urgent medical care if they feel faint, dizzy or unwell"), a lab above ("above the highest value the roadmap records in this unit: ask the user to confirm the value and unit; if it is right, suggest they discuss it with their doctor"; adversary R4; Brad confirmed the wording 2026-10-16) or below ("ask the user to confirm the value and unit"; reached only by an HbA1c or creatinine stated in % or mg/dL, since every other lab's ask-unit floor sits above its range's floor), and weight, waist or a stated height ("outside what the roadmap records: ask the user to check the value and unit"). Every refusal of a stated value except "older" and the "later" duplicate takes that field out of the run (adversary R2, 2026-10-16: before, only an out-of-range value did): its saved value and dated series are dropped, and so is any stated value for it dated that day or earlier, the same day included ("a later or same-day value for this field could not be used, so this one was not used either"; Codex R1, 2026-10-16: "BP 118/76 on 2026-10-14, 260/155 on 2026-10-15" used to plan from 118/76). So neither a saved number nor an older stated one answers for a value the roadmap cannot hold, and a newer usable value still answers over an older refused one (except height: it barely changes, so an out-of-range stated height keeps the saved one and the plan still runs; orchestrator, 2026-10-15); a blood pressure that is not a usable pair (one number stated, either refused, or the two dated on different days), which refuses both and takes the saved pair out, unless every stated number (one or both) is older than the saved reading, which then stands (adversary round 2, 2026-10-16: one older number used to remove the saved pair); a bare `heightCm` ("value or unit missing or not a number": height comes as `{ value, unit }`); and any stated age or birth year when the saved profile is a known minor (US-07 AC6). A field with any value past the 20-value cap is taken out of the run, even when an earlier value for it was read: a history pasted in date order puts the newest values last (2026-10-16). A refused age, birth year or sex keeps the saved one (simplified 2026-10-16, Brad's Option A: with ages rounded down a refused one is only nonsense, and removing the saved one lost the inputs eGFR needs). The protein-target card is withheld, with a reason saying so, only when the run has no eGFR although the saved data had one or a creatinine was stated in this run (the reason names the cause, 2026-10-18, Brad: when the run used a creatinine but has no age to read it by, it is "the protein target depends on kidney function, which needs the user's age: ask for their age", under `age`; when a value was refused, it stays "… left out until the refused value is confirmed", under `creatinine`): without an eGFR the card falls back to the standard 1.2 g/kg, which would quietly drop a kidney adjustment (Codex rounds 2-3, adversary round 4). A saved creatinine with nothing refused shows the card as the saved plan does, kidney-adjusted when it applies; a known minor's eGFR is hidden, not lost, so it never triggers this; the potassium advice already needs a known eGFR of 45 or more, so it fails safe. `withRoadmapRound` is the one loop all three callers share (the website chat's `getChatCompletion`, the Pages chat's `sendMessage`, the answer-check harness): at most one round and one plan run. The values of every `run_roadmap` call in the first reply merge into one run under the one 20-value cap (each profile field from the first call that gives it); the first call gets the result and every other gets "Not run: one run_roadmap per turn; use the first result." A form tool beside it gets "Pre-filled for the user to review and Save." (or the medication line) only when `parseProposedEdit` accepts it, since the client applies exactly those, and otherwise "Not applied: the edit did not pass the form's checks, so nothing was pre-filled or saved." The first reply, thinking signatures included, is replayed unmodified; the second call carries `tool_choice: none`, and its text is the answer; usage is the two calls' sum; a failed second call is the ordinary api-error fallback with no tool data, and keeps the first call's usage and the round's counts for `chat_timing`, the audit row and the counter. The streamed chat shows "Running your numbers through the roadmap" between the calls. Surfaces: the server sends the form tools and `run_roadmap` only on a widget turn (`localFirst: true` with `canApplyEdits: true`, AC19), whatever another surface's body says; Discord, YouTube, the blog bubble and the chatbot embed get neither, so no round. `getChatCompletion` takes both as options (`{ subscriptionTool, guestInputs }`); the route never sends the subscription tool on a widget turn (AC19), so the two meet only if a caller sends both: then, in a round, a `propose_subscription_change` call beside `run_roadmap` gets its own result ("Proposed: a card under your reply asks the customer to confirm this change …" for the call that becomes the card, "Not proposed: …" for any other), never the form stub, and the proposal is read from both calls, so its card survives the round; a failed second call is the fallback with no card, as it has no form edits. Prompts: the analyse bullet (AC31) no longer asks for "what is on target"; a value with no card or verdict gets "the roadmap raises no card for it". The Pages compact prompt's form-tools line reads "without these tools … Use them only when …", so it no longer forbids every tool; nothing else in either prompt changed for AC33. Privacy: the tool's input and output never reach `chat_timing` (which gains only the flag `roadmapRun`), Sentry or any log. The widget's `chat_match_events` row stores the question with every run of digits, in any script, masked to `#` (`redactForWidget`), so a value typed in for the tool never reaches it; the topic names AC7 lists keep their digits, and `router_raw` and `router_error` get the same mask. **This narrows Brad's 2026-09-10 decision to keep the widget question verbatim (AC7): Brad confirmed 2026-10-16.** A number written in words still passes. - AC34 (2026-10-16, Brad's decision, no benchmark): the classifier, lab extraction (single call, batch and BYOK upload) and the BYOK chat run on Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`), up from Haiku 4.5. Each request sends `thinking: {type: 'disabled'}` and no sampling param, built by `modelParams`. Thinking is off for parity, since Haiku 4.5 never thought, and because extraction must still fit the connector's 40 s budget (US-35 AC5). Haiku 5.5 answers `temperature` with a 400, so the `temperature: 0` shape and its branch are gone; an effort level sends adaptive thinking, as on the Sonnet 5 family. It also rejects an assistant prefill with a 400, so a malformed extraction answer is re-sent as the same request, once, within the same deadline, where it used to be re-sent with a `{` prefill; a second failure throws the same class-only error. Responses are read by block type, because a Haiku 5.5 response can begin with a thinking block. Cost: $0.10 / $0.50 per MTok for prompts up to 100K tokens ($0.50 / $2.50 above), a tenth of Haiku 4.5's $1 / $5, on about 30% more tokens for the same text; one live smoke call per hop (synthetic input, 2026-10-16) cost under $0.001 in all. The classifier's 923-token prompt now caches (Haiku 4.5 needed 4,096). Its output cap rose from 8 to 16 tokens: in the smoke, "MEASUREMENT", the longest label, stopped at `max_tokens` with all 8 used (the raw text was not kept, so whether the label alone or text after it took them is not known). The label is now read from the answer's first word, so text after it never turns a good label into ERROR, which silently fires the router; the harnesses (`tools/test-classifier.ts`, `tools/youtube-comment-dryrun.ts`) send 16 and parse the same way. Extraction caps rose for the ~30% token growth: 8192 to 12288 for full transcription in a batch and on the BYOK upload, and to 10000 for the website's single file (see below), 2048 to 3072 for the connector's metadata mode; unused tokens are not billed. Refusals, new with Haiku 5.5's safety classifiers and with no server-side fallback: an extraction refusal fails the file at once, with no outer retry, since the same request usually refuses again; a refused batch request, which still comes back `succeeded`, is a file error, never a parse of its partial text; on the Pages build the shared transport (`byok-anthropic.ts`) turns `stop_reason: 'refusal'` into an error carrying the website chat's line (AC14: a health-topic or unknown category points to a doctor), so partial text is never a chat answer, saved history or lab values. Not parity in every respect: with thinking off and no effort sent, Haiku 5.5 runs at its default effort, medium, and at temperature 1, the only value it accepts, so extraction is no longer deterministic between runs; every value still passes the user's review before it is saved. Extraction quality at this setting was not benchmarked (Brad's decision). Tests: `models.test.ts` (both Haiku 5.5 shapes, the production pins, Haiku 4.5 now throws, harness pricing), `anthropic.server.retry.test.ts` and `byok-upload.test.ts` (the re-send is the same body: no assistant turn, thinking disabled, no temperature; a leading thinking block is skipped), `anthropic.server.batch.test.ts` (the batch params; a result that starts with thinking), `byok-chat.test.ts` (the Pages chat body), `chat-classifier.server.test.ts` (the classifier body, its cap and the first-word parse), the refusal cases in `byok-upload.test.ts`, `anthropic.server.batch.test.ts` and `anthropic.server.retry.test.ts`. Follow-up (2026-10-16, after review). Extraction is one loop on one deadline: at most two calls per file, on the website and in the connector alike. The outer retry that made a malformed file cost four identical full-length calls is gone, so these now fail the file at once where they used to get one more try after 1 s: a transport failure that outlasts `fetchAnthropicRaw`'s own two HTTP attempts, an HTTP 500 or 429 (neither in its retry list), and an empty answer that ended normally (thrown as "No text" before the parse, so it is not re-sent). A refusal or a `max_tokens` stop fails the file at once, with no re-send, since the same request stops the same way; only an answer that ended normally but will not parse is re-sent. Each gets its own file notice on every path (single call, batch, BYOK) and both builds: "Not read. Claude declined to read this file, so trying again will not help." and "Not read. The file is too long to read in one go.", counted as `refused` and `tooLong` in `upload_outcome` (US-12 AC10). The website answers such a single file 422 with `errorCode: 'refused'` or `'too_long'` and no document text, and a batch result carries the same code. Monitoring: each stopped website file sends one Sentry message, `Lab import: extraction refused` or `Lab import: extraction too_long`, tagged with its path and, on a refusal, the bounded category, never text; a batch's messages go once, from the poll that sees it end, however often it is polled after; a connector file sends the same message (path `connector`) in place of its generic exception, and the assistant still sees `unreadable` with its hint (superseded 2026-10-19 by US-35 AC13: the assistant now sees `too_long` or `refused`, each with its own hint); a classifier refusal is its own message, `Chat classifier: refusal`, tagged with its category, where it used to read as unparseable output, and it still fires the router. The BYOK chat's cap rose from 1024 to 2048 tokens for the token growth; a cut-off reply is kept, as on the website chat. A batch result is read as the single call reads it, every text block joined. One copy each, in health-core `models.ts`: the stop codes (`refused`, `too_long`) and their mapping from `stop_reason`, which the server, the BYOK upload and the upload modal's types share, the refusal categories and their normaliser, the refusal lines (the website chat and the BYOK chat share them), and the classifier's labels, first-word parse and cap of 16, which both harnesses import. Throughput, measured once (synthetic text, thinking off, 2026-10-16): 2,041 output tokens in 9.3 s, 219 tokens a second including time to first token, so a full 12,288-token answer would need about 56 s against the website's 60 s non-streaming timeout. The single file's cap is therefore 10000 (about 46 s), its own constant (`SINGLE_FILE_MAX_TOKENS` in `anthropic.server.ts`); the batch and the BYOK upload have no such call and keep 12288 (`EXTRACTION_MAX_TOKENS`). The single file also gets one 60 s deadline for its calls, so a malformed answer's re-send gets what is left, not a fresh 60 s; a timed-out HTTP attempt is still retried once in a fresh window (`fetchAnthropicRaw`, kept for capacity blips), so the worst case for a very slow file is about 120 s. On the Pages build a `max_tokens` stop with no text is `too_long`, not `empty`. A Pages chat reply that ends with no text to show (cut off before any text, or holding only tool calls that did not parse) is an error, "Empty response from Anthropic. Try again.", never a blank answer saved to history, as the website chat falls back (`byok-chat.test.ts`). Streaming that call is the option if long transcriptions need more. Tests: `anthropic.server.retry.test.ts` (one call on a refusal or a `max_tokens` stop; at most two on malformed answers; the 10000 cap), `anthropic.server.batch.test.ts` (refused and too_long codes and their category, handed back, not reported; joined text blocks; the 12288 cap), `api.lab-import-v2.test.ts` (the 422 answers, the 60 s deadline, a batch's stops reported once), `mcp-import.server.test.ts` (the connector's stop signal), `models.test.ts` (the stop codes), `upload-api.test.ts`, `byok-upload.test.ts`, `UploadModal.outcome.test.tsx` (both notices and counts on both builds), `chat-classifier.server.test.ts` (the refusal signal), `byok-chat.test.ts` (the 2048 cap).

- AC37 (2026-10-14, Brad approved; landed 2026-10-19 as AC37, since AC31 to AC35 were taken and PR #168 holds AC36; evidence: Sentry 6Z, `docs/loops/sentry-fix/2026-10-14.md`): the router's output is counted. Every `chat_match_events` row on every surface (both websites, YouTube, Discord) carries `router_output_tokens`, the router's output token count from Anthropic's usage. A reply that arrived but failed to parse (cut off at `max_tokens`, a refusal) keeps its real counts, so the long replies this measures are not lost (adversary R1, 2026-10-18); a row with no reply (timeout, API error) reads 0, as `router_input_tokens` does, and its `router_error` says why; the column is null when the router did not run. The web `chat_timing` line carries `routerOutputTokens` beside `routerCacheReadTokens`. Both hold a number only, never text. Why it matters: on 2026-10-14 the router timed out twice in a row, and a slow upstream and a long reply (up to `max_tokens` 200) looked the same. With the count logged, latency can be judged against reply length: on replies that arrived (a slow success, a retry after a first-try timeout, a reply cut off at `max_tokens`), since a timed-out try itself has no reply to count. Usage signal: the column itself, read by the sentry-fix loop through the read-only product-health role. Ordering: `ALTER TABLE chat_match_events ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS router_output_tokens integer` (`supabase/rls-policies.sql`) must run in production before the code deploys, or every match-event insert fails. Tests: `app/routes/api.chat-stream.test.ts`, `app/routes/api.chat-widget.test.ts`, `app/lib/chat-router.server.test.ts`, `app/lib/youtube-bot.server.test.ts`, `app/lib/discord-bot.server.test.ts`.

- AC40 (2026-10-26, Brad approved on issue #271, decision 2; Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-79): an Anthropic API error names its cause. On 2026-10-26 every call returned 400 for about 12 hours because the org spend limit was hit, and Sentry showed only "Anthropic API error (status 400)": `fetchAnthropicRaw` discarded every error body, so the cause could not be read. A final error response now keeps one field from its body, `error.type`, checked against Anthropic's closed set (`invalid_request_error`, `authentication_error`, `billing_error`, `permission_error`, `not_found_error`, `request_too_large`, `rate_limit_error`, `api_error`, `timeout_error`, `overloaded_error`). A type off the list is `other`; a missing, unparseable, failed or over-4 KB body is `unknown`. The message, the request id and the rest of the body are never read out, so none of it reaches the console, Sentry, the thrown error or Supabase. The read is capped at 4 KB, runs under the request's own timeout and never throws, so a bad body cannot change the error or the retry. A retried status (502, 503, 504, 529 before the last attempt) still cancels its body unread. The type shows in the error message, `Anthropic API error (status 400) (billing_error)`, which reaches the Fly log, `chat_match_events.router_error`, `chat_messages.error_detail` and the Sentry title; it is a Sentry tag (`anthropic_error_type`) and extra (`errorType`). `(status NNN)` keeps its form, so `classifyChatError` and the connector's `/status 400/` read it unchanged. The streamed `error` event uses the same closed set, where it used to strip the raw type to `[a-z_]`. Not every cause gets its own type: Anthropic's own "credit balance too low" answer is a 400 `invalid_request_error` (the shape `byok-upload.test.ts` pins), so a spend-limit outage may still read as `invalid_request_error`, never as its message. Tests: `anthropic.server.retry.test.ts` ("US-15 AC40": billing and invalid_request types in the error, tag and log line; message text and request id absent from the error, Sentry and the console; off-list is `other`; empty, non-JSON, typeless, non-string, over-cap, mid-read-failure and endless bodies are `unknown`; the retried body is cancelled unread and the 503/529 silence holds).

### US-16 · Chat can fill my form
As a user, when I tell the chat my numbers ("my LDL is 3.2"), it proposes structured form edits that I confirm — it never silently writes data.
- AC1 (2026-09-25): one reply can carry several field edits: "120/80" is a systolic and a diastolic, and a weight can come with a waist. Each edit the page has a place for lands in the form, and the next save saves them all. Known gap (adversarial review, 2026-09-25): a blood-test edit sent before the blood-test matrix is on the page (a first-time user who has not given a weight yet, form stage 2) is dropped, and the chat still says it pre-filled it; an LDL alone is dropped the same way. It predates this AC; holding the edit until the matrix mounts is the fix owed. A chat value pre-filled into the vitals matrix is typed into its cell in the unit the chat stated, and the focus stays there: it no longer jumps to the email field, which on a phone pulled the page to the plan tab, away from the cell the user was asked to review. Found by the 2026-09-25 cleanup review: for a first-time user each edit rebuilt the form from the same copy, so only the last survived, and the next save wrote half a blood pressure.
- AC2 (2026-10-20, Brad: "the chatbot should be asking the user to input the missing values, which it can do either in the chat or in the tool itself"): the website chat (the widget's own chat and the Pages chat, never the hosted connector) can save a stated sex and height, with the user's confirmation. A third form tool, `propose_profile_edit` {`sex`: male or female, `height`: {value, unit cm or in}} (health-core `chat-edits.ts`), goes wherever the other two form tools go (US-15 AC19). The model passes the height as stated (5 ft 10 in as 70 in); the parser converts it to cm and holds it to the plan schema's range (50 to 250 cm), and refuses the whole edit for an out-of-range height, a sex outside the enum, an unknown unit or key, or an empty edit, as a measurement with an unknown unit is refused; the tool result then says "Not applied". The form writes sex and height on change, so the widget never puts the proposal into the form directly: a banner shows it in the user's units ("Save to your profile: Male, 178 cm?", or 5'10" for conventional units) with Save and Not now. When the profile already holds a different sex or height, the banner names the value it replaces, in the same units ("Save to your profile: height 178 cm (replaces 175 cm)?"; orchestrator, 2026-10-20). A field the profile already holds with the same value, as the user's units show it, is left out, and when no field changes there is no banner and no counter. Save sets the fields as typing them would, the profile saves through the same path (LWW profile scalars, US-10 AC6), and the plan computes. Not now writes nothing. A tool-only reply says "Please check the details shown and press Save to add them to your profile." The no-plan rule (US-15 AC36, `NO_PLAN_CHAT_RULE` and its copy in `chat-system-prompt.md`) now asks for the missing values and, once they are stated, proposes saving them with the tool when the chat has it; the user can also enter them in the roadmap tool. `run_roadmap`'s description offers the same. Both prompts' tool sections describe the new tool. Usage signal: `chat_profile_edit` with `{ field: sex | heightCm, choice: shown | saved | declined }` (once per tab per pair), the field's name and never its value; saved over shown is the measure. Tests: `chat-edits.test.ts` (in range in cm and in, out of range, a bad sex, unknown unit or key, the fixture round-trip, the ack), `run-roadmap.test.ts` (the stub, the refused stub, the description), `chat.server.test.ts` and `byok-chat.test.ts` (the rule), `HealthTool.chat-profile.test.tsx` (Save writes the profile and the plan computes; Not now writes nothing; feet and inches for conventional; the replaced value named; no banner for a value already saved, and only the changed field otherwise), `product-events.server.test.ts` (the counter's closed words). Tool-use fixture `profile-sex-height` ("I'm a 52 year old man, 178 cm") in `tools/test-tool-edits.json`, not yet run (paid harness; test key capped until 2026-11-01). **Review fixes, 2026-10-20 (orchestrator):** the tool and its edits go only to a client that sends `canApplyProfileEdits: true` beside `canApplyEdits` (the widget's chat from this build; the Pages chat always has it), since an older widget applied any edit that was not a field as a medication and would write a blank medication row; the client also drops an edit kind it does not know. A reply's proposal replaces any pending one (within a reply, a later stated field wins), the banner shows only fields the profile does not already hold, and erasing the data or the user setting sex or height in the form clears it. `sex: null` or `height: null` is absent; an unknown key inside `height` refuses the edit. The banner and the medication Undo banner stack in one fixed column (`.chat-banners`) that carries the Clarity mask (US-09 AC8). The answer-check fixtures require the proposal itself (`expect_profile_edit`). Tests: the above, plus `chat.server.run-roadmap.test.ts`, `api.chat-stream.test.ts`, `chat-api.stream.test.ts`, `clarity-masking.test.tsx` and `test-chatbot-matching.test.ts`.
- AC2a (2026-10-21, split from outside PR #207 by Austin Bell; reworked after review): a re-read that brings no erase keeps an unanswered profile proposal and the medication Undo, an empty record's included. Before, the page read an empty record as an erase and dropped them, so an empty guest's proposal vanished at the first re-read.
