Each banner now stands for the erase the record was at when it was made: `meta.eraseEpoch` and `meta.erasedAt` (`RoadmapStore.eraseIdentity`). An erase moves them, this tab's or another device's once this tab re-reads the record, and the banners go, even when post-erase rows came with it. The store takes in and announces a re-read whose only change is the erase (`contentOf` and `visibleContentOf` now include it), since an empty record erased again can differ in nothing else. The page also marks on the store the erase its screen shows (`RoadmapStore.showErase`), set at load, by each re-read it shows and by its own erase once the store holds the erased copy. While the store holds a different one, the screen's values are pre-erase: this tab's erase is still writing, its write failed (the store keeps the erased copy, the next hide retries the write, and the device mirror carries it to the next session; US-11 AC7), or the relay holds a remote change behind an unsaved profile edit (US-34 AC4). Then a chat reply applies none of its edits, medication, field or profile, since it comes from the conversation the erase tombstones; and Save and Undo write nothing and the banner goes (review R4). Undo's prior values come from the store, the copy the check reads, not the screen; so a form change still on its 300 ms debounce when the chat changes the same medication is not what Undo restores (review R1, 2026-10-21). The store itself refuses every write (adversary R6, 2026-10-21; it replaced the page's per-path guards, which kept missing one): from its own erase's swap to the end of that erase's write, and whenever the write's stamp is not the erase this copy holds. The stamp is the erase the page showed when the write was asked for: a keystroke or chat reply arms the medication, supplement and screening saves and the profile's 500 ms auto-save with it, a matrix save takes it as it is asked for, the first-time vitals fields' save as the field is left, a reminder enrolment as it begins, and an upload's screening dates as the upload's save begins (skipped outright when the erase moved meanwhile); a write that passes none takes the page's mark as it runs. This tab's erase also cancels the vitals fields' pending save. A global mark alone could not tell a save armed before an erase from one asked for after the page showed it (Codex R3, adversary R3). A document upload is stamped as it starts, refused before any upload if already stale, and checked again at its commit, since an erase can land while the blobs upload; the connector's metadata-only row it upgrades is tombstoned only inside that commit, so a refused upgrade leaves it as it was (Codex R1-R2, adversary R4). Every write method answers a refusal with its own error result, never a throw, and changes nothing: a measurement, correction, profile, medication, supplement, screening, lab, upload, document deletion, Lp(a) unit, email-capture flag or reminder setting; the last three now answer true or false too. A reminder token the record refuses is cancelled on Brad's server and the enrolment fails, as a superseded silent enrolment always did (adversary R2), unless the file already holds that token active (Google's lane hands back the existing token): then nothing is cancelled and the switch marker stays (re-check adversary R1). Callers show it as they show a failed save: a matrix keeps its draft and says it was not saved; an upload counts its rows as errors; a medication, supplement, screening or profile save says "That change was not saved: your data was just deleted, here or on another device", once per erase however many saves it refuses (adversary R5), and never for the leftovers of this tab's own erase, and the page re-reads, which also releases a remote change the relay held behind the edit (US-34 AC4), except during this tab's own erase, which throws the change away anyway. So a save the form scheduled before an erase, or the profile's 500 ms auto-save firing during it, never lands in the erased record, and a successful erase clears the form's save timers too. While this tab's erase runs, the whole form, both matrices included, also sits in a disabled `fieldset` (a number already typed into a field can stay on screen, saved nowhere). A save that folded a remote change in and then failed on a later pass now announces the change, so the page catches up (adversary R3). A chat drug or dose change resets that drug's escalation answer when one is saved or one the form holds is still waiting to save, unless the same reply states one. The change is judged against the form's drug and dose as well as the saved ones, so a chat dose equal to the saved one still resets an answer given after a form dose change not yet saved (Codex full review R2); only a saved answer is Undo's to restore (US-06 AC12, Codex re-check R1). A store replacement inside one page does not happen in production (`initRoadmapStore` runs once per page load; every connect path reloads), so it needs no rule of its own. A successful erase also clears the lab rows, documents and supplements the page holds, and every re-read now takes the supplements in too; they stayed until a reload (adversary R1). A later erase from elsewhere at the epoch already held now clears the matrices' drafts too, as a higher one did (adversary R6). The PR's first version announced an erase before the stored record was read, so an erase refused because the cloud could not be read (US-09 AC23) blanked the medications and screenings on screen until reload. Now that refusal changes nothing, on screen or in the on-device copy; the screen changes only once an erase lands. An erase whose write fails is not that refusal: the store keeps the erased copy and retries it, so the screen shows that copy too and the alert says the write failed (review R5). Whenever this erase moved the store's erase, written or not, both matrices' drafts and the Lp(a) check's kept answers go too, from the device and from the screen, so a draft the chat filled into a matrix the user never opened cannot come back after a reload and be saved into the erased copy (Codex full review R1). The page tells the two apart by whether this erase moved the store's erase, not by whether the screen is behind one: a refused erase while a remote erase is held back leaves the form, an unsaved edit and the banners as they were (Codex final check R2). Tests: `HealthTool.chat-profile.test.tsx` (an empty guest's proposal through an unchanged re-read, then Save; Undo through one; a proposal made after this tab's own erase kept; another device's erase written to a shared `MemoryCloud` and re-read by this tab's own store, for an empty record, again at the same epoch, and with a post-erase weight, at a higher and at the same epoch; Save refuses when the page was not told; an erase refused because the cloud read failed leaves the chat context and mirror unchanged; a successful erase empties the upload view's history; a chat reply during this tab's erase write applies nothing, makes no banner and writes no pre-erase medication back; a height typed during the erase write is not saved; after a failed erase write the screen shows the erased copy and the next reply shows its banners; a medication save scheduled just before the erase does not land in the erased record; a chat statin change resets an escalation answer still waiting to save; an erase refused while a remote erase is held back changes nothing on screen; a chat dose equal to the saved one resets an answer given after an unsaved form dose change; after a failed erase write a chat-filled matrix draft is gone from the device and the chat context; a height typed just before Delete and saved by the profile timer during the erase write does not land; a profile save refused behind a held remote erase says so and shows the erased record; a chat medication change armed before another device's erase is shown does not land after it, with one alert for two refused saves; this tab's erase and another device's both clear the supplements on screen; a supplement edit refused behind a held remote erase says so and saves nothing; and in `HealthTool.journey.test.tsx`, a vitals cell committed during the erase write reaches nothing), `roadmap-store-erase-guard.test.ts` (each of the 14 write methods refused, with its answer and an unchanged record, both while the page shows another erase and while this copy's erase writes; with no page mark and after the erase lands, writes land; a save whose later pass fails still announces a folded remote change; a write asked for before an erase is refused after the page shows it; a blob upload landing after the erase appends nothing; a refused archive upgrade leaves the metadata-only row; a same-epoch erase clears the drafts), `reminders.test.ts` (a refused token is cancelled and the enrolment fails; a reply landing after an erase the page has shown is refused by its stamp and cancelled; a refused reply carrying the token the file holds active cancels nothing), `UploadModal.outcome.test.tsx` (a screening date is written with the save's stamp, and not at all when the erase landed while the document saved).
- Tests: ✅ chat-edits parsing + the paid tool-edit harness (`tools/test-tool-edits.json`). ✅ 2026-09-25: `HealthTool.journey.test.tsx` (one reply carrying a blood pressure, or a weight and a waist, leaves both in the first-time fields, and a save saves both).

### US-59 · A signed-in customer can pause, skip or cancel a subscription in the microvitamin.com chat — **built 2026-10-16 (Brad: "it would be relatively simple just to add on the API stuff with Appstle so that people can actually edit their subscription via the chat", "the code should be shared"); off until Brad switches it on; not deployed**
As a customer signed in to microvitamin.com, I can ask the chat to pause one of my subscriptions, skip its next order, or cancel it, see exactly what will change, and confirm it with one press, so I do not have to email or find the account page. Deliveries stay every 3 or every 6 months, and nothing moves an order earlier.
- AC1 (commerce only, off by default): only `health-tool-app` with `CHAT_SURFACE=brand`, `CHAT_SUBSCRIPTION_ACTIONS=on`, `CS_GATEWAY_CHAT_URL` and `CHAT_GATEWAY_SECRET` set does anything; the education app never shows, proposes or routes any of it (`/api/subscription-action` is a 404 there). The gateway has its own switch, `CHAT_SUBSCRIPTION_MODE` off | pilot | live, default off.
- AC2 (identity from Shopify only): every gateway call is HMAC-signed (method, path, timestamp, one-time value, body) and forwards the app-proxy query Shopify signed on the customer's own request; the gateway checks that signature itself with the commerce app's secret. No field anywhere takes a customer id, an email or an order number.
- AC3 (facts and rules, no tokens): a logged-in commerce customer's subscriptions (product, every 3 or 6 months, status, next order date, and which of pause / skip / cancel can be proposed, with the skip's new date) go into the turn as a per-request block, cached 1 minute per machine, after the cached base. The gateway's tokens (single use, 10 minutes) never enter the model's context.
- AC4 (propose, never execute): the model has one tool, `propose_subscription_change` {subscription ref, action, optional reason code}, sent on every brand-surface turn while enabled (one cached prefix shape), except a widget turn, which is always a guest (US-15 AC19, 2026-10-16). A proposal becomes a card only when the gateway listed that subscription and action as allowed; otherwise the whole reply is replaced by "I can't make that change here." and the account-page-or-email line (never left under a streamed "press Confirm below"). While on, a signed-in customer's double-sent message is answered again, never replayed from the stored text (cards are never stored).
- AC5 (the customer's own confirm): `POST /api/subscription-action` {token, reason?} needs the app-proxy signature, a logged-in customer, a JSON body, a known reason code or none, and 10 a customer an hour; the gateway re-checks everything, makes one Appstle call and reads it back, and the card shows done, accepted (still updating), unconfirmed, or refused with where to go instead. A timeout, network error or 5xx between the chatbot and the gateway is unconfirmed, never refused (the change may have been made); only the gateway's own refusals are refused.
- AC6 (chat turn): see AC3 and AC4 end to end; "I'm jane@example.com, cancel my subscription" can only ever reach the signed-in customer's own list.
- AC7 (tools): `getChatCompletion` sends the subscription tool only when its caller passes `subscriptionTool` (the chat route does so on every brand-surface turn while enabled, AC4), alongside the form tools when a caller sends both (the route never does: a widget turn gets no subscription tool, US-15 AC19); a tool-only answer gets a short line, never a fallback, and keeps both a form edit and a subscription proposal.
- AC8 (card): nothing changes until Confirm; cancel says it cannot be undone; every refusal and every unconfirmed outcome ends with the account page and email (an out-of-date card also says to ask again; a change still being checked says so); the card's text is plain text.
- AC9 (state): the card lives with its answer in this tab only, never synced or saved; Confirm sends once however often it is pressed; a busy store leaves it open to try again.
- Usage signal: `subscription_action_confirmed` (name only), recorded server-side by the confirm route when the store accepted the change, so it counts on every bundle that shows the card (the site chat and the embed).
- AC11 (live pilot, 2026-10-18): the card carries the subscription's status; for a paused one it shows "Paused" instead of a next order date, and the cancel card leaves out "You could pause it instead".
- AC10 (live pilot, 2026-10-18): a request for monthly deliveries, another frequency or an earlier order date gets the rule (every 3 or every 6 months; an order date only moves later) and no account link; the model never says an earlier card is still waiting or tells the customer not to press Confirm (it cannot see the outcome, and the list can lag a change by up to a minute), and points to the card and the account page instead; a reply only about a subscription carries no medical-advice line.
- Tests: ✅ `app/lib/subscription-gateway.server.test.ts` (AC1–AC4), `app/routes/api.subscription-action.test.ts` (AC5), `app/routes/api.chat-subscriptions.test.ts` (AC6), `app/lib/chat.server.subscription.test.ts` (AC7), `widget-src/src/components/SubscriptionChangeCard.test.tsx` (AC8), `widget-src/src/hooks/useChatState.subscription.test.tsx` (AC9). The gateway side (private repo): `customer-service-gateway/test/chat.test.js`. Not yet: WebKit check of the card, and the live pilot test.

### US-50 · Topic masters: one current page per supplement, and the chatbot loads it instead of old posts (**added 2026-10-20**, plan: claude_business docs/roadmap-chat/chat-topic-masters-plan-2026-10-20.md, Brad decisions D1–D20)
As Brad, I want each supplement's reference page to carry my current view, and the chatbot to load that page rather than my older videos' posts, so answers reflect what I think now and a change of view lands in one place. Extends US-15 (chat) and US-42 (refresh rules for references).
- AC1 (master shape): a rewritten master has one-line frontmatter keys `reviewed: "YYYY-MM-DD"` and `sources:` (single-line JSON: name, url, checked, fingerprint); a `## Current view (reviewed …)` section whose every sentence cites Brad's posts (a link to the post) or his position files (products.md, the clinical files, the system prompt, the guidelines) as "(Brad's current guidance, D Mon YYYY)", each backed by a verbatim quote in the report; a `## Current evidence position` section, which never claims to be his view, is used when neither holds a position; a `## Brad's videos on this topic` list (date, title, one-line take, "superseded on X" where it applies); a review that agrees; and a rewritten index summary (check: US-42 checker extended for master keys; owner: orchestrator). Under `--masters`, `--check-ids` resolves every DOI and PMID in each batch file's references, retained ones included, one request a second, unless `--check-ids-cap <n>` limits it (the default without `--masters` stays 60).
- AC2 (post links): video posts may carry `topics: [...]` (master handles) and, only when the whole post is about one master's substance, `router: hidden`. Drug, lifestyle and test posts are never linked to a supplement master. Post bodies are never edited. `rebuild-blog-index.ts`, `BlogIndexEntry` and the claude_business `/blog-post` index writer carry `topics`, `router` and `reviewed` (check: unit test; owner: orchestrator).
- AC3 (router view): the router's index block, handle allow-list and stated entry count omit a `router: hidden` post only when its master's `reviewed` is on or after the post's `publishedAt`; every other post, every master and every pathway stays. `TOPIC_MASTER_HIDE=off` restores the full view. `ROUTER_VERSION` is bumped. The matching harness uses the same view. `loadBlogIndex()` is unchanged, so YouTube still finds every post by video ID (check: unit tests including a mixed-topic post and a newer-video-than-master post; owner: orchestrator).
- AC4 (no frontmatter to the model): `loadMatchedContent()` strips frontmatter before content reaches the answer model and before it counts against `MAX_BLOG_CHARS` (check: unit test).
- AC5 (precedence): loaded blocks carry a header naming type and date ("[reference — reviewed …]", "[video post — published …]"), plus the title and links. The answer prompt says the system prompt, products.md and the answer bank outrank every loaded block; a master's current view outranks a post published before its `reviewed` date; a post published after that date wins over the current view, since it may record a change the master has not caught up with; a reply says plainly when the position changed, as Brad's view on the doctor surfaces and in the assistant's own voice on the brand surface. Within a reference, only Current-view sentences that cite a Brad post are his view; posts and the answer bank keep the "Brad's stated views" rule (check: prompt test + answer fixtures; owner: orchestrator).
- AC6 (YouTube): a comment loads its video's post as today, with its publish date, plus the Current view or Current evidence position section of each master the post names, followed by that master's body sections whose heading names safety, side effects, cautions, interactions, contraindications or who should not take it (Brad, 2026-10-20), de-duplicated against the router-matched entries that actually loaded (a master the cap skipped still adds its sections). Each safety section brings the bibliography lines its [n] markers cite. Every master's view goes in first; a view runs to the next `## ` heading or `---` line, and one over 6,000 characters is dropped and logged. A master with key safety points adds those instead of its safety sections (AC12). For the others, safety sections fill the rest of an 80,000-character total (views and key points count against it) in topics order: first every master's Drug Interactions, then the Safety and Side Effects sections, never for a master whose interactions were skipped; each skip is logged with the master's handle (review rounds 1 and 2, 2026-10-20). Sections go in whole, never trimmed mid-section. The block's heading names both ("current view and safety notes"), and the prompt calls the safety sections evidence summaries, never Brad's view. A video published after a master's `reviewed` date wins on Brad's view today. The dry-run tool builds the same context. These sections never count as router-matched content for the reply-or-skip rule. A reply may say publicly that Brad's view has since changed (Brad, 2026-10-20) (check: unit test + a skip fixture).
- AC7 (lint): in `test:all`, static only: a post naming a missing master; a rewritten master without sources; a hidden post whose master fails the gate (warn); a current-view DOI missing from products.md for a product ingredient (warn). In the weekly US-43 lint: a master reviewed before its newest linked post; a source checked more than 35 days ago; a master whose current-view hash changed while a place registered for its topic in `lint-topics.json` (anchored by text, never line number) did not, unless waived in `lint-allowlist.json` with author and date; overlapping masters that disagree. Master hashes are written by each batch's publish commit. An answer-bank entry older than a master's reviewed date on the same topic is flagged (weekly). (check: lint tests).
- AC8 (review and publish): masters are written by Opus under US-42's rules, checked by the US-42 checker, and reviewed by a fresh adversary and Codex (adversary alone when Codex is out of quota, Brad 2026-10-20). A clean master publishes. Brad sees only the always-ask list: a recommendation that changes direction, a dose change, a safety warning added or removed, a licensed source or NIH disagreeing with Brad's latest video, any claim about a Brad product, and any change that touches products.md, the system prompt or the three clinical files (owner: orchestrator; Brad for the list).
- AC9 (web pages): after Brad's deploy is verified, the drstanfield.com article is updated, its ID resolved by handle through the API, the store chosen explicitly (`--edu`), the old body saved for rollback; then the microvitamin.com copy is rebuilt and published (Brad, 2026-10-20: commerce copies follow the master) (check: before/after `updated_at` snapshot).
- AC10 (triggers): `/blog-post` proposes `topics` and `router` for a new post and compares its position with each named master: same view on a rewritten master moves `reviewed` forward; a master not yet rewritten is queued, never given a `reviewed` date; a changed view queues a master update. A monthly local session re-fetches NIH ODS and the licensed source (only the sections supplement-wiki allows), compares normalised fingerprints, and queues a draft on change. No literature search (Brad, D4).
- AC11 (omega-3 brand, Brad 2026-10-20: products.md wins): on the doctor surfaces, when a user asks which omega-3 Brad takes or which one to buy, the bot gives the EPA/DHA criteria and says he takes and recommends WHC UnoCardio 1000 Fish Oil, with the products.md Amazon link, and says "Brad earns a small commission through this Amazon link." (Brad 2026-10-20: disclose commission; on YouTube that sentence is exempt from the do-not-copy rule and the length limits, and the products.md "what does Brad take" list follows the same scope); Dr Stanfield still sells no omega-3. The doctor posture and the competitor-brands rule name this exception. The brand surface gives the criteria only, since its posture never presents Brad's routine as an endorsement (check: prompt tests on the files and the assembled doctor and brand prompts in `app/lib/topic-masters-prompts.test.ts`).
- AC12 (key safety points, orchestrator 2026-10-21): a master with a view carries `## Key safety points` directly after it: 3 to 8 bullets ranked by clinical weight (serious drug interactions such as warfarin first, then who should not take it, then dose ceilings and toxicity, then common side effects), each one or two plain sentences with the [n] markers of the master's own References, no claim its safety, interaction or view sections do not already make, hedging kept, at most 1,500 characters (heading and body). On YouTube, the view and these points always go in, uncapped, and the master's whole safety sections do not. The points go without their reference lines and with the [n] markers stripped, since a marker with no line is noise in a comment reply (estimated 2026-10-21: about 3,000 characters per master, about 42,000 for 14); masters with key points never use the 80,000-character cap, which masters without them still compete under; points over 1,500 characters or with fewer than 3 bullet lines ("- ", "* " or "1. ") are dropped and logged, and that master falls back to its safety sections under AC6. The weekly lint warns (`master-key-points`) on a master without sound points until the retrofit lands; the batch checker's `--key-safety-points`, passed with `--masters` on new batches, fails it (check: unit tests `app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts`, `tools/knowledge-lint-masters.test.ts`, `tools/knowledge-batch-check.test.ts`).
- AC13 (a master over the content cap, 2026-10-21): when routed topic masters would push the loaded content past `MAX_BLOG_CHARS` (160,000 since 2026-10-22, separators counted), no master is dropped while a smaller form fits. A master has three forms: whole; reduced with its Recommended Dosing section (where the upper limits live); reduced without it. A reduced form is the master's header, an internal note ("do not quote… for anything not below, say the full page covers it and give its link"), then its Current view (or Current evidence position; a view of 6,000 characters or more is dropped as malformed, as on YouTube), its Key safety points (dropped when malformed by AC12's checks: over 1,500 characters or under 3 bullets) and every safety section (`reducedMaster()` in `youtube-context.ts`, AC6's section rules), followed by the reference line of every [n] those sections cite; when a reduced form loads, a dropped view or key points is logged once with the handle, as on YouTube (a master that loads whole logs nothing). Every entry leaves room for the smallest form of each master routed after it. A master takes its largest form that leaves that room, else the shortest form that fits, so a large first master yields. A non-master loads whole only if it leaves that room, so a large post routed before or between masters yields too. A master also leaves room for each later post, whole, when that post still fits with every routed master at its smallest form: a post has no smaller form, so masters shrink first, and [vitamin K, vitamin A, lithium] loads all three with vitamin K reduced. Otherwise the post yields as above. A handle the router returns twice loads once. A master whose smallest form cannot fit is skipped and listed, as is a non-master that does not fit (US-15 AC23). Every ordered pair of the current masters loads both, inside the cap: when [vitamin D, vitamin K] passes the cap (as at 120,000), vitamin D loads whole and vitamin K reduced with its warfarin section; when a large first master leaves no room, it yields and loads reduced. The tests grow real pages with filler the reduced forms leave out, so they pin this behaviour at any page size. Every ordered pair with one of the three largest non-masters before or between them also loads both masters, inside the cap: [lithium, probiotics, vitamin K] skips probiotics and keeps vitamin K's warfarin section (before 2026-10-21 the re-check measured 197 of 1,140 such pairs dropping a master with the post between, 42 with it first). Three or more routed masters whose smallest forms together pass the cap can still lose one. The connector's `search_knowledge` gives a master's whole Current view, up to 4,000 characters (US-41 AC7), since the writer contract puts who should not take it last (check: unit tests `app/lib/matched-content.test.ts` "vitamin D + vitamin K: both load, with vitamin K's warfarin lines", "every citation in a reduced master keeps its reference line…", "a large first master yields…", "every ordered pair of masters loads both…", "a reduced master keeps its Recommended Dosing when it fits…", "the separators count against the cap…", "a non-master entry that would overflow is still skipped whole", "a master whose reduced form still does not fit is skipped", "[lithium, probiotics, vitamin K]: vitamin K loads with its warfarin lines", "[probiotics, vitamin C, B vitamins]: a non-master first leaves both masters their room", "a non-master that fits alongside the later masters' reserve still loads", "every ordered pair of masters with a large non-master first or between…" (a post between two masters loads whenever it fits with both at their smallest), "[vitamin K, vitamin A post, lithium]…", "a handle routed twice loads once", "a reduced master logs what it dropped once…"; `app/routes/mcp.knowledge.test.ts` "a master excerpt is its whole Current view…", "every served master's Current view fits MAX_MASTER_EXCERPT_CHARS"; `app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts` "reducedMaster keeps the malformed-view check", its three key safety points cases (`reducedDrops`), and "a master the router picked but the cap skipped, even reduced, still adds its current view").
- AC14 (masters before older posts, Brad 2026-10-22): when a question is about a topic with a master, the master loads, not the older posts; an older post loads only when the user asks about that post. After routing, in code (the cached router prompt is unchanged), each `[article]` the router picks whose `topics` name at least one master (AC1: a reference with `reviewed`) is replaced by its masters in its slot, but only when every one of its `topics` is a master reviewed on or after its publish day, AC3's exact rule (`covered()`, shared with the router view): a post with any topic not yet a master stays whole (multivitamins-are-no-longer-expensive-urine: 5 topics, 3 masters), as does one newer than any of its masters, or undated (AC5). A post's masters rank by where the current message names their topic, earliest first, then by the post's `topics` order. A master's names are each part of its title before the colon, split on "(", ")", ",", "/" and " and "; each part also without trailing generic words (supplements, boosters, powders, powder, fish oil, oil, peptides, extract; a dropped "fish oil" still names its master); and its first word when that has a digit or hyphen or is in capitals of 2 or more letters (omega-3, NAD, NMN); a final "s" is optional. So "is the vitamin A in a multivitamin safe in pregnancy?" puts vitamin A's master first, "Is omega-3 better than B vitamins for the brain?" and "fish oil or B vitamins" put Omega-3 Fish Oil first, and "NMN" names the NAD Boosters master. The article also stays when it is named: the storefront chat is open on it (optional body field `articleHandle`, which `site-chat.tsx` sends from a `/blogs/<blog>/<handle>` path; the server treats it as untrusted, uses it only as a lookup against article handles and microvitamin.com slugs, ignores anything else and never stores it), or the message gives its handle or slug in a `/blogs/<blog>/<slug>` path or URL, or as a bare hyphenated word of at least 4 words ("calcium-rich-foods" and "resting-heart-rate" name nothing), or it is the YouTube video's own post. Naming reads the whole message as accepted (up to its 8,000-character cap), not the router's 2,000-character cut, as a lookup only, never logged; it is linear in the message (an 8,000- or 10,000-character run takes under 50 ms). The filter runs only on a turn the router ran: when the classifier skips the router, nothing loads and nothing is forced in. At most 3 handles, filled in passes: (1) every pick the router made that stays, masters included, in its own slot, never dropped; (2) for each replaced pick, in slot order, its first-ranked master not already in, in that slot (each pick owns a slot, so one always fits, and `replaced` lists only picks whose master loaded); (3) the open post, when the router picked nothing or one of its masters is in after passes 1–2 (picked or brought in by a replacement), then each post the message names that the router did not pick, router-hidden ones included, in the order the message names them (the YouTube video's own post is never forced in: it is already in the bot's context); otherwise the open post is not forced in, since the reader may ask about something else; (4) the ranked masters of every named, open or YouTube-own post that stays, covered or not, picked ones in slot order, then pass-3 ones (so a picked post whose URL the message gives loads as [post, first master, next master]); (5) the remaining masters of replaced picks, in slot order. The list is in slot order; a post added in pass 3 sits right after the first of its own masters (in its ranked order) in the final list, else at the end; duplicates drop. Pathways, guidelines, references and posts with no master topics are untouched. The filter runs on the web chat (storefront bubble, widget, app), YouTube and Discord; MCP `search_knowledge` is untouched (its own ranker, AC7 of US-41). The router harness's answer check and the YouTube dry run apply the same filter. Usage signal: `chat_match_events.router_context.replaced` (picks that gave way) and `.reduced` (masters loaded in AC13's reduced form), index handles only, absent when empty; `matched_handles` stays the router's own picks (check: unit tests `app/lib/router-view.test.ts` "preferMasters (US-50 AC14)" and "namedArticles (US-50 AC14)", `app/routes/api.chat-masters.test.ts`, `app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts` "…(US-50 AC14)" (YouTube and Discord), `app/lib/discord-bot.server.test.ts` "US-50 AC14: the row records…", `app/lib/matched-content.test.ts` "names each master that loaded reduced…", `widget-src/src/lib/assistant-config.test.ts` "resolveChatArticle (US-50 AC14)", `widget-src/src/lib/chat-api.test.ts` "the open blog post (US-50 AC14)").
- Usage signal: loaded characters per routed turn, and the share of supplement turns whose first loaded entry is a master (`chat_match_events`).
- Tests: 🟡 AC2–AC6 built on branch `claude/topic-masters-chat`, except AC2's claude_business `/blog-post` index writer, which is NOT yet done (a separate claude_business change) (unit tests: `scripts/rebuild-blog-index.test.ts`, `app/lib/router-view.test.ts`, `app/lib/chat-router.view.test.ts`, `app/lib/matched-content.test.ts`, `app/lib/youtube-bot.masters.test.ts`, `app/lib/topic-masters-prompts.test.ts`, harness tests in `tools/test-chatbot-matching.test.ts`). Answer fixtures (`tools/test-queries.json`, category `topic-masters`) and the YouTube skip dry run are pre-registered, not yet run. AC1, AC7–AC10 ⬜ not built. AC12 🟡 built on `claude/key-safety-points` (2026-10-21); the masters' retrofit is not done. AC14 🟡 built on `claude/us50-ac14-master-routing` (2026-10-22), unit tests green, not deployed.

### US-43 · The chatbot's knowledge base stays consistent (weekly lint) — **added 2026-09-29 (Brad, knowledge-refresh plan decision 6); deterministic half built and run, model half built and not yet run**
As a user asking the chatbot, the pathway, the supplement reference and the plan my answer draws on agree with each other, or they differ where Brad chose to; as Brad, a weekly check finds the contradictions and the knowledge base gets fixed, while my algorithm is only reported.
- AC1 (deterministic rules; no model, and no network unless asked): `tools/knowledge-lint.ts` checks every entry in `docs/blog` and `docs/guideline` (pathways left 2026-10-22, US-15 AC39) for citation markers with no reference line and reference lines nothing cites; DOI and PMID shape, and links whose text and target differ; bodies that cite Grokipedia, with the sentences resting only on it; a number plus unit in the `index.json` summary the body never states (the refresh plan's AC2 tokeniser); and product mentions above the stored baseline. `--check-links` sends HEAD requests for the due entries' DOIs and PMIDs, 1 s apart, capped at 500.
- AC2 (the report fits the loop): counts come first and the markdown report never passes 150 lines, however many findings; `--json` holds every finding.
- AC3 (the selector): `docs/loops/chat-health/lint-state.json` holds the last run date, the slice cursor, a hash per algorithm topic and, per entry, a content hash and product baseline. The due list is every entry new or changed since the last saved run, every entry paired with an algorithm topic whose text changed, and one of 13 stable hash slices, so a full pass takes 13 weeks. `--dry-run` prints it and writes nothing. Only `knowledge-lint-compare.ts --run` advances it: every comparison attempt is recorded, a missing, refused, truncated or unparseable answer marks it retry and leaves cursor and hashes alone, three in a row park it (listed, no longer blocking), a comparison's id carries both excerpt hashes so a body rewritten mid-cycle is compared again, and a capped run works through what is owed, oldest attempt first, over the following weeks. Dead links are checked once per identifier and reported against every entry that cites one. Algorithm-side findings print with both quotes, each cut to 200 characters, never dropped.
- AC4 (divergences are deliberate and written down): every rule, deterministic or model, consults `lint-allowlist.json`; a handle entry with no rule covers every rule and model comparison on that handle, and the compare step counts the model findings it drops; an entry missing its rule, its handle or pair, its reason, date or who stops the run. The loop proposes entries and never edits the file.
- AC5 (the model half has a known cost): `tools/knowledge-lint-compare.ts` builds the entry-versus-algorithm, pathway-versus-reference and reference-versus-reference prompts for the due entries and prints the token estimate and cost at the pinned Sonnet 5.5 price (`PRICES` in `models.ts`) before anything runs. It calls the API only under `--run`, refuses `--run` without a `--max-calls` cap, refuses a `--max-usd` that is not a positive number, and before each call stops if the spend so far plus that call's worst case (estimated input plus the output cap) would pass it. A response that fails to parse, or carries any finding with a missing or malformed quote, side, handle or severity or an unverifiable quote, is rejected whole: that pair's retry, keeping none of its findings and clearing nothing; every other pair's result is kept. An instruction-shaped quote leaves a `WARN` line naming the handle and the span (cut to 120 characters), never a queue item. A model item resolves only when its pair was compared again with both quotes inside the excerpts sent; otherwise it keeps its status and records `unverified`. A dead-link item resolves only on a run that got a 2xx/3xx for that identifier on behalf of that entry in this week's slice (a timeout, network error or 5xx is inconclusive), and every item a run covers records `last_checked`. A reference excerpt takes its dosing, intake, upper-level, safety and interaction sections first, and every side records characters sent against characters available, printed as a `CUT` line when it did not fit. The first `--run` waits for Brad's written yes on the cost line.
- AC6 (external text is data): excerpts and their labels sit inside the data frame; a closing tag inside one is escaped; the model has no tools. Injected text cannot reach the model as instructions; a planted finding is caught by the batch protocol (Opus writer, AC2 raw quotes, Brad's sign-off), not by this tool. The tool keeps a finding only if both quotes are verbatim in their excerpts and its fix names one of the two handles, drops one whose quote reads like an instruction, and flags instruction-shaped text rather than following it.
- AC7 (who fixes what): every knowledge-side finding joins `lint-fix-queue.json` once: model findings from `--run`, deterministic ones under `--queue` with their rule name, deduped across weeks by rule, handle and item (a repeat refreshes `last_seen`). Algorithm-side findings go to the report only, and a pathway against the algorithm is always algorithm-side; any other fix aimed at a pathway body is report-only, never queued. A fixed or resolved item that recurs becomes `regressed`; an open or regressed one that a run covered and did not see becomes `resolved` with the date; the Grokipedia item's detail carries the counts; both tools print open, regressed and resolved counts. The loop reports and queues; a build session (Fable orchestrating, Opus writers) fixes queue items under US-42's batch protocol (AC1 to AC8), and Brad signs each batch. No lint step edits `health_roadmap_algorithm.md`, `evidence.ts`, `roadmap_text.html`, `index.json` or the allow-list.
- Usage signal (declared): `metrics.csv` `lint_*` rows and the queue's open count, falling quarter over quarter.
- Baseline (2026-09-29, corrected run after the adversarial review; allow-list of 2 entries): 1,024 entries; 87 unresolved markers in 5 entries (73 in `diet`, whose markers point to the AHA paper's list), 207 uncited reference lines in 39, 39 bibliography-only lists, 1 DOI shape, 1 PMID shape, 3 links whose text differs from the target, 67 bodies citing Grokipedia (506 reference entries), 12 summary dose mismatches in 10 entries (now counting %, mmHg and pmol/L). Estimated model cost: about $0.27 this week; about $3.83 for the 13 weekly slices ($9.37 at most); $2.80 for one `--all` pass.
- Tests: ✅ `tools/knowledge-lint.test.ts` (AC1 to AC4 and the deterministic half of AC7 on fixtures, plus the corpus shapes the first run surfaced). ✅ `tools/knowledge-lint-compare.test.ts` (AC3, AC5 to AC7; every fetch is a stub, no test calls the API). ⏳ The first `--run` waits for the test key's cap to lift (2026-10-01) and Brad's yes on the cost line.

### US-45 · The chatbot answers Potassium Fiber questions from the signed label — **added 2026-10-07 (Brad approved: "build those, then deploy")**
As someone who asks either chatbot about the Potassium Fiber drink, I get the label's real numbers and its warning, no health promise, and, on Dr Brad's education surfaces, no sales pitch and a plain statement that he profits from it. Source: `docs/products.md` § "Potassium Fiber Drink" (the Makers Nutrition panel Brad signed on 2026-10-06, and its editor notes).
- AC1 (facts): the bot quotes the panel as written: 8 g of fiber (29% Daily Value) from 10 g of acacia gum, a scoop of about 15 g, 500 mg of potassium as potassium citrate (11%), 45 calories. It never gives the pre-panel figures: 10 g of fiber, 36%, a 12.9 g scoop, 20 calories.
- AC2 (the warning decides): when the user has kidney disease, has been told to limit potassium, or takes an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin receptor blocker, a potassium-sparing diuretic or another potassium supplement, the bot gives the label's 500 mg and sends them to their doctor. It never clears the drink for them or suggests it, including on the brand surface when they ask which product to buy.
- AC3 (no health claims): nothing ties the drink or its doses to blood pressure, the heart, cholesterol, the gut, bowel regularity, a prebiotic effect or blood sugar. Nutrient-content statements only ("high in fiber", "a good source of potassium"). Saying the drink makes no such claim is fine. Asked whether the drink helps any of these or any condition, the bot says it makes no health claims and is sold for its nutrient content, gives the per-scoop amounts, and does not summarise potassium or fiber outcome research; no answer about the drink cites an outcome study (orchestrator ruling, 2026-10-07, after a sampled brand answer summarised potassium blood-pressure trials). General potassium or fiber questions that don't mention the drink are unaffected.
- AC4 (surfaces): the doctor surfaces (drstanfield.com, YouTube, Discord) never volunteer, recommend or link the drink, never name a store and give no price unless asked the cost. They name it only when the user does, answer the factual question, and say that Brad owns the company that sells it and profits from its sale. The brand surface (microvitamin.com) may describe it and link https://microvitamin.com/products/potassium-fiber-drink, with no outcome claims; the brand posture's structure/function wording and its "MicroVitamin is a daily multivitamin" line do not apply to the drink.
- AC5 (never organic): the bot never calls the product organic. Only one ingredient's name, Inavea™ Essential Organic Talh, holds the word.
- AC6 (the harness tests a surface and a claim): a `tools/test-queries.json` entry may carry `surface: "doctor" | "brand"`. The answer check then adds that surface's posture file (`app/lib/chat-posture-<surface>.md`) after the products block and before any articles, the order production's `buildSystemBlocks` uses. An unknown surface stops the harness before any API call. Entries without it are scored as before. An entry may also carry `must_not_claim` (added after the Codex review of b322d5d7 and two adversarial reviews): a phrase stated as fact fails. A negation (no, not, never, cannot, without, nor, nothing, none, neither, n't) excuses it only within the 12 words before it and inside its clause; a semicolon, dash, "but" or "and" ends the clause. So "it makes no claim that it can lower blood pressure" passes, while "it has no added sugar and can lower blood pressure" and "it isn't a medicine, but it keeps you regular" fail. Affirming idioms that hold a negation word ("no doubt", "not only", "no wonder", "no question", "without doubt", "none other than") never excuse a claim (Codex, range review of 2026-10-07). Markdown emphasis is stripped and curly apostrophes straightened. It is a heuristic, so the phrases stay claim-shaped. Referral checks ask for "your doctor" (so "Brad is a doctor" does not count) and disclosure checks ask for both "owns" and "profit", with "n't profit" and "not profit" forbidden.
- AC7 (medicine spacing): asked about taking the drink with other medicines, the bot gives the live store's direction: "Take other medicines at least two hours before or after a scoop." (potassiumfiber.com product page and FAQ; products.md since 0cc47a16). This is product-label guidance in the chatbot's product knowledge only, not a roadmap suggestion, so the three-file clinical sync (algorithm, evidence.ts, roadmap_text.html) does not apply.
- Usage signal (declared): no new event. Questions naming the drink show in the stored transcripts of the blog chat bubble, chatbot embed, Discord and YouTube (30-day window, US-15 AC8). The main widget stores no text (US-15 AC7), so its answers cannot be audited after the fact.
- Known limitations (orchestrator ruling, 2026-10-07: leave the router and posture files as they are):
  - Routing is not asserted. Router rule 7 names only MicroVitamin and Sleep as Brad's products, and on 2026-10-07 it sent most Potassium Fiber questions to the potassium, psyllium, kidney, hypertension and ACE-inhibitor entries. Each fixture pins the 3-run router intersection for its text (the router sees no surface), minus what production skips at the 120K article cap (US-15 AC23). A later change in what the router returns is not caught here.
  - The posture files name only MicroVitamin, MicroVitamin+ and Sleep. The drink's surface rules live in the products.md editor notes.
  - The doctor fixtures model the drstanfield.com web chat only. YouTube and Discord also use the doctor posture but add their platform prompt (YouTube caps a reply at 90 words), which the harness does not load; nor does it load the evidence document, the knowledge overview or user data, as before this story.
  - The limit-potassium fixture's "your doctor" can be met by echoing the user's own words.
  - Nothing reruns this category automatically when products.md or a posture file changes; run it by hand before such a deploy.
- Tests: ✅ 24 fixed-handle answer checks, category `product-potassium-fiber` in `tools/test-queries.json` (12 doctor, 12 brand; AC1 to AC5 and AC7). The five AC3 fixtures require "health claim", "nutrient content", "8 g" and "500 mg", and the brand ones forbid "daily multivitamin". The two AC7 fixtures (added 2026-10-07 without router pins, because the test workspace was out) require "at least two hours" and "before or after" and forbid "no more than two hours"; the AC3 fixtures also forbid a stated "makes health claims". Run: `npx tsx tools/test-chatbot-matching.ts --category product-potassium-fiber --fixed-handles-only --answer-check-runs 3`. 2026-10-07: 22/22 at 3 runs each (majority) on `products.md` at 8ad6a7bc, before the research rule and the medicine-spacing direction; the paid suite has not run since (the test workspace is out until 2026-11-01), so the research rule was checked live instead (see the chatbot changelog); 3/22 at 1 run on `products.md` before a97d629e (the three that pass are the guards that need the drink absent from the answer: two doctor-surface "never volunteer" questions and the brand kidney-disease "which product" question). ✅ `tools/test-chatbot-matching.test.ts` (AC6, offline: each answer call carries its own surface's posture, after products and before articles; a referral-free answer, a stated claim and a claim after an unrelated negation or an affirming idiom fail, and so does an outcome-research summary (the five AC3 fixtures forbid "lowered systolic", "systolic pressure by", "mmHg", "meta-analysis", "randomized trials", "randomised trials" and "Cochrane"), while denials pass; a liveness check confirms every other fixture fails on a stub answer).

## Epic F — Staying engaged

### US-17 · Email reminders — the retention engine (cloud lane BUILT 2026-08-13; typed lane = US-23)
As a user who has connected a cloud and entered real screening/blood data, I am reminded by email when something comes due **without having had to hunt for a setting** — because a reminder I never receive is the whole reason the tool failed to change my behaviour.

**Reframed 2026-08-14 (constitution):** reminders are not a settings feature — they are the product's retention engine, and email is the primary surface for the primary avatar. This story covers the provider-verified (cloud-connect) lane, which the funnel shows is the rare path; the typed-email lane — ~10× larger and therefore the trunk — is promoted to its own story, **US-23**. Shared mechanics that apply to BOTH lanes (full-schedule-in-every-email, the annual floor, calendar links) are specified in US-23 AC3/AC6 and US-24 to avoid duplication.

**Status: the opt-in design was a proven failure; the opt-out replacement is built (2026-08-13).** The old behaviour was explicit opt-in behind three barriers (cloud-connect → scroll past the disclaimer to the bottom of the results panel → two clicks). Result: **~1 genuine opt-in in two months** (the second `reminder_optin_v2` row is Brad's own e2e test). Nothing was broken — cron healthy, sends correct, nothing yet due (earliest 2027-05-12) — the feature simply never reached anyone.

**What now ships (`autoEnrolReminders`, [standalone/reminders.ts](../widget-src/standalone/reminders.ts)):** every app load on a reminders-capable cloud enrols the user unprompted, unless the file already records a decision. Details that are load-bearing, not incidental:

- **No credential, no popup (rebuilt 2026-09-10 — see AC7).** Auto-enrolment reads the account email in the browser (Drive: a signed ID token, which grants nothing; Dropbox: `get_current_account`; GitHub: `/user/emails`) and posts only that. It never opens a Google popup — it runs at page load, where a popup is both browser-blocked and unasked-for — and the popup path that used to send a Drive ACCESS token as proof is deleted. Failures are swallowed: an enrolment nobody asked for must not raise an error nobody asked for. Pinned by a real (unmocked) test on the adapter, `storage/drive-reminder-identity.test.ts`.
- **The disclosure renders ABOVE the widget, not inside the plan panel.** The plan is slide 2 of the mobile tab layout and every connect path reloads onto slide 1, so a notice inside it would announce itself to an off-screen panel; it is also absent from the no-data-yet render branch — exactly the user who just connected. It is the reminders control itself, so the off switch is one click from the sentence announcing it, and it survives a reload (sessionStorage) until dismissed.
- **Shopify surface only** (a deliberate narrowing of AC1's literal text — Brad to confirm). The Pages/self-host build is marketed as almost no Brad server (the record and the chat never reach us; Google sign-in, reminders and scrubbed Sentry errors do) and runs uploads + chat on the user's own key; enrolling that user unprompted would post their account email to Brad's server at page load, the one thing they chose that build to avoid. They keep the manual toggle. It also matters for the kill criterion: `trackProductEvent` no-ops off-Shopify, so a Pages opt-out would be invisible to the very ratio this decision reverts on.
- **"No email to give" stops the retry loop permanently** (`hr_reminders_autoenrol_blocked`): a GitHub token without the email permission, or a pre-openid Drive grant, will answer the same way next visit. The manual toggle still works and asks the user to type the address once (AC9) — never a silent enrolment on a typed address. Transient failures are not blocks.
- **Switching clouds moves the enrolment, it doesn't duplicate it.** Server rows are keyed by email, so a fresh opt-in cannot replace one made under a different provider; the old row is cancelled first. Not counted as an opt-out — a storage switch is not a user's verdict on reminders. **A refused cancel stops the switch (2026-10-14, adversary R3).** Enrolling anyway wrote the new token over the old one, the only key to the old row, so any 4xx, 5xx, 429 or network failure orphaned it for good. Now the file keeps the old opt-in and the next visit on the new cloud retries the cancel, then enrols. Tests: `standalone/reminders.test.ts` (400, 429, 500, 503 and a network failure: no enrolment, then the retry).
- Removed 2026-10-15 (Brad: not needed); a failed reminder cancel on erase is reported to Sentry only.
- Brad, 2026-10-15: email-box (typed) sign-ups stay cancellable ONLY by the email link. The browser never receives their token: handing tokens out for rows a request did not create would let anyone who types an address take over its reminders, and Brad does not want that exposure. Rows that may have stayed active while cancels failed (2026-09-10 to the AC4 fix) are left as they are: every reminder email carries a working unsubscribe link.
- **Erasing your data reaches the server row** (AC1b — tombstoned, or deleted when Drive can prove the inbox), via a pre-erase hook — the capability token that authorises the delete dies with the file, so it cannot run afterwards.

**The decision (Brad, 2026-08-11):** move to reminders **on by default**, opt-out rather than opt-in. Sends are rare by design (screening 90d / bloods 180d / med-review 365d cooldowns), so the cost to a user who ignores them is near zero while the value to one who forgets a colonoscopy is the product's entire thesis.

**Two constraints that bound the redesign** (they are not negotiable and any implementation must satisfy both):
1. **RETIRED for Dropbox, GitHub and typed on 2026-09-10 (Brad; see AC7–AC10). Drive alone keeps the provider's word, via the ID token.** Former text: The email must be verified — the provider's word, or proven delivery (superseded 2026-08-14; original wording said "never a client-typed address … only after a confirm-link round trip").** The threat is unchanged: anyone can enter `victim@example.com` and make Brad's server email a stranger. What changed is the accepted proof: Brad rejected the confirm click (loses 20–40% of honest users) in favour of **delivery-validation + defense-in-depth**, now specified in US-23 — bounce/complaint webhook un-enrols, 3-day quiet period before any reminder, server-side label allow-list (no attacker-authored text can transit), typed writes can never touch a provider-verified row, refreshes preserve token + cooldowns (no resend amplification, no broken unsubscribe links), one plan-ready email per address ever, prominent in-body unsubscribe. A typed address with none of those protections remains forbidden.
2. **Default-on must stay visible, never silent.** Auto-enrolling silently would push every cloud-connected user's due-dates + labels to Brad's server without them knowing — quietly weakening the "your health data lives in your cloud, not our servers" promise that the product is marketed on ([architecture-v2.md](architecture-v2.md)), and inviting spam complaints that damage the sending domain shared with transactional mail. **Recommended design point:** at the cloud-connect success moment, a visible, pre-checked "Email me when something comes due" with a one-line plain statement of exactly what leaves the device (due date + label + email — never values), unmissable on one screen, plus a permanent off switch in settings.

**Where the audience actually is (live pull, 2026-08-10 — this reorders the work):** Klaviyo holds **874 captured emails** on the commerce list (+39 edu), still growing ~4–5/day (135 in the last 30d). `cloud_connect_success` has fired **2 times ever**. So the provider-verified lane covers ~2 people and the typed-address lane covers ~900: **the typed lane is not a nice-to-have Phase 2, it is the entire audience.** Build order follows the numbers, not the ease.

**Confirmation email sends via Resend, never Klaviyo (decision 2026-08-11).** Reminder consent must never be coupled to the marketing list: Klaviyo suppression is list-wide, so a supplement-promo unsubscribe would silently stop "your colonoscopy is due" — a marketing preference overriding a health reminder, with no error and nobody noticing. Two consents, two systems, two suppression lists. Supporting reasons: the confirm mail is textbook transactional (one-time, user-triggered, expected in seconds); a confirm landing in spam fails the whole redesign silently, and transactional streams land better; Resend is already wired (`reminder-v2.server.ts`, `email.server.ts`). Precedent already in the code — [api.reminders-v2.ts](../app/routes/api.reminders-v2.ts) takes `verified.email` for reminders and a SEPARATE `marketingEmail` for Klaviyo, fire-and-forget so Klaviyo can never fail an opt-in. Bonus: confirming before adding to Klaviyo filters typos/fakes, which raises Meta/Google audience match rates and cuts per-contact spend.

**No confirm-click gate (Brad, 2026-08-11; reaffirmed 2026-09-10 when the credential proof was dropped — the confirm-link alternative was planned, reviewed and rejected for the same reason).** Double opt-in loses 20–40% of legitimate signups — taxing every honest user to catch a rare bad one. Instead the plan-ready email (US-22) does the work: a bounce proves the address is dead, and delivery is the enrollment trigger. The residual risk a bounce can't catch is a typo into a *valid stranger's* address (`john@` for `johnn@`), which delivers fine; AC2c bounds that (rare sends + prominent one-click unsubscribe). A click on that email is a strong ownership signal but is never required — treat clicks, not opens, as real (Apple Mail Privacy Protection fakes opens).

**The ~900 existing captures (still needs a Brad call):** they gave an email for a report, not for reminders, and predate any send. A bulk "want reminders?" mail is a re-permission campaign to people who never asked — real complaint risk on a domain that also carries transactional mail. Preferred shape if we do it: one genuinely useful email (plan re-entry + the reminders offer), once. Both lists are `single_opt_in` today, so no confirmation habit exists with these contacts.

- AC1: On cloud-connect success (Drive/Dropbox/GitHub), enrollment happens **immediately and without any user action** — true opt-out (Brad, 2026-08-11). A user who reads the line and clicks away IS enrolled; only an explicit toggle-off unenrolls. The disclosure is a visible statement + already-on switch on that same screen, never a gate.
- AC1b: Consequence of AC1, accepted knowingly: every cloud-connecting user's due date + label + verified email reaches the server, where before only explicit opt-ins did. Still no measurement, lab value, or reasoning — the local-first invariant holds — but the population sending metadata widens from ~2 to everyone who connects. **Amended 2026-09-10 (review of aae35a3):** a toggle-off or erase TOMBSTONES the row (schedule emptied; email + token kept) on every lane; it is DELETED outright only when the request also carries a valid Google ID token for the row's own address. Reason: a bare-token delete made optin→cancel→optin mint a fresh `isNew` — and a fresh plan-ready email — every cycle. Consequence, stated plainly: for Dropbox/GitHub/typed users "delete all my data" leaves their address in a tombstone on Brad's server until they unsubscribe from an email. **Bounded 2026-09-10:** a row switched off stays 90 days, then is deleted — the daily reminder cron sweeps emptied rows older than `TOMBSTONE_TTL_DAYS` (`purgeTombstones` in `app/lib/reminder-v2.server.ts`), after the day's sends, and a purge failure is reported to Sentry rather than failing the run. Residual: past the window a replayed optin on that address is `isNew` again and earns one more plan-ready email — at most one per address per 90 days, under the capture route's 5/day-per-email limiter. Tests: `app/lib/reminder-v2-typed.test.ts` (window, live rows untouched, select failure throws), `app/lib/reminder-v2-cron.server.test.ts` (once per run; a purge error never fails the day).
- AC2 (amended 2026-09-10): The enrolled email is either Google-verified (ID token) OR an address whose plan-ready email **delivered without bouncing** — that now covers Dropbox, GitHub and typed alike — the typed lane is now its own story, **US-23** (promoted 2026-08-14: it is ~10× the cloud lane and the highest-leverage unbuilt thing in the product). No confirm-click gate — see the consent reasoning below.
- AC2b: A hard bounce disenrolls: no reminders, and the address is suppressed (unsubscribed, not deleted) in Klaviyo — matching US-22 AC3's reversibility decision.
- AC2c (widened 2026-09-10): Because a delivered-but-mistyped address belongs to a stranger, EVERY reminder to EVERY lane carries the one-click unsubscribe prominently in the body, not just the header. Rare sends (90/180/365d) + one click to stop = bounded, self-correcting harm.
- AC3: A user can turn reminders off permanently in one action, from the results surface and from any reminder email (RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe already ships).
- **Known residual risks, accepted not fixed (adversarial review 2026-08-13).** (1) If a user moves their `health-roadmap.json` to the Drive trash, the app sees a legitimately-empty query result — indistinguishable from a new user — and re-enrols, minting a token that invalidates the one in the real file; the next schedule push 404s and flips them to `cancelled`. A silent unsubscribe, very narrow. (2) Drive does two `tryServerRefresh` round trips per load until enrolment succeeds (one in `resolveBackend`, one in `getReminderIdToken`), on two adapter instances sharing localStorage. Refresh grants don't re-issue the refresh token, so no credential can be stranded — it's waste, not risk.
- AC4: Turning reminders off survives a sync from a second device (see the 2026-08-07 incident below — this AC exists because that exact bug shipped).
  - **Bug fixed 2026-10-14 (failing test first; live since c2d4192e, 2026-09-10):** with no Google proof the client posted the cancel as `{op:'cancel', token, idToken: null}`. The route's zod `idToken: …optional()` accepts a missing key but rejects null, so it answered 400 "Invalid input" and never reached the row. Every cancel on Dropbox or GitHub, and a Drive cancel without a silent ID token, failed: "Turn off" showed an error, while the cloud switch and "Delete all my data" (AC1b) left the server row active. Those three were the live failures. (Corrected 2026-10-14, adversary R5: this line first said every hidden-tab cancel failed live too. The keepalive cancel, the age gate's, arrived in d9020aad on 2026-10-14 and was never deployed.) The client now leaves the key out when it has no token (`postCancel`), on all three cancel paths; the server is unchanged. Optin and update never send a null. Test: `app/routes/api.reminders-v2.client-contract.test.ts` feeds the client's exact body into the real route `action` (Turn off on Dropbox, GitHub and tokenless Drive; the age gate's keepalive cancel; erase; the cloud switch): 200 and `cancelByToken` called. `reminders.test.ts` no longer pins the null body.
- AC5: The server still receives only due date + label + verified email + capability token. No measurement, lab value, or reasoning ever leaves the device — default-on must not widen the data sent. **Open nuance for Brad (adversarial review, 2026-08-13):** a label can carry an inference even though it carries no value. `'Lung screening (low-dose CT)'` is emitted ONLY for a ≥15-pack-year smoker, `'Medication review'` only for someone on active medication, and result-dependent intervals make some `dueAt` values a function of a result. Under opt-in the user chose that knowingly; under default-on they didn't. The shipped copy was changed to be concrete rather than reassuring ("the NAME and due date of each check-up, for example 'Colonoscopy — due May 2027'") instead of the earlier "never your measurements or results", which was true and misleading. If Brad wants the inference closed rather than disclosed, the options are generic labels ("A screening is due") or dropping the lung item.
- AC6: Local-storage-only users (no cloud, no account email) are never enrolled and are never shown a broken control.
- AC7 (Brad, 2026-09-10 — a ChatGPT audit found enrolment posting the Dropbox access token and the GitHub PAT as "proof of email"; a PAT confers write access to the repo the health data lives in): **No storage credential ever leaves the browser for reminders.** The optin request carries the account email + the schedule (+ the optional typed marketing address). Google Drive alone still sends its signed ID token — it grants nothing, and the server reads the verified address from it. `api.google-token` is unchanged (Drive connect needs it; its `idToken` passthrough now also feeds the browser-side email prefill).
- AC8: **An address-only optin follows the typed lane's rules, for every lane.** A NEW address creates the row, receives its capability token ONCE, gets the plan-ready email (US-22) and sits out the 3-day quiet period. An EXISTING address is a schedule refresh (except a Google-verified row, which the address lane never refreshes: US-23 AC7): provider immutable, token never rotated and **never returned on the ADDRESS lane** (returning it there would hand the cancel capability to whoever typed the address — the silent-unsubscribe attack). **Scoped 2026-09-10:** the google-drive lane ALWAYS receives its token, new row or existing, because the caller proved the inbox with a signed ID token; withholding it stranded every Drive user on a second device and every user whose squatted row had just been rotated (no token in the file means schedule pushes never start and the toggle-off is a no-op). An address-lane row's token still rotates when a Google-verified caller proves that address. Email-link unsubscribe is a tombstone for every lane, and a tombstoned token refuses schedule pushes so the device flips its own file to cancelled. **Accepted, plainly: the refreshed-vs-new reply is a bounded membership oracle** — an unauthenticated optin reveals whether an address is enrolled. Bounded by 5/day per email and 20/hour per hashed IP (the capture route's numbers); accepted by Brad 2026-09-10 over the confirm-click alternative. **Residual (review of aae35a3):** after an email-link unsubscribe, an address-only optin naming that address refills the schedule silently (a tombstoned Google-verified row is the exception: never refreshed by this lane; no plan-ready email, since it is not `isNew`), and the widget offers that inbox no off switch other than the link in the next reminder. **Token squatting is closed:** a Google-verified optin ROTATES the token when the existing row was not itself Google-verified (`provider` = `'google-drive'` means verified; the widget's no-ID-token Drive fallback enrols as `'typed'`). **Per-email limiter key** is normalised (case, `+tag`, Gmail dots) — the stored address is not. **Transient Drive refresh failures never set the "no email" block**; a fresh connect clears it.
- **Lane B note, deferred 2026-09-10 (late): the tombstone refill.** AC8's residual is that an address-lane optin naming a tombstoned address refills that row's schedule silently. The better answer is to send the owner a mail instead: an address-lane optin that hits a tombstone emails that address a "turn reminders back on" link carrying the row's own token, so the person who owns the inbox decides, and nobody else can restart a schedule by typing their address. Not built. It has no usage signal yet — we have never observed the case — and per the constitution a feature we cannot evaluate does not get built.
- AC11 (2026-09-10): A `google-drive` optin without an ID token is REFUSED with a 400 by the request schema, never downgraded to the address lane. A body naming the verified provider must carry the proof that provider's lane rests on; accepting the address instead would let anyone write a row wearing the verified label. Before this AC (deployed c2d4192, the morning of 2026-09-10) the address lane accepted that body; a row it wrote would have kept a squatter's token across the owner's verification. Checked the same day: every `google-drive` row (9) predates that deploy, so no such row exists and nothing is rotated. Two stated residuals on the verified lane: an existing verified row re-enrolled from a new device now shows that device the one-time "reminders set up" notice, and a Drive device whose file records no decision refills an email-link tombstone on its next visit (it always did; the email's off link works every time).
- AC9: When the provider has no email to give (a GitHub token without "Email addresses: read-only"; a pre-openid Drive grant), auto-enrolment stops and the control asks for the address once, visibly — never a silent enrolment on a typed address. An address already enrolled elsewhere shows "already set up for x@…; use the link in any reminder email to turn them off", never a broken "on".
- AC10: `reminder_optin` is counted by the SERVER when a new row lands, for every lane (it is in `SERVER_ONLY_EVENT_NAMES`; the client emission is deleted). Only the server knows the enrolment landed, and abuse enrolments count rather than hide — the ratio stays honest. `reminder_optout` is unchanged.
- AC12 (2026-10-14, adversary R1/R2/R4): **A cloud switch to the same email keeps the row.** Rows are keyed by email, so the old token still owns the only row there is. Before cancelling, `autoEnrolReminders` compares the new cloud's address with the file's (trimmed, lower-cased). When they match it posts nothing, keeps the token and writes only the new provider, so the next load does nothing. Before this, the switch cancelled the row and opted the same address in again; the server refreshed it and returned no token, the file kept the old provider, and every load repeated both posts. After five a day the limiter's 429 left the row tombstoned, and the next push's 404 wrote a `cancelled` the user never chose. A different address still cancels, then enrols, and defers on any failure. If the new address already holds a row (`refreshed`), the file keeps the old opt-in and the next visit tries again. From the moment a switch's cancel is sent until the new enrolment lands, `pushReminderSchedule` sends nothing from the new cloud, on load or on tab hide, on that visit and on later ones in the same browser (see the sub-bullets); on load the push runs after the enrolment, so it never races the cancel. A switch that never cancelled holds nothing, and the age gate's cancel still runs. A refused switch cancel goes to Sentry (`op: 'switch-cancel'`) with its status code only. Tests: `standalone/reminders.test.ts` (Dropbox to GitHub and Drive to Dropbox, same email; the `refreshed` switch; the held push and the pushes that still run: no switch on this page, local and self-host, Pages, the age gate; the Sentry event), all failing first except the pushes that still run.
  - Orchestrator decision (2026-10-14): when the new cloud gives no address yet, the switch stops BEFORE the cancel, so the old row and its reminders continue (the control reads "on → old address") and the next visit retries. Test: reminders.test.ts "a switch to a cloud with no address keeps the old row" (fails without the guard).
  - Codex R1/R2 on a9966d80 (2026-10-14): the switch re-reads the opt-in after the identity lookup and acts only if it is the same active opt-in (an erase, a toggle-off or another device's change during the lookup is never overwritten; US-11 AC4); a switch TO Google Drive compares the browser's Drive account email, because Drive's identity carries an ID token, not an address, so a same-address switch to Drive keeps the token too. Tests: reminders.test.ts "the same-address shortcut, to Drive and across an erase" (both failed first).
  - Deploy-gate adversary (2026-10-14): the push is held only from the moment THIS page's switch cancels the old row until the new enrolment lands (`switchHoldsOldToken`), and on load the push runs after the enrolment, so it never races the cancel; a switch that never cancels (no address, unverified email, a stale block) keeps pushing with the old token and keeps the 404 unsubscribe probe. Tests: reminders.test.ts "…enrolment did not land, the push is held" (fails without the hold) and "…no switch run on this page keeps its schedule current".
  - OPEN for Brad (adversary R1, 2026-10-14): a DIFFERENT-address switch whose new address already has a row (typed capture, an earlier cloud) gets `refreshed` with no token every visit: the old row is cancelled, the address row stays live, the control reads the old address, and Turn off / erase reach only the dead token. Rare (two addresses plus an existing row), bounded by the 5-a-day limiter. A proper fix needs a file state for "enrolled elsewhere, no token" (a `FileReminderOptIn` schema change, merge semantics) and a control line pointing to the email link. Also accepted: after a same-address switch, a second device still on the old cloud pushes the same row from its own file.
  - Deploy-gate adversary R1/R2/R4 on 028a627a (2026-10-14). R1: the in-page hold died with the page, but the tombstone lives on the server, so a switch that cancelled and then failed to enrol (5xx, 429, network, no address) let the next visit's push 404 into a `cancelled` nobody chose. The switch now writes `hr_reminders_switch_cancelled` (the old token, in localStorage) before its cancel, clears it on a refused cancel and when the new token lands, and a thrown cancel keeps it. The push is held while the file's opt-in belongs to another cloud and either the page flag is set or the marker names its token; a 404 on a token the marker names is never written as `cancelled`. R2: after the switch's identity recheck the silent enrolment still awaits the cancel, a second lookup and the optin POST, and an erase or a Turn off in that window was overwritten by the new token (US-11 AC4, AC4). Once the optin answers, the silent path re-reads the opt-in; if it is no longer the one the enrolment began from (for a first enrolment, still no decision) it writes nothing and cancels the new token's row, uncounted, with a refused cancel sent to Sentry (`op: 'superseded-cancel'`, status code only). A file that meanwhile holds the same token active (the verified lane keeps its token) is left alone. The manual toggle is unchanged. R4: the load push waits for the enrolment, and GitHub's email read had no timeout, so it now gives up at 10 s like Dropbox's. Tests: reminders.test.ts "a switch's cancel is remembered across visits" (7) and "a decision made during a silent enrolment stands" (5); github.test.ts "a hung read gives up" (1); all failed first.
  - Residual (accepted with R1): the marker lives in one browser. Another device on the same new cloud never saw it, so if its own switch attempt stops before the cancel (a failed or empty address lookup, the block key), its push of the old token 404s into a `cancelled` that syncs to every device. A browser with blocked storage keeps only the page flag. Both need the same file state as the OPEN item above. Also open: a user who goes back to the old cloud before the new enrolment lands keeps an `active` opt-in whose row is a tombstone; its 404 is no longer written as `cancelled`, so the control reads "on" while nothing sends.
- **Usage signal (Lane B, declare before code):** `reminder_optin` fires on enrolment (auto or manual; server-side since 2026-09-10, AC10) and `reminder_optout` on disable — both wired 2026-08-13, both in the shared `PRODUCT_EVENT_NAMES` enum. `reminder_sent` fires server-side on each successful reminder send (nil-UUID sentinel; metadata = provider + due-item count, never labels or addresses) — added 2026-08-30 (W35 backlog #3, Brad-authorized live) after the first real send proved sends were invisible. Server-only event names and the nil sentinel are rejected at the client event route, so a browser cannot forge these counters (adversarial review, same day — closed the pre-existing `report_email_*` hole too). The ratio is the honest measure. Kill criterion: if opt-out exceeds ~30% of enrolments, or spam complaints appear in Resend, the default-on decision is wrong and reverts. Caveat to read the first numbers with: `trackProductEvent` is Shopify-surface-only and throttles to once per event name per tab session, so these are session counters, not per-user counts.
- Evidence: ~1 genuine opt-in ever (live query 2026-08-10); `reminder_optin` 0 fires since instrumentation went live 2026-08-06 — but both existing opt-ins PREDATE instrumentation, so zero events measures reach, not rejection. First default-on week (2026-W33): 18 enrolments, 0 opt-outs (kill-ratio 0% vs the 30% threshold); `reminder_optin_v2` 2 → 20 rows all-time. Week 2 (2026-W34): 38 enrolments (+111%), still 0 opt-outs ever (0/56 cumulative); rows 58 all-time (52 typed + 6 google-drive, ~9:1). Week 3 (2026-W35): 31 enrolments, still 0 opt-outs (0/87 cumulative); rows 89 (81 typed + 8 drive, ~10:1); 0 bounces, 0 complaints. **The first genuine reminder send happened 2026-08-28** (W35): a row enrolled 08-25 with an item already due 08-01 carries a `last_sent` stamp — the typed lane enrols overdue-at-capture items, so "nothing due until 2027" is stale; sends are live now (evidenced by the cron stamp; no send event existed at the time — `reminder_sent` shipped 2026-08-30, W35 backlog #3). Cron `reminder_v2_cron` healthy (lock acquired daily; a transient-lock-error day-skip class was hardened 08-28 — see US-28). Week 4 (2026-W36): 20 enrolments and the **first opt-out ever** (kill-ratio 1/109 cumulative vs the 30% threshold — `reminder_optout`'s emit is now production-verified); rows 109 all-time (101 typed + 7 drive + the first dropbox row); `reminder_sent` fired twice (typed, 08-31 colorectal + 09-01 breast) and matched the window's only two `last_sent` stamps exactly — the event and the stamp now corroborate each other, so sends are observable (W35 backlog #3 closed). Weeks 5–6 (2026-W37/W38): 26 + 14 enrolments; second opt-out ever (2/149); rows 149 (136 typed + 11 drive + 2 dropbox); `reminder_sent` 2 in W37 (matching the two `last_sent` map dates) and 0 in W38 (no date in the window — corroborated).
