### US-23 · Typed-email reminders — **THE TRUNK (Brad-approved 2026-08-14; LIVE since the 08-14 deploy — heading corrected 2026-09-06, it still said "awaiting deploy")**
As someone who typed my email to get my plan PDF, I get reminded when my check-ups and blood tests come due — because my lane is ~10× the cloud lane (874+ captures, ~4–5/day vs 3 cloud connects ever). **This was the highest-leverage unbuilt thing in the product; it is live, and the ~10:1 bet has held every week since (US-17 evidence).**

**Why it's safe now:** US-22's delivery-validation machine is live and verified (signature-checked bounce/complaint webhook → Klaviyo suppression + `deleteByEmail`). Delivery is the consent gate Brad chose over confirm-clicks; a bounce un-enrols before any reminder could ever fire.

- AC1: When the capture button is pressed, the client sends the **schedule alongside the email** — the same client-computed labels + due dates as US-17, stored as one `reminder_optin_v2` row with `provider: 'typed'`. Nothing else crosses (constitution: calendar, not chart).
- AC2: No reminder is ever sent to a typed address until the plan-ready email has had time to bounce. **Precisely (2026-08-14, second review):** the gate is a quiet period, not positive delivery confirmation — the cron skips typed rows for 3 calendar days from `created_at` (effective floor ~2d8h given the 08:00 UTC send hour; never `updated_at`, which refreshes touch), and the bounce/complaint webhook un-enrols within minutes-to-hours, comfortably inside it. This covers the overdue-at-capture case too. Residual, accepted: a plan-ready send that FAILS outright (Resend outage) is logged, not retried — the enrolment stands on the typed consent + quiet period alone. Upgrading to a Resend `delivered`-event flag is future hardening.
- AC3 (both lanes): Every reminder email carries the user's **full upcoming schedule**, not just the due item — the email is the surviving artifact for a user whose localStorage is long gone (constitution: durability). The server already stores the whole list; this costs nothing.
- AC4: Labels are **specific** ("Colonoscopy, due May 2027"), per the constitution's recall-letter decision — and **server-validated against health-core's `SCHEDULE_LABELS` allow-list**: an unauthenticated capture names someone else's inbox, so no client-authored text may ever transit into an email (the old free-text `label` field was the hole). The capture UI carries a one-line disclosure that typing the email turns reminders on, with the off switch named. Regression coverage: `reminder-impossible-date.witness.test.ts` refuses rolled-over days such as February 30 before storage; it documents, but does not migrate, already stored invalid dates.
- AC5: EVERY reminder to a typed address carries the one-click unsubscribe prominently in the body, not just the header (a superset of US-17 AC2c's "first reminder" — a delivered-but-mistyped address belongs to a stranger; rare sends + one click = bounded harm).
- AC6 (both lanes): **The annual floor** — if the computed schedule has nothing due within 12 months, seed one "Annual health check-in" item 12 months out. Every enrolled person gets at least one touch a year; a colonoscopy-every-10-years user must not get a decade of silence (Brad, 2026-08-14).
- AC6a: A malformed or missing active-medication review stamp contributes no candidate and cannot suppress a valid medication-review date. Keep the existing 12-month interval and annual floor without inferring or persisting a replacement date. Tests: `reminder-medication-malformed.test.ts`. Amended 2026-10-21 (Codex R4): a stamp that is not a real calendar date (`not-a-date`, `2026-02-30`) reads as an unknown time at migration, never as the file's anchor, which the schedule would have taken as a review date. The whole stamp is checked, not just its day: a real day with a broken time or offset, or trailing junk (`2099-01-01T99:00:00Z`, `2026-05-01 junk`), is not a time either. Every shape a writer emits stays valid: `toISOString`, a date-only day, `+13:00` and `+0530` offsets, fractional seconds, lowercase `t`/`z`, a zone-less time, and Postgres's text style (`2025-01-15 03:00:00+00`), which files imported from v1 may hold. That style needs its zone: a zone-less `2025-01-15 03:00:00` is unknown time, because the merge would read it in the machine's own zone. Residual, `createdAt`: a garbage row `createdAt` is still clamped to the anchor, as before. Reading it as unknown time would let an erase drop the row, a deletion, so it stays out of this AC. Residual, deploy order: a client older than this fix still turns a garbage stamp into its file's anchor at migration, and a file it saves keeps that anchor as a real stamp, which no later reader can tell from a genuine one. Tests: `migrate.test.ts`.
- AC6b (Brad, 2026-10-21: "we always need to use international time, so that everything is standard and timezones don't break"): reminder date maths is UTC calendar arithmetic. The same file at the same instant gives the same schedule in every timezone: the annual floor, the age the rules read, v1's overdue check and the cron's re-send cooldown. Screening due dates were already zone-independent (built and read in the local zone, always the 1st of a month). **The time rule (Brad, 2026-10-21: "the database is always UTC, and then it's the user interface that actually shows the correct time zone"):** moments (saved, uploaded, erased, every row stamp) are stored in UTC and shown in the user's time zone; calendar dates (a lab's collection date, the birth month, a screening date) are stored as the date itself, with no zone, and shown as written everywhere; "today", the day what is due is measured against, is the user's local calendar day, computed at display time. Server-side reminder maths uses UTC days until the user's time zone is stored (AC12). The schedule is server-side reminder maths: it is pushed to the server and emailed on a day, so it uses UTC days now; the plan's own "today" (US-31 AC11) stays the user's local day. Tests: `reminder-utc.test.ts` and `reminder-v2-cron-utc.test.ts`, both pinned to Pacific/Auckland.
- AC7: Re-capturing with the same email **refreshes the schedule ONLY** — the token and `last_sent` cooldowns are preserved, and a typed write can never touch a provider-verified row. Each of those three is load-bearing: a rotated token breaks the unsubscribe links in every email already sent (the page would claim success while the row lives on); reset cooldowns turn one re-capture/day into daily re-sends of whatever is due; and clobbering a verified row would 404 the victim's own device into a silent "you unsubscribed". **The schedule too (2026-10-20, security; found by an outside scanner):** until then an address-lane optin (typed, Dropbox, GitHub: email and schedule only, and the Origin allow-list is not authentication) rewrote the schedule of whatever row held that address, a Google-verified one included. Now `enrolByEmail`'s refresh is an UPDATE filtered `provider <> 'google-drive'`, so a verified row's schedule is left whole; its owner keeps it current through the token-authenticated `update` op. The filter sits in the write itself, so a verified write landing after the lookup is covered, and the reply (`{refreshed: true, email}`), the queries and the round trips are the same whichever row it met: no oracle beyond AC8's accepted refreshed-vs-new one. **Residual, accepted by Brad 2026-09-10 and restated:** an address-lane row (typed, Dropbox, GitHub, or Drive's no-ID-token fallback, stored as `typed`) still takes its schedule from anyone who names its address, bounded by AC8's limits and by AC6's annual floor; token, `last_sent` and provider stay untouched. **A verified owner on the address lane gets the same reply and is not refreshed either:** a device without its capability token, or the PDF-capture typed enrol (`api.measurements.ts`), cannot move the schedule; it stays what their token-holding device last pushed, floored by AC6. Tests: `reminder-v2-typed.test.ts` "US-23 AC7".
- AC8: Abuse bound for `victim@example.com` (rebuilt after the second adversarial review found the first version had three bypasses): **the plan-ready email fires ONLY on a NEW enrolment** — a schedule-less body sends nothing (was: per-capture), a capture against a cloud-enrolled address sends nothing (was: per-capture at exactly the most engaged users), and **unsubscribe is a durable TOMBSTONE for typed rows** (schedule emptied, row + token kept), so a replayed capture is a refresh (no email), not a fresh enrolment (was: unsubscribe→re-capture minted a new email each cycle). Plus: per-IP rate limit (20/hr) beside the per-email 5/day, the response is CONSTANT (an `enrolled` field was a membership oracle for typed emails), labels allow-listed (AC4), unsubscribe links never rot (AC7 + provider-upgrade token preservation), complaint (US-22 AC10) suppresses + un-enrols immediately.
- AC9: Shopify surface only — the capture UI is now gated on `SHOPIFY_SURFACE` **explicitly** (before 2026-08-14 Pages was protected only by its hardcoded `data-logged-in="true"` attribute — an accident, not a gate).
- AC10 (2026-09-24): every reminder email, every provider, opens the tool through `${APP_BASE_URL}/roadmap/open?src=reminder`, never the GitHub Pages build. Its clicks count as `reminder_email_clicked` (server-only, no metadata), apart from the plan-ready email's `report_email_clicked`; the query only picks the counter, by exact equality, and the destination stays one literal (US-22 AC13). The footer makes no storage claim that is false for a lane: "Dr Brad's server keeps your reminder calendar and this email address. Your plan is not stored there." replaced "Your health data lives only in your own cloud storage", false for the typed lane (169 of 183 rows on 2026-09-24). The button reads "Open the Health Roadmap", and the email has no em dashes. Why: the button linked `drbradstanfield.github.io/roadmap/`, a different site from the storefront where every reminder reader made their plan, and a 404 on the day it was found; five reminders had gone out, one since 09-18. `PAGES_APP_URL` went with it: the button was its only caller. The unsubscribe page both emails link to said the same false thing ("it lives only in your own cloud storage") and now says only that the health data is unaffected (adversarial review, 2026-09-25). Tests: `plan-ready-email.test.ts` (the button, the footer, no em dash), `roadmap.open.test.ts` (the counter), `product-events.server.test.ts` (server-only), `reminders-v2.unsubscribe.test.ts` (the confirm page).
- AC11 (Brad, 2026-09-28): the capture box and the reminders opt-in name the MicroVitamin mailing list and say whose it is. The box reads "Getting your plan adds you to the **MicroVitamin mailing list** (Dr Brad's supplement company), and we'll email you when a check-up or blood test is due. We store only check-up names and dates, never your results. Every email has a one-click unsubscribe." The reminders control's unticked box reads "Also add me to the MicroVitamin mailing list (Dr Brad’s supplement company). Unsubscribe anytime." Why: every sign-up from both stores joins MicroVitamin's list (one Klaviyo account, on purpose), and the server records marketing consent (`email.marketing.consent: 'SUBSCRIBED'` in `klaviyo.server.ts`). The old copy named only the reminders, and the opt-in promised "Dr Brad’s evidence-based health emails", so neither said what the person was joining. Decided (Brad, 2026-09-28: "stay as is"): the capture box discloses rather than asks. The stricter EU/UK reading of GDPR consent, a separate unticked box for the list unbundled from getting the plan, was offered and not chosen.
- AC12 (⬜ planned, Brad 2026-10-21): reminders fall due on the user's own calendar day. The enrolment saves the user's IANA time zone, read in the browser from `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, beside the schedule, and the cron computes what is due on that zone's local day. Until then reminders use UTC days (AC6b), so a reminder can land up to a day early or late for a user far from Greenwich.
- **Usage signal:** `reminder_optin` vs `reminder_optout`, both carrying `provider` so the lanes are judged separately; same ~30% kill criterion as US-17. Both sides of the typed ratio are counted SERVER-side: optin on the capture route (only NEW enrolments — refreshes don't inflate the denominator, and abuse enrolments are counted rather than invisible), optout on the unsubscribe page (the typed lane's primary off switch — it was structurally blind before the first review). Bounce rate on new sends stays the estimator for the legacy-~900 backfill decision (US-22 AC8, still Brad's open call).
- The **annual floor (AC6) is computed client-side AND clamped server-side on every write** (`ensureAnnualFloor` — pure date arithmetic, so the server stays a dumb scheduler). The server clamp is an integrity bound, not UX: anyone who knows a typed user's email can overwrite their schedule via re-capture (AC7's refresh is unauthenticated by construction), which would otherwise be a silent per-user kill switch for the retention engine; with the clamp, the worst an attacker achieves is degrading a victim to annual check-ins — each carrying the one-click off switch. Tombstones (explicit unsubscribe) are exempt: an off stays off. `annual_checkin` is a first-class `ReminderCategory` (group `annual`, 365-day cooldown).
- **Known residual risks, accepted knowingly (second review, 2026-08-14):** (1) a typed schedule remains rewritable by anyone who knows the email — bounded by the floor clamp, label allow-list and real-date validation to "someone could change WHICH canonical items/dates a victim is reminded of", with every email carrying the off switch; (2) a deliberate re-capture refills a tombstoned schedule — that's the opt-out model's re-consent path, and an attacker using it buys only rare reminder-cadence emails; (3) the rate limiters are per-process in-memory (reset on deploy, per-machine) — bounds are soft, ×2 across the two Fly apps.
- Evidence: first live week (2026-W33, deployed 08-14): 17 typed enrolments vs 3 cloud rows all-time — the ~10:1 typed-lane bet held almost exactly; plan-ready CTR 40%. Week 2 (2026-W34): 35 typed enrolments (accelerating), plan-ready click:send ratio 60% (21 click events / 35 sends — event-level, no per-recipient dimension yet), 0 bounces, 0 complaints. Week 3 (2026-W35): 31 enrolments (typed-dominant; moved with the week's -26% reach dip, not worse); 29 sends / 10 click events (34% — uncohorted drift, not a verdict); 0 bounces/complaints in W34–W35 (all-time: 1 bounce, W33; 0 complaints). Production rows with provider 'typed' + delivered emails now exist, though the deliberate end-to-end capture walk-through the Tests line calls for is still owed. Week 4 (2026-W36): 20 enrolments (moved with the reach dip), 19 sends / 11 click events, 0 bounces/complaints; typed rows 101 of 109 all-time — and the typed lane produced the first two observable reminder sends (08-31, 09-01; see US-17) and the first opt-out (1/109). Weeks 5–6 (2026-W37/W38): 26 and 14 enrolments; sends / click events 24/14 and 13/8; 0 bounces/complaints; typed rows 136 of 149. Week 7 (2026-W39): 47 enrolments; sends / click events 47/26; 1 bounce (second ever); typed rows 178 of 195. US-22 AC13 / US-23 AC10 live 09-24: `email_landing_empty` fired twice in its first days (one visitor, 09-24, 15 min apart) and that visitor fired nothing else — no recovery yet (W39 backlog #4); `reminder_email_clicked` 0 (two of the week's three sends predate the deploy; one after — a zero at n=1).
- Tests: ✅ 25 server/health-core cases 2026-08-14, incl. a ROUTE-level suite (`api.measurements.test.ts`) pinning the isNew gate, the schedule-less and cloud-row no-send paths, the constant response, the tombstone, `upsertOptin`'s typed-refusal, the server floor clamp, and the real-date refine. ❌ live verify after deploy: a real typed capture → row lands with provider 'typed' → plan-ready email carries the calendar. ✅ AC11 (2026-09-28): `ResultsPanel.local-first.test.tsx` pins the capture box's list sentence; `standalone/reminders-control.test.tsx` pins the opt-in's label, placeholder and aria-label. ✅ Real WebKit on the live page, 2026-09-28 (edu-93, iPhone 13 and desktop), AC11: the capture box showed the new sentence, with "MicroVitamin mailing list" at weight 600. The reminders opt-in's label is pinned by reminders-control.test.tsx. Its live check is owed, because it needs a connected cloud.

### US-24 · Add my check-ups to my calendar — **Brad-approved 2026-08-14 (links, not attachments)**
As a user reading my plan or a reminder email, I can add any due item to my own calendar in one tap — Google/Apple's calendar becomes a reminder engine Brad never operates (the zero-server rung of the reminders ladder).
- AC1: Implemented as **Google Calendar template links** (`calendar.google.com/calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE…`) — plain URLs, no attachments (Brad, 2026-08-14: cleaner than .ics; Resend supports attachments but links beat them on deliverability and simplicity).
- AC2: Each link creates an all-day event on the due date, titled with the label, description linking back to the tool — **via the canonical storefront URL** (`drstanfield.com/pages/roadmap`), never a fly.dev backend host: the description is visible text in the saved event, and a raw redirect URL reads as phishing (found live by Brad, fixed 2026-08-14; cost accepted — calendar-sourced returns go uncounted, only the email buttons route through `/roadmap/open`, since 2026-09-24 both of them, US-23 AC10).
- AC3: Links appear wherever the schedule renders in email (plan-ready email once US-23 gives it a schedule; every reminder email).
- AC4: Zero server-side storage change; zero new data crosses.
- Tests: ✅ URL-building pinned (`plan-ready-email.test.ts`: TEMPLATE params, exclusive end date incl. year rollover, re-entry pointer); email placement pinned in the calendar-section suites.

### US-25 · The mobile app — architectural destination (**native iOS build started 2026-10-21**; decisions: [ios/architecture.md](../ios/architecture.md))
As the avatar's future self, I have an app that makes the whole thing automatic: **on-device notifications** (reminders with no server at all — the true serverless end-state), **HealthKit ingestion** (US labs push results into Apple Health; the app reads bloods, recomputes the plan, no typing), durable storage (no localStorage wipe anxiety). The enrolment/consent model built for US-17/US-23 transfers as-is; the server calendar shrinks toward zero as users migrate. Every near-term decision gets checked against the constitution's question: *does this move toward or away from the phone?*
- **Usage signal (Brad, 2026-10-21; amended 2026-10-22, AC19):** App Store Connect analytics (installs, sessions, retention, crashes, opted-in users), and Microsoft Clarity over masked screens (AC19). The app sends no product events to our server.
- AC1 (spike, 2026-10-21): the app runs the same health-core engine as the web, in JavaScriptCore, with no WebView. For the sample record (`docs/examples/health-roadmap.sample.json`) at a pinned instant, the app's plan JSON equals Node's byte for byte, with the time zone pinned to UTC and to Pacific/Auckland. Tests: `ios/HealthRoadmapTests/EngineParityTests.swift`, goldens from `ios/scripts/build-engine.mjs`.
- AC2 (spike): on launch the app shows that plan's suggestions natively, in the web results panel's groups and order (Requires Attention, Next Steps, Foundation, Skin Health, Supplements), each card opening to its full text, ingredients, guideline tags, the reason and the references, with the web's disclaimer, whose "consult with your healthcare provider" line carries the doctor framing (no plan header, so the cards start near the top: Brad 2026-10-21; My plan has a small title bar since 2026-10-21, so scrolled rows blur away under it instead of running beneath the clock; My data has none since AC17), and how long the plan took on the phone. An opened card stays on screen however long it grows: a section counts as in view, and fades in, as soon as any of it shows (Brad 2026-10-23: opening "Micronutrient base" made its whole section fade out, because the scroll transition's default threshold wanted most of the section on screen; seen and fixed in the simulator, no unit test reaches a scroll transition). Under Reduce Motion a section fades in without rising. Limits: plan under 100 ms, cold engine load under 300 ms (ios/architecture.md D2). Simulator only so far; a real iPhone is still owed.
- AC3 (tabs, Brad 2026-10-21): two tabs, **My data** first and **My plan** second, the web's mobile order (Input, Plan); the app opens on My data. Chat is the third tab (US-52, 2026-10-21).
- AC4 (the record lives on the phone): the app keeps one `health-roadmap.json`, the web's schema, in its own storage under the phone's data protection. Until the user connects a cloud (AC11) it is stored nowhere else, and it is never stored on our servers (chat and lab upload send what US-52 lists); its folder is marked for iOS to leave out of iCloud and computer backups (`isExcludedFromBackup`, Brad 2026-10-21). My data says so: since AC11 it names the connected cloud, or, after a Disconnect, that the copy synced earlier stays in that cloud, or that connecting one is how the record reaches the web or a new phone. First launch starts an empty record with health-core's `createEmptyFile`. Every write is health-core's own (`updateProfile`, `stampProfile` for the unit choice, `appendMeasurement`, `correctValue`, and since AC7 `upsertMedication` and `upsertSupplement`) run in the engine: Swift builds no rows and checks no ranges. A write reaches the disk, atomically, before the screen shows it; a refused write changes nothing on disk; a record the app cannot read is never overwritten.
- AC5 (My data): About you (sex, birth year and month, height), units (metric or US), Vitals (`VITAL_METRICS`) and Blood tests (`BLOOD_TEST_METRICS` without PSA, as the web: PSA belongs to prostate screening). Each row shows its latest active value in the user's units, with its day. Adding a value takes the user's unit and a day (today by default, never the future); a value the engine refuses shows the engine's own words. A second value for a day that already has one asks first, and replacing it is a FHIR correction (a new row with `correctsId`, the old row `entered-in-error`). Nothing can be removed (append-only).
- AC6 (the plan is the record's): My plan computes from the stored record whenever it changes. A record without a usable height or sex (health-core's one `PlanError`) asks for them in plain words, with a way to My data; any other failure shows the engine's own words.
- AC7 (engine writes for medications and supplements, D4b 5/5, 2026-10-21): the engine's My data edits take a medication (`medicationKey`, `drugName`, dose) and a supplement (`supplementKey`, `supplementName`, dose, `status` active or stopped, an optional `startedAt`). Each is checked against the API's own `medicationSchema` and `supplementSchema` (a known medication key, a positive dose, a lowercase supplement key, a status), then written by the web's own `upsertMedication` and `upsertSupplement` (state-edits.ts): the keyed row with its lamport, an append-only history row when the change classifies (started, stopped, switched, dose changed; none for an identical re-save or an escalation answer), the file clock moved forward. A supplement's `startedAt` must be a real day or instant that has happened; a stop needs a supplement the record holds. A refusal answers `{ ok: false }` with a reason and writes nothing. The tab shows them since AC8. These writes do not yet run through `RecordSession.edit`, so they have no save loop, merge on conflict or erase guard: follow-up, once the app keeps a session open (ios/architecture.md D4). Tests: `ios/engine/my-data.test.ts` (6: a medication started then dose-changed; a bad key or a negative dose refused; a supplement saved and soft-stopped keeping its start; a start that is not a real past day refused; a stop of an unknown supplement refused; a bad supplement key or no status refused).
- AC8 (medications, screenings, supplements on screen, 2026-10-21): My data shows the web form's medication, cancer screening, bone density and supplement questions, with the web's words, options, hints and show-when rules, because both clients read them from health-core's `input-form.ts` (`medicationForm`, `screeningForm`; the web's InputPanel.tsx imports the same text and write rules, and `InputPanel.input-form-parity.test.tsx` renders the web form against them). Medications follow the plan's cascades (the plan's lipid marker and weight trigger, computed from the stored record): each step opens as the plan suggests it, flat questions without hints when no cascade runs, no section without a relevant value. An answer is written by the web's own rule: `medicationWrites` then `upsertMedication` behind `medicationSchema`; `screeningWrites` (the answer, then '' for each later answer it closes) then `setScreening` behind `SCREENING_KEYS` and `screeningSchema`. The engine writes only a question the form shows now, with an answer it offers (a pickable option, a month in the web's ten-year past or five-year future range, pack-years a whole number 0 to 200); anything else is refused and writes nothing. Screening questions wait for the plan's age (sex, birth year and height) and say so. PSA, under prostate once the user will screen, is a dated measurement with its own history. Supplements: the featured list as one-tap quick-add with the web's default doses, the rest of health-core's list by search, any typed name with the web's custom key, a dose and unit per supplement, and stopping as a soft stop (status stopped, a history row) kept under Stopped with "Taking again". No delete or remove control anywhere.
- AC9 (value history, 2026-10-21): tapping a vital, blood test or PSA that has values opens its history: a trend chart of the active values, and (one tap further, under Show All Data, since 2026-10-23) every row newest first, entered-in-error rows struck through and labelled, the plan's current value marked (or, when the plan sets it aside as out of range, marked as not used). A metric whose rows are all entered in error still opens its history. Tapping an active value corrects it (`correctValue`: a new row, the old one entered-in-error); there is no delete. A metric with no values opens entry directly. **Amended 2026-10-26 (US-58 AC4b, Brad: "Open a page with the guide"):** a metric with a guide opens its page whether or not it has values. **Since 2026-10-26 (cleanup):** every metric has a guide, so every row opens its page on tap; the page's "Add your first value" or "Add Data" opens entry.
- AC10 (launch, 2026-10-21): a new user first sees a welcome screen: what the app does, that the record lives on the phone or in their own Dropbox or Google Drive and never on our servers, and that it is education, not medical advice (App Review 1.4.1); "Get started" is the only way on, and it shows once. The app asks for an App Store rating only after values were saved on three separate days, at the next opening of the plan, once per app version, after a two-second pause that leaving the tab cancels (iOS itself caps it at three a year). Only day stamps and the version asked are kept, in UserDefaults, never a health value. The app has its icon (the welcome screen's logo, the original icon: a white road with green lane dashes winding up from the bottom edge to a red heart with a white outline, on its green gradient, drawn full-bleed by `ios/scripts/make-icon.swift`; the mark is our own drawing, `LogoMark`, which the welcome screen (in a circle, the road running off its bottom edge) and the script share. Never SF Symbols, nor a shape traced from one: Apple's SF Symbols licence forbids them in app icons and logos, so the 2026-10-23 mark traced from one was replaced on 2026-10-25 by the original drawing, Brad), a green accent, the Health & Fitness category and Apple's privacy manifest (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`: no tracking; UserDefaults reason CA92.1). Tests: `ReviewPromptTests.swift` (new user not asked; three days then the plan asks once; many saves on one day count once; a new version may ask again); the welcome screen checked by hand in the simulator. Since 2026-10-23 (Brad) the welcome screen is the app's logo, title and byline over a looping story that replaces the three written points: "Add your numbers" (made-up values arrive, in the region's units), "Get your plan" (a step per area, ticked), "Your data stays yours" ("This iPhone" linked to "Dropbox or Google Drive", and a lock closing on "Never on our servers"). Under Reduce Motion the scenes cross-fade and each shows whole, with no slide, spring, bounce or haptic. VoiceOver reads the story as one sentence saying all three (`WelcomeStory.summary`), and at accessibility text sizes that sentence replaces the scenes. Checked by hand in the simulator, light and dark. App Store screenshots (2026-10-22): `ios/scripts/app-store-shots.sh` takes them on a 6.9-inch simulator (1320 × 2868) from the fictional sample record (docs/examples) plus five synthetic weights, with Apple's 9:41 status bar: My data, My plan, a card opened, the weight page and Chat past its consent screen (nothing sent), each asserted by the opt-in `AppStoreScreenshots` UI test.
- AC11 (cloud sync, 2026-10-21; design: ios/architecture.md D2, D4, D5): the cloud button on My data's About you line (AC17) opens Sync, which offers Connect Dropbox and Connect Google Drive. Google Drive is wired but waits on its iOS OAuth client id (Brad creates it in the web's Google Cloud project); until then its button is disabled and says so, so only Dropbox is claimed to work. Sign-in is PKCE through `ASWebAuthenticationSession` with the web's own Dropbox app and an iOS client in the web's Google Cloud project; tokens live in the Keychain, this device only, and refresh with no client secret. Once connected the app's record IS the cloud's `health-roadmap.json`, the file the website uses. The sync is health-core's own code run in JavaScriptCore: `RecordSession` (save loop, re-read, merge on conflict, erase guard), `SyncManager`, `dropbox-rest.ts` and `drive-rest.ts`, over a small fetch and timer bridge (`ios/engine/shim.ts`); Swift rewrites none of it.
  - AC11a: first connect when the phone and the cloud both hold a record merges them (health-core's `liftDeviceCopy`); neither side's rows are dropped.
  - AC11b: every My data edit runs through `RecordSession.edit` with the erase the screen showed, so it gets the debounced save, the merge on a conflicting write (both rows survive) and the erase guard.
  - AC11c: the app re-reads the cloud on launch, on returning to the foreground, and every minute while on screen; a change made on the web appears without a relaunch. An erase made on another device (a higher `eraseEpoch`) is taken in.
  - AC11d: a save the cloud refused is kept on the phone (the device mirror, US-09 AC4) and sent with the next session; while the cloud cannot be reached the app works on the phone's copy and says so.
  - AC11e: Sync shows where the record is and its state in plain words ("Synced with Dropbox", "Saving…", "Not synced: Dropbox could not be reached. Your changes are on this iPhone."). Since 2026-10-22 (US-52 AC10) it also says what sync does before a connect (one record in your own cloud, read by the website and a new phone, never by Dr Brad's server), each Connect row says where the file goes, and the connected screen names the cloud it is connected to. Its footer says a lab report from Dropbox or Google Drive comes in through "+" and Files (since 2026-10-25, US-52 AC11; it used to point to the Dropbox folder). Connected, Sync names the account by its email (orchestrator, 2026-10-22): Dropbox's `users/get_current_account` at connect, verified only, as the web's `accountEmail`; Drive's `about.user.emailAddress`, under `drive.file` (not yet seen in a real Google sign-in: unverified until one; the cloud's name shows when it is absent); no new scope, and a connect never fails for want of it (the cloud's name shows instead). The email is kept only in `sync-account-email` beside `sync-account` in the backup-excluded Record folder, never logged, and removed on Disconnect and on Delete all my data. The account id is never shown. Not connected is drawn as a phone, never a struck-out iCloud symbol, which read as iCloud. Disconnect copies the cloud record down, merged, then drops the tokens; the app goes back to the record on the phone. The cloud file is never deleted.
  - AC11f: My data says where the record is kept: in the cloud the user connected (never on Dr Brad's server), or after a Disconnect on this iPhone with a copy still in the cloud synced earlier (review A3), or only on this iPhone. My plan's line claims only where the plan was worked out, since chat and lab upload send data (US-52).
  - AC11g (review, 2026-10-21): an edit is checked against the record the user saw. A sheet pins the erase and the units it opened on; a value saved after a remote erase, a remote unit change or a switch of sync on or off is refused with plain words (Codex R1, R2). An edit is taken only once it is merged into the phone's file and marked pending; a phone that cannot write it refuses it and nothing changes (R3).
  - AC11h (review, 2026-10-21): a reopen that fails goes back to the phone's file, and edits made while the cloud opens wait there and are merged in; a Disconnect made while an open is under way wins (R4, R5, A5). A re-read that fails says why (a revoked grant shows "Sign in again"); a Drive rate or daily limit is a retry, a full Drive says so, and none of them asks for a sign-in (R6, A8). "Synced" shows only when nothing waits on the phone (F1). Each engine session is numbered; news from a session the app no longer shows is dropped, and of two racing opens only the newest stays (F2, F4). Signing in again as a different account is refused: Disconnect first (A6). The record's account is Dropbox's `account_id` or Drive's `about.user.permissionId`.
- AC11i (sync explained, Brad 2026-10-22: "visually explain to them what's going on and why"): where the person chooses a cloud (Sync before connecting, and the welcome screen's "I already use Health Roadmap"), a diagram shows their own cloud at the top, this iPhone and the website below it, and silver data flowing both ways along each line, with nothing to Dr Brad's server. Still under Reduce Motion; VoiceOver reads one sentence saying the same. Text past accessibility size 2 is capped there; it redraws at most 30 times a second. Checked by eye on the simulator.
- AC12 (reminders, on-device, D7, 2026-10-21): My data has a Reminders section: one switch, "Remind me when something is due", then each item health-core's `computeReminderSchedule` gives (the web's email schedule: per-category preferences honoured, the annual floor, nothing for a minor) with its month (health-core's `formatReminderDate`, "May 2027", as the web's emails write it), or "Due now". Turning it on explains first, then asks iOS's permission; a refusal leaves it off and points to Settings; not yet asked offers "Allow notifications". The engine (`ios/engine/reminders.ts`) also gives the notification days: the due day, then every group cooldown (90, 180 or 365 days) while due, today kept and never earlier, one a day however many fall due on it, the soonest 64 (iOS's cap), ids `reminder.<day>`. The app rebuilds them from scratch on launch, on return and on every record change, at 9:00 on the phone's clock. The lock screen says only "Health Roadmap: A check-up is due. Open the app to see which."; a tap opens My plan. The opt-in is the phone's (a file beside the record, left out of backups, holding the record's erase epoch), not the record's email `reminderOptIn`; an erase (the epoch moves) ends it and cancels every pending reminder; an unreadable record cancels them for that round only. No server, no email. Tests: `ios/engine/reminders.test.ts` (11: health-core's schedule, soonest first; due day then cooldown repeats; today kept across a day boundary in Pacific/Auckland; nothing for the past; the cap and stable ids; one a day; the web's date text; preferences; the erase epoch; a minor gets nothing; overdue marked), `ReminderSchedulerTests.swift` (14, a fake notification center: nothing before opt-in; permission then the engine's days; a refusal; Settings off; 64 pending; a refill replaces ours and keeps others; an erase cancels and ends the opt-in; the opt-in survives a relaunch, in the record's folder; an unreadable record cancels but keeps the opt-in; a grant with an unreadable record is not a refusal; opting out redraws the switch; the generic wording and 9:00 trigger; the real engine's annual floor). Checked by hand in the simulator (a synthetic record): the section and its list, the explanation, then iOS's own permission sheet. Not yet checked by hand: Allow, a delivered notification and its tap to My plan (the simulator panel had no access for the agent); owed with the real iPhone.
- AC13 (Apple Health in, engine rules, 2026-10-21; ios/architecture.md D6): readings of weight, waist, blood pressure and height come in as `{ externalId, metricType, value (SI), measuredAt, pairId? }`, `measuredAt` being the instant with the UTC offset of the zone it was taken in (`2026-10-21T08:30:00+13:00`), and health-core's `importDeviceSamples` (device-import.ts) decides what lands, through the My data edit `appleHealth`. Each reading is an appended row with `source: apple_health` and the HealthKit UUID as `externalId`; `recordedAt` is that instant with its offset (`2026-10-21T08:30:00.000+13:00`), so its date is the slot's day and the web shows it as a moment, not a UTC day. A reading whose id any row carries, entered-in-error included, is skipped. It fills an empty day, or replaces the day's earlier Apple Health reading (compared as instants) as a FHIR correction (`correctsId`, the old row `entered-in-error`, the new row keeping its own time on the same day), so the day's latest reading is active whatever order readings arrive in; it never supersedes a value a person typed or corrected. The two halves of a blood pressure (one `pairId`) land together or not at all: a pair missing a half, with a half out of range, or meeting a typed or later half, lands neither. Readings measured before the record's `erasedAt` are skipped. Height fills an empty profile height only. Out-of-range values, other metrics, readings timed after now (five minutes allowed for a device clock running ahead; compared as instants, so a reading from a zone already on the phone's tomorrow still lands) and times without an offset are skipped. A batch with nothing new returns the same record, so nothing is written. Deletions in Health are never handed over (append-only). These rules hold on one device; across devices the merge keeps the newest-written row of a slot, which can undo them (cloud-sync slice, merge-class). Blood glucose is not read: it is a catalogue lab value, and lab rows carry no `externalId` (Health Records labs are out of scope, D6).
- AC14 (Apple Health out, engine rules): health-core's `deviceWrites` (device-export.ts) lists what the app writes to Apple Health: each slot's active weight or waist row, and a day's blood pressure once both halves are there, as one reading. A row from Apple Health, or a correction of one (judged by the chain's root), is never written back. Each write is keyed by the root id of its correction chain, with the chain's length as a rising version (both chains' for a blood pressure), so a correction replaces the sample even if the phone's clock went back. Blood tests are not written.
- AC15 (Apple Health in the app, 2026-10-21; ios/architecture.md D6): My data has an Apple Health section. "Connect Apple Health" shows Apple's sheet, with purpose strings that say what is read (weight, height, waist, blood pressure) and written (weight, waist, blood pressure), then imports. New readings arrive at launch, on return to the foreground, on unlock and through observer queries with background delivery; each kind's anchor is kept outside the record and moves only after the record holding that batch is on disk, and none is kept until a kind has given a whole reading, both halves for a blood pressure (iOS answers a refused read with nothing, and a kept anchor would skip the past once allowed). The zone of each reading is HealthKit's `HKMetadataKeyTimeZone` when present, else the phone's. The app's own samples are never read back (bundle id, or the `healthroadmap:` sync identifier). A locked phone shows "waiting for unlock" and retries, the anchor kept. A batch with nothing new writes nothing, to the phone or the cloud. An import takes a typed value's path (`RecordStore.applyNow`): with cloud sync on (AC11) it goes through the session, its merge and its erase guard, checked against the erase and units shown at that moment, never a sheet's pin (AC11g pins sheets, and an import is not one); a refusal re-reads the record and tries once more, and a second refusal keeps the anchor so the batch comes again. Typed weight, waist and paired blood pressure go to Health once per (sync id, version), as HealthKit sync identifier and version, so a correction replaces our sample; a kind the person did not allow to be written is skipped; a write Health refuses is retried next time and does not hold back the others; a value for today is dated noon or now, whichever is earlier. A refresh asked for while one runs waits for it, so a background wake reports done only after the import saved. Not yet: an erase deleting our samples from Health (the app has no erase yet).
- AC16 (delete all my data and export, US-11 on the iPhone, 2026-10-21): My data ends with a "Your record" section. **Export my record** shares `health-roadmap.json`, the record as shown, in the web's schema, through the share sheet, which writes the file itself (the app keeps no copy); its footer says anyone given the file can read the record. The website has no "load a file" flow yet, so the file is for keeping, for an agent (US-29, US-30), or to drop into the cloud folder by hand. **Delete all my data** is two steps: a page saying what goes (the record on this iPhone, the chat history, the reminders, and, with a cloud connected, the record in that cloud: the file stays there with the erase in it, a higher `eraseEpoch` and the erased rows listed, so other devices take it in, US-11 AC6; never a delete) and what it cannot reach (exported copies, the provider's version history, chat questions already sent, a value another device has not synced), then iOS's "Delete everything?" alert. The erase is the engine's, in the web's order: the record is read first; then the chat tombstones (health-core `ChatSession.eraseAll`, best effort, written only when they were made; with a cloud open, the `chat-history.json` the website saved there first, through `ChatSession` on the cloud host as the web does, then the phone's own; the cloud step is best effort and reported on its own (`cloudChatErased`), so a corrupt file or a newer website's schema never blocks the phone's chat erase; the confirmation names the website's chat in that cloud, and the result says whether it is gone or still there: Try again when the provider did not answer, and when the file cannot be read (corrupt, or a newer schema) delete it on the website or delete `chat-history.json` in the cloud; a refusal after the chat step never says nothing was deleted when a chat file was tombstoned; its writes send no sync status, 2026-10-22, adversary R1-R3); then the record. With no cloud, the phone's file is erased by health-core's `buildErasedFile` (`ios/engine/erase.ts`); a record the app cannot read refuses and nothing changes. With a cloud open, `RecordSession.deleteAllData` runs (`cloudErase`): a cloud that cannot be read refuses, nothing changes anywhere, chat included, and the app says so; on success the pre-erase phone copy and the pending marker are cleared and the erased record becomes the phone copy; a write that fails after the read leaves the erased record on screen and on the phone, marked pending, and the app says the cloud has not taken it yet (the next save sends it). With a cloud connected but not open (the app on its phone copy), the erase refuses, as the web refuses in its on-device fallback. Reminders end because the epoch moves (`ReminderScheduler`). The open chat drops its conversation. Afterwards My data is empty, the user's units are kept (a setting, as the web keeps its unit preference), and the welcome screen does not come back. With Apple Health connected (AC15), the erase then deletes the samples this app wrote to Health (by source, all `healthroadmap:` sync ids) and forgets their written versions; readings other apps and devices wrote stay in Health, and the import anchors stay, so they are not imported again (D6). The confirmation says both. Health refusing the delete never undoes the record erase; the result says so and points to the Health app. Known gap: an erase made on another device erases this phone's record and reminders, but not its chat history, which lives only on the phone. Review fixes, 2026-10-21 (adversary R1-R6, Codex R1-R3): with a cloud open the chat tombstones are written by the app inside the engine's pre-erase step, after the read and before the record goes up, so a kill between the two never leaves the record erased and the chat whole (Codex R3); Connect and Disconnect are refused while an erase runs, and the erase page hides its back button, so the session the erase writes under cannot be swapped (R2); an answer streaming in the chat when the erase lands is dropped, never shown in the emptied chat or saved (R1); after a Disconnect the confirmation says that connecting that cloud again erases the same values there (the higher epoch and its listed rows win, US-09 AC23; R3); an unreadable phone record names the one way left, deleting the app (R4); a refusal other than an unreachable cloud shows the engine's own words (R5); the cloud file is described as keeping the erase, not as empty (R6). Usage signal: none from the app (D9); App Store Connect only. Tests: `ios/engine/erase.test.ts` (5), `ios/engine/cloud.test.ts` "cloudErase" (9: erase into the fake Dropbox with the phone copy erased and nothing pending, the chat written before the cloud write; a chat write the phone refuses is reported and the erase goes on; the website's cloud chat history tombstoned before the record goes up, with no sync status for its write; a cloud chat history that is unreadable, from a newer schema, or unreachable is reported as `cloudChatErased: false` with `cloudChatProblem` while the phone chat and the record are erased; another device takes it in; an unreachable cloud changes nothing and writes no chat; a failed write is kept pending and sent by the next flush), `ios/HealthRoadmapTests/DataEraserTests.swift` (17: a refusal after the chat step names what was deleted; the website's chat history in Dropbox tombstoned by the app's cloud erase; a cloud chat the app cannot erase still erases the phone chat and the words say the website's conversations are still there; the result words name the website's chat per provider; a Disconnect during the erase refused, a mutation run without the guard fails it; an answer asked before the erase not saved after it, a mutation run fails it; Apple Health's own samples deleted and forgotten, a refused delete said, never-connected Health untouched).
- AC17 (My data layout and metric pages, Brad 2026-10-22; ios/architecture.md D11): **Vitals are Apple Health cards (Brad 2026-10-23):** each vital is its own tile; one with a reading shows its name in the regular text colour (no symbol), its day and a chevron, then the value large (**the day as Apple Health's cards write it, Brad 2026-10-25:** "Today", "Yesterday", then the short date, as US-56's live cards do; compact rows such as blood tests keep their date; `DayText.when`, tested in `LiveMathsTests.testAVitalsCardSaysTodayYesterdayOrTheDate_US25_AC17`) with a larger trend beside it; one with none says Add. **Colour lives only in the chart (Brad 2026-10-23):** each metric has its own graph colour (`MetricChart.colors`, one palette), used by its card's or row's trend line and its metric page's chart; no two metrics share one, blood pressure's systolic and diastolic are related reds, and a metric without one takes the accent colour (US-56's readings get theirs when US-56 is built). Each chart colour is a fixed, hand-chosen pair, one for light mode and a calmer one for dark, each reading 3:1 or better as a line on its card (`MetricChart.palette`, built once). The section icons and the welcome story's row icons are calmer in dark mode too (`Color.softInDark`: less saturation and brightness). Section headings keep their one coloured symbol (AC17d). A section's rows share one value column, as wide as its widest reading, so a wide value never pushes its row's trend out of line (review 2026-10-23); the trend's width scales a little with text; at accessibility sizes the row stacks as before. **No title bar on My data.** The sections run Vitals, Blood tests, Medications, Screening, Supplements, Reminders, About you, Apple Health, Your record (Brad 2026-10-23: About you rarely changes, so it moves down). The lab upload "+" and Sync sit on the Vitals line, right-aligned; the Metric/US switch is a "Units" row in About you, set once. Scrolled rows stop under the clock: a strip of the list's own background covers the status bar. **Height in US units** shows as feet and inches ("5 ft 10 in") and is entered on two wheels, whole feet and 0 to 11 inches. The engine converts with health-core's `feetInchesToCm` and shows with `cmToFeetInches` (the web's rules, InputPanel.tsx: 11.5 in rounds up to the next foot); the record still stores centimetres, and updateProfile's 50 to 250 cm range refuses the rest in its own words. Saving the wheels unchanged writes nothing, so 178 cm is never rounded to 177.8 (adversary R4). Feet and inches mean one height in any unit system, so a unit change on another device does not refuse them. **Blood pressure is one row**, "124/79 mmHg" with its day: the newest day holding an active half; a missing half shows as a dash. Entry takes systolic and diastolic side by side with one day. The engine's `bloodPressure` edit (ios/engine/blood-pressure.ts) writes both rows on that day, as the web's matrix pairs them, or neither: a half out of range, a future day or a missing number writes nothing. A day that holds either half asks first ("This day already has a blood pressure"); replacing it corrects only the half that changed (a `correctsId` row, the old one `entered-in-error`): re-correcting an unchanged half would join merge's last-writer-wins and could undo another device's fix of it (review, 2026-10-22). A half the day lacks is added; the exact same pair writes nothing. A replace carries the ids of the day's active rows the user saw (from the value being corrected, or read when the "replace it?" prompt shows); if the day's active rows differ at save time, in the phone file or through the cloud session, nothing is saved and the user sees "Your record changed while this was open, so this was not saved. Close this and enter the value again." (Codex R1, adversary R3). **Tapping a value with any history pushes its page** (no longer a sheet), laid out as Apple Health's: the range picker's card sits right under the title, with no empty band (Brad 2026-10-25: "why is there a large gap"; `metricPageList`, shared with US-56's pages, trims the list's top margin to 8 pt); a range picker (W, M, 6M, Y; no All since 2026-10-25, Brad: "the maximum that we should show is the previous year, kind of like what Apple Health do"; all four are offered whenever the metric has a value to draw, however sparse, as Apple Health's are, and the page opens on the narrowest range that holds every value, else Y; a range wider than the values shows them at its right edge on its own axis, so one reading on W sits on a week's axis, never one labelled by the hour; Show All Data still lists every value), the latest value large with its day, and a Swift Charts line chart. **Since 2026-10-23 (Brad: "just copy what Apple Health have done")** a range opens ending on the newest value, not today, and scrolls back across every value, so a weight from months ago fills the chart instead of leaving it empty on the right; a newer value added moves the window to it, and coming back from Show All Data keeps the scroll; scrubbing picks only days in view; "+" (top right) opens entry; under the chart, **Show All Data** pushes every value newest first with AC9's correction (no delete), and **Unit** shows the unit, with a menu for a test that has its own units (Metric or US) and Lp(a)'s three. Dragging a finger across the chart picks the nearest day and shows its value and date in a callout, with a selection haptic. Blood pressure plots systolic and diastolic as two lines; its history replays each day (orchestrator, 2026-10-22). Every row of the day, both halves, active or not, is put in write order (`createdAt`; at a tie a correction after the row it names, then id) and grouped into writes: a row joins the open write when its half is not there yet, it is within 5 s of the write's first row (the web, CLI and MCP stamp each half with its own clock) and it does not correct a row in that write. Each write sets its halves on the pair and leaves a snapshot; a half not yet written is a dash. The pair now is shown active and every other snapshot struck, newest first; a snapshot equal to the one before, written only by rows now set aside, is dropped. So correcting only systolic 120 to 130 shows "130/80" and, struck, "120/80"; a one-half day replaced shows "120/82" and, struck, "–/80"; edits a second apart (120, 125, 128) and an Apple Health batch of three readings keep every value. A row merge's slot reconciliation set aside (entered in error, no correction naming it) is listed, as AC9 lists every value, over the pair as it stood, but never changes the pair later writes build on, so it cannot leak into the active pair. Each history row has its own id; `pairIds` are the day's active rows from the engine's own slot lookup (`findActiveInSlot`), the ids a replace sends back. No target band: the engine gives the app no target or reference range, and the app invents none. VoiceOver reads the chart through `accessibilityChartDescriptor` (audio graph, one series per line); at accessibility text sizes the rows stack label over value and the chart asks for fewer axis labels. - AC18 (engine updates over the air, D3, 2026-10-22; Brad: "should automatically come through if I update github"; design amended by a fresh adversary, R1-R15): a fix to health-core reaches installed apps without an App Store release, and nothing but a release signed with a pinned key can. **Release:** two steps, so no repo code runs next to a key: `npm run engine:build` (`env -u ENGINE_SIGNING_KEY`; its first module refuses if a key is still set, then loads the build) builds the engine (parity checked; refuses uncommitted engine source and more than one release a minute), then `node ios/scripts/sign-engine.mjs`, run directly (Node's own modules and `engine-signing.mjs` only, `/usr/bin/security` by absolute path), checks and signs what was built. Together they write `ios/engine-release/bridge-<id>/`: the bundle as `<sha256>.js`, `manifest.json` (canonical JSON, keys sorted: `appId`, `bridge`, `channel` "production", `format` 1, `issuedAt`, `keyId`, `minAppBuild`, `minVersion`, `notAfter` 30 days on, `schemaVersion`, `sha256`, `size`, `version` UTC `yyyymmddHHMM` above the last release) and `manifest.sig` (base64 Ed25519 over `"health-roadmap-engine-manifest/v1\n"` plus the manifest's exact bytes). `bridge` is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `ios/engine/bridge-contract.json`; Node and XCTest fail if the engine's doors, natives or events or Swift's drift from it. Three keys are pinned by id: `daily`, only in Brad's login Keychain, trusted by no app; `cold`, in 1Password; `ci`, only in the GitHub `engine-signing` environment's secret. A test fails if a key-shaped file or a private key appears in any tracked file. `--if-changed` releases nothing for an unchanged engine. Publishing is committing the folder to `main` (locally today; the GitHub job `.github/workflows/engine-release.yml` is added, 2026-10-25: secret-less build, a `verify` job that takes the commit from the event, computes the bridge itself and checks the artifact (the build decides only whether to upload), then signing in a separate `engine-signing` environment with Brad as reviewer, running no repo code; it needs Brad's push, the `ENGINE_SIGNING_KEY` secret, and his approval of each release). **Check:** on coming on screen (launch included), at most once per 6 hours, the app GETs `manifest.json` and `manifest.sig` from `raw.githubusercontent.com` on an ephemeral session (no cookies, no cache, a plain User-Agent, no redirects, no health data, no device id; short timeouts; failure keeps the current engine silently). It verifies the signature over the exact bytes against the pinned keys before parsing, the `keyId` naming the key that verified, the canonical spelling (a duplicate or unknown key refused), then `format`, `appId`, `channel`, `bridge`, `schemaVersion` equal to the bundled engine's, `minAppBuild` at most this build, `version` above both the bundled engine's and the highest this phone ever accepted (no rollback) and at or above the stored floor (`minVersion` raises it), `issuedAt` and `version` no more than 2 days past the phone's clock, and `notAfter` still ahead (install only, never for a bundle already installed). Only then it downloads the bundle, refuses one over its size or 8 MB or whose SHA-256 differs, and stages it with its manifest and signature in `Application Support/Engine`, left out of backups. **Activation:** only at a fresh launch, never mid-session. The staged files are read once; signature, fields and hash are checked again against the pins of this app; the bundle then runs in a quarantined context (no network, no token, the phone file in memory) through a self-test: its version and schema, every contract door, a new record, edits, My data, a plan and its layout, and merge goldens (rows in equal rows out, entered-in-error sticky, the higher `eraseEpoch` wins). Only then is the live engine built from the same bytes. A "trying" mark is set before a version's first foreground load and cleared once the engine has drawn the user's own record on My data and planned it, or the plan screen planned it, whichever comes first (a plan or health-core's PlanError counts; a throw never does); still there at the next foreground launch (a crash or hang before the record was shown), or a failed check or self-test, marks that version bad and deletes it; the next staged version or the bundled engine runs. A background launch never tries a new version, and an unreadable staged file there is "not now", never "bad". The bundled engine carries its version (the source commit's UTC minute); an app update whose engine is newer deletes older downloads. **Fence:** JavaScript never holds a token: `accessToken` answers `native-token:<provider>`, and Swift swaps the real token in only on an allow-listed method, host and path of that provider (Dropbox `files/download` and `files/upload`, with `files/list_folder` and `/continue` removed 2026-10-25 when the phone stopped listing folders, US-52 AC11; Drive's `files` list, create, get and upload create and update); each route lists its query parameters (Dropbox none, Drive only what drive-rest.ts sends) and only the adapters' headers pass; any other path (Dropbox `sharing/*`, Drive `permissions`), host (the app's server included), scheme, query parameter (`access_token`, `key` and the like refused in any case), header or Authorization is refused, and no redirect is followed. The chat context the engine builds is checked in Swift (a JSON object with a unit system, under 512 KB) and only the top-level keys health-core's `chatContextOf` produces are sent to our server. `highWater` and `floor` are mirrored in the Keychain and only ever raised, so a corrupt or missing state file cannot lower them; a corrupt one also deletes every staged version. **Disclosure:** the privacy policy says GitHub sees the IP address when the app checks for engine updates and the check carries no health data; the App Review notes say updates change computation and text only. **Success measure:** engine-load failures in crash reports (App Store Connect; the app sends nothing, D9). Tests: `ios/scripts/release-engine.test.ts`, `ios/scripts/signing-key-guard.test.ts`, `ios/engine/bridge.test.ts` (Node); `EngineManifestTests`, `EngineUpdaterTests`, `EngineBootTests`, `EngineFenceTests`, `EngineBridgeContractTests` (XCTest); an end-to-end run in the simulator against a local server (DEBUG-only base URL and test key, compiled out of Release).

Tests: `packages/health-core/src/cell-unit.test.ts` (2); `ios/engine/my-data.test.ts` "Lp(a) unit (US-05 AC2, US-25 AC20)" (5: the default by units, display and history and trend in each unit, typed values, a correction and out-of-range words in each unit, the field-stamped write equal to `stampProfile` and its merge with the web's edits, the plan text unchanged); `cloud.test.ts` "AC20: Lp(a) is read in the record's unit…"; `RecordStoreTests.swift` `testLpaUnitMenuWritesTheRecordAndATypedValueIsReadInIt`, `testAnLpaUnitChosenInTheOpenSheetReadsItsValue`, `testAnLpaValueTypedBeforeItsUnitChangedIsRefusedOnThePhone`, `testACorrectionKeepsItsSheetWhenItsScreenMoves` (a unit chosen in a correction's sheet moves its screen, never its id); `CloudSyncTests.swift` `testLpaValueTypedBeforeTheWebChangesItsUnitIsRefused`; the web's own suites unchanged.
- AC21 (engine off the main thread, Brad 2026-10-22: "we want the main/UI thread to only be for UI elements"; ios/architecture.md D2 stage 2): the engine runs on its own serial queue, never the main thread: the plan, every My data edit, My data itself and the phone's file writes run there, and the main thread only shows what comes back. Record changes land one at a time in the order they were asked for, and the decisions about the record are steps in that same line: whether to show a cloud record just opened (every edit asked for before has landed and been counted; if any came in, the app opens again and that open merges the phone's file in), the phone erase (an import accepted meanwhile lands after the erase, never under it; a cloud connect completing meanwhile opens again and takes the erase in, never restoring what it removed), and a units switch or an Lp(a) unit choice (entry waits until it lands). A sheet saves against the record it showed when its row was tapped (AC11g; the tap's screen travels with the sheet, nothing stays pinned), even when it closes or the screen changes while the save waits; an Apple Health import is checked against the record as it is when its turn comes. A value typed before the record's units changed is refused on the phone, as in the cloud. A sheet stays open, its buttons held, until its save lands, and closes only on a save; a picker waits while its edit lands. A session never clears a pending marker set after it read the phone, a phone edit's marker is set before its write (a failed write puts back the generation it found), and news a session sends after it is shown is never overwritten by the open finishing. A lab report's saved count is taken in the same engine step as its import, against the record it lands on. A cloud record handed over before one already shown never replaces it; a record or failure a session sends before it is shown is kept and shown with it. Reading a report from a Files pick, a file or a folder (PDF pages drawn, ZIPs opened), runs on the shared pool, neither the main thread nor the engine's queue (`LabFileReader.decoded`, merge review R2, 2026-10-23); an Lp(a) unit choice holds entry and takes its turn in the tap itself, as a units switch does (R1). Stage 3 (2026-10-23) moved the rest: resizing a photo or a camera scan runs on the shared pool (`LabFileReader.photo`, `pictures`); chat history's list, messages, saves and deletes await the engine, and each save's read-modify-write runs in one engine step, as the erase's tombstone write does on the phone and in the cloud; a typed number is read in Swift by the engine's own rule (`TypedNumber.read`, held to the engine on the edge cases; it is in the binary, so a change to health-core's number rule needs an app release, not only an engine update); a value's history page and its chart draw what the engine answered, asked again whenever the record or its units move (one engine call per change per metric, a second ask joining the first), and the chart's points are built once per history, not on every redraw; a history read for an older record or unit is drawn but opens no correction until the fresh one lands, and a correction's "Now" hint comes only from a history in the sheet's own unit (adversary R2, Codex: never "100 mg/dL" from a 100 nmol/L Lp(a) row); a chat conversation still loading when the person taps New chat or opens another is dropped (Codex), and a swiped conversation leaves the list at once (R9); onboarding's unit conversions, a trial engine's confirm and the sync attach (queued on the engine ahead of any later call) never wait; a cloud session's news is decoded on the engine's queue before it reaches the main thread. Late answers never undo a later choice (re-check 2026-10-24): of two quick onboarding unit taps the last wins, a late conversion never lands over it (Codex); a list read before a swiped conversation's tombstone is written leaves that row out (N3); a page opened after an erase or a unit switch never shows the earlier values (histories cleared; a row tap opens its page at once since 2026-10-26, so the N4 tap guard is gone); and a history is asked again only when the record or its units really change (N2). The engine updater (AC18) does its network work off the main thread (the GETs, the signature and hash checks, the staging of a bundle), while its reads and writes of the update state stay serialized on the main actor with a trial engine's confirm, so neither overwrites the other's write (Codex and adversary R1, 2026-10-24). The app cannot wait on the engine: `blocking` exists only in the test target. Wherever JavaScript runs (`callValue`, `settle`, `evaluate`), a DEBUG build checks it is on the engine's queue and not on the main queue. - AC21b (launch off the main thread, Brad 2026-10-23; a plain opening, Brad 2026-10-26): at launch the system launch screen and the app's launch view show only My data's background (`LaunchBackground`: `systemGroupedBackground`, light and dark, with Increase Contrast's variants), so nothing changes on screen until the first real screen appears; the launch view is labelled "Loading" (Brad 2026-10-26: "on open, there's a brief flash of a screen, then the 'my data' page appears"; the logo it replaced showed for about 100 ms). A new user goes from that background straight to the welcome screen, and a relaunch mid-questions straight to the questions, both on the same background: the first-run cover is presented without animation, never sliding up over an empty My data. Behind it the app builds its parts off the main thread: the engine's files, its signature, hash and self-test checks and its load (`EngineBoot`), then the phone's record, read and drawn once (`RecordStore.open`). Then it swaps to the app. The order holds: a downloaded engine on trial is marked before any screen shows the record; the record is read once before the first screen; the sync is attached, and the pending marker armed, before any edit can be asked for. The notification delegate is set as the process starts, so a reminder tap that launches the app still reaches My plan, and a background launch (a Health delivery) builds the parts too. Apple Health's observer queries and background delivery are registered then too, synchronously, as Apple requires (adversary R1); a delivery awaits the parts, refreshes, and only then tells HealthKit it is done, or at once if the parts never come. Coming on screen reads what is new in Health, beside sync and the engine check. Measured by hand in the simulator, 2026-10-23 (a two-year record, six launches, `LaunchClock`): before, the first frame came about 150 ms after the app's init, all of it waiting; after, the launch screen shows about 50 ms after init and the app about 165 ms after, with the main thread free between. Measured on an iPhone 15 Pro Max, 2026-10-26 (Release, five true cold launches, a 103 KB record and a connected cloud): process start to app init 55 to 95 ms, engine ready and record drawn by 146 to 177 ms, My data on screen at 184 to 226 ms, then one main-thread stall of 105 to 121 ms for the first render; the cloud record opens 1.4 to 2.2 s later. - AC21c (the main-thread watchdog, Brad 2026-10-23; slimmed in review 2026-10-24): a debug build can watch the main thread when the launch argument `-mainWatchdogLog <path>` names a log; otherwise it does not run, and never in Release. A background thread pings main every 50 ms and, when main took 100 ms or more to answer, appends a timestamp and "main stalled N ms" to that file (`MainThreadWatchdog`). It takes no stacks and no test reads it: it is for timing by hand. The rule it watched is enforced in code instead (AC21: test-only `blocking`, the JavaScript precondition). A debug build in the simulator stalls over 100 ms in the system's own first-time work (the scene connecting, Metal compiling a shader, the keyboard loading, Charts' first draw: seven such, 108 to 371 ms, measured by hand on 2026-10-23), which is why no test fails on a stall (docs/reference.md gotcha). Tests: none (a debug tool).

A tile the engine cannot draw leaves the tiles out, never the plan below them (adversary R7). Values read in the phone's per-test units (AC17e); a known minor's tiles keep the values and drop every adult reading (US-07 AC6). Drawn as Apple Health cards, two across (one at accessibility text sizes): the name in plain text with no symbol (Brad 2026-10-23, as the vitals cards), the value large with its unit, the status in a capsule tinted by the web's status colour, the only colour on the tile. VoiceOver reads each tile as one sentence ("BMI, 25.2"), with the hint "Shows why".
