### US-52 · Chat and lab upload in the iPhone app, with no sign-in — **added 2026-10-21 (Brad: "chat and lab upload in the app, no user sign-in"; design: ios/architecture.md D8)**
As an app user, I ask Dr Brad's chatbot about my plan and upload a lab report, without making an account, and the server that pays for the AI knows each request came from a genuine copy of the app.
- **Usage signal:** App Store Connect analytics only (US-25, D9): the app sends no product events. The server's own operational counters (turns and files per day, refusals by reason) are numbers with no health value, kept in its logs.
- AC1 (the gate): `/api/app/v1/chat` and `/api/app/v1/lab-import` answer only a request that carries an App Attest assertion from a key the server registered (`/api/app/v1/attest/challenge`, `/api/app/v1/attest/register`). Registration verifies the attestation against Apple's App Attest root CA (pinned), a fresh server challenge (HMAC'd, 5 minutes), the nonce in the leaf's extension, the key id as the hash of the certified public key, the app id (team id + bundle id, from env), counter 0, the environment's AAGUID, and the credential id; a key id already stored is a 409. Each assertion signs `SHA256(method, path, SHA256(raw body))`, so it covers this request and no other; its counter must be higher than the stored one, advanced atomically, so a replay fails. The key is looked up before the body is read. Any other failure is a 401 with a closed reason, and no Anthropic call is made.
- AC2 (fail closed): with no team id configured, the key store unreachable, or on the brand surface (`CHAT_SURFACE=brand`), the endpoints answer 503; they never fall back to letting a request through. A key-store error is never reported as an unknown key.
- AC3 (simulator bypass): the simulator has no App Attest. A request with the dev header is accepted ONLY when `APP_ATTEST_DEV_BYPASS=1` AND `NODE_ENV` is `development` or `test` (an allow-list: unset or `production` refuses, whatever the flag says; tests prove both). The app sends the header only in a DEBUG build on the simulator (`#if DEBUG && targetEnvironment(simulator)`, checked by reading the code: a test cannot build the other configurations).
- AC4 (limits): per key exactly (60 turns, 30 files per UTC day, counted in the same SQL step as the counter), per IP (IPv6 by /64) and per machine (`APP_CHAT_DAILY_CAP`, `APP_LAB_DAILY_CAP`), for chat turns and lab files separately; lab files also spend the web's shared per-machine file cap (`machineFiles`, US-35 AC10), and the app's own cap is the smaller one so the app cannot use up the web's. Over a limit answers 429 and calls no model. Key registration attempts are capped per IP.
- AC5 (chat): the app's turn runs the web widget's pipeline (`api.chat.ts`): classifier, router, the same model, posture and guardrails, NDJSON streaming (status, sources, text, done). The app sends what the widget sends: the question, the conversation's earlier turns from its own file, and `chatContextOf` over the record (health-core). The server stores nothing of the turn: no conversation or message rows, no guest session, no match-event row, no audit row (D9). No form edits are proposed to the app (its UI cannot apply them yet).
- AC6 (chat on the phone): a Chat view, native SwiftUI. Before the first message a consent screen names Anthropic, says what is sent (the question, the conversation, and the health summary from the record), that Brad's server keeps none of it, and that Anthropic handles it under its API terms (no training on it, kept for a limited time); nothing is sent until the user agrees. A "Stop sharing" control withdraws the agreement. The answer streams in with its status lines and the articles it drew on. Conversations are kept on the phone in `chat-history.json`, written by health-core's `ChatSession` (the web's rule: title, cap, tombstones). A saved conversation reads back with each question above its answer, on the phone and the web (health-core's `mergeMessages` order, 2026-10-21).
- AC6a (one chat history store, 2026-10-24): the app makes one chat history store at launch, shared by Chat and "Delete all my data". An erase reads its list again, so Chat shows what the erase left; opening History reads it again too, so the sheet lists the conversations saved on the phone. Chat keeps no list of its own. Tests: `AppChatLabTests.testTheHistorySheetListsSavedConversations`, `DataEraserTests`.
- AC7 (lab upload): a "+" button opens a sheet, "Add lab results", that asks where the report is (AC10). The phone reads the file the way the web does (a PDF page with text goes as text, a scanned page as a JPEG; a ZIP's PDFs and images one by one; the web's page and size limits) and sends it to `/api/app/v1/lab-import` with `ownDates: true` and `refusedRows: true` (so values the report dates itself are kept, and refused rows come back as such), which runs the web's extraction (`extractOrClassify`) and returns proposed values. The server stores nothing. A consent screen like AC6's comes first: before the first file is sent, after it is picked (since 2026-10-22, so choosing a source comes before the AI question); nothing leaves the phone for the server until the user agrees.
- AC8 (the app writes the record): the extracted values are shown for the user to confirm, each with its day (the value's own day, else the report's; when the report prints no full day the user picks one). A value the extractor asked about (its `question`, such as "Was this a blood test?") shows the question and starts unticked; one it was unsure of, or whose unit it guessed, says to check it. Only ticked values are written, by health-core's `bulkAppendValues` (the web's and the connector's one bulk rule) with `source: lab_import`: a slot that already holds a value is skipped and said so; a lab unit the catalogue refuses is listed as not saved. Values from an undated previous column are not offered (the server strips them: the app does not send `undatedPrev`). Non-lab documents are filed by AC13d.
- AC9 (the privacy sentence, D9): the plan screen no longer says "No health data left your device", which chat and upload make false; it says the plan was worked out on this iPhone.
- AC10 (where the report is; first built 2026-10-22, rewritten 2026-10-25; Brad 2026-10-25: Files first, then Photos and Scan): the sheet offers three sources, in this order, each with a few words on what happens. **Files** leads, under the header "Where are your medical records?", with "A PDF, photo, ZIP or folder"; it opens the iOS file importer (`UIDocumentPickerViewController` through SwiftUI's `fileImporter`) for a PDF, JPEG, PNG, ZIP or folder. Under it one line: "Files reaches Dropbox, Google Drive and iCloud Drive when their apps are on this iPhone. The app gets only the file you pick." Then **Photos** ("A photo of a paper report") opens the photo library; the picture goes as one JPEG page, as a picked JPEG does. Then, on a phone with a camera, **Scan** ("Use the camera, one page at a time") opens the iOS document camera; its pages go as one report of JPEG pages, the web's 20-page limit kept. There is no From Dropbox or From Google Drive list (AC11). Reading from Files (adversary R3, R4, 2026-10-25): a file's size is checked before it is read, and it is read through a file coordinator, so a Dropbox, Google Drive or iCloud file not yet on the phone downloads first. A folder's walk stops at 5,000 entries ("This folder holds more than 5,000 files. Pick a smaller folder."); every report's size is checked before any is read, so one over the web's limit or more than 200 MB in all refuses the folder ("This folder holds more than 200 MB of reports. Pick a smaller folder, or the reports one at a time."); a folder with none says "This folder holds no reports the app can read: no PDF, JPEG or PNG."; the reading screen counts "Reading report 2 of 9", and Close stops it between files. Tests: `LabSourceTests` (an oversized file refused before reading, a folder over the cap, an empty folder, cancelling between files, the count). Test: UI `LabUploadUITests.testThePlusSheetOffersFilesThenPhotosThenScan_US52_AC10` (Files above Photos, Scan after Photos where it shows, the Files line, no cloud list).
- AC11 (no cloud-folder lists, Brad 2026-10-25; replaces the 2026-10-22 "From Dropbox" list): the sheet never lists a cloud folder itself. Why: the app's Dropbox access is App folder only and its Google access is `drive.file`, so neither list could ever show a person's own folders; Brad could not see his own "Health" folder. The Files picker reaches any folder in Dropbox, Google Drive or iCloud Drive through their File Provider apps and hands the app only the one file (or folder) the person picks, with no wider grant. Removed with it, end to end: the From Dropbox and From Google Drive screens (`LabSourceViews.swift`), the engine doors `labFolderJson`, `labFolderFilesJson` and `labFile` (`ios/engine/lab-files.ts`) with their Swift doors, so the bridge id moved (D3); health-core's `dropboxListTree` went with them, and the engine's network fence no longer allows Dropbox `files/list_folder` (EngineFenceTests `testADropboxFolderListingIsRefused`). Sync is unchanged: the record file still syncs through `CloudSync`, the token store and the same App folder and `drive.file` scopes (US-25 AC11), and the hosted connector still reads lab files from Dropbox › Apps › Health Plan by Dr Brad (US-35 AC2), unchanged.
- AC12 (connecting a cloud, 2026-10-25; replaces the 2026-10-22 "From Google Drive" screen): the sheet asks for no sign-in. Connecting Dropbox or Google Drive is Sync's job (US-25 AC11), and only keeps the record there; a report in either cloud comes in through Files, signed in or not.
- AC13 (reading shown, Brad 2026-10-22): while a report is read, the sheet shows a diagram in place of a spinner: the report, "Read by AI" and the record, silver beads flowing to the reader and green ones on to the record, with the step in words and one sentence: the report goes through Dr Brad's server to Claude, is not kept, and every value is checked before it is saved (the consent screen's own facts). Still under Reduce Motion.
- AC13b (the upload explained, Brad 2026-10-22): above the sources, an animation shows what the feature does before anything is picked, as the sync diagram does for sync: a lab report and a clinic letter, a light sweeping the report, and result names (LDL, HbA1c, ApoB: names, never values) arcing into "Your record", ticking it one by one. Its words are AC13c's, written as the finished feature (Brad 2026-10-22: "word it assuming feature complete"); clinic letters land with AC13d. The drawing is capped at the xxLarge text size; the sentence grows freely. Still under Reduce Motion. While reports are read (AC13), a progress bar sits under the step: real at each report's end ("Report 2 of 3"), as the web's "Processed 2 of 3" is, and inside one report an estimate easing toward 90% of that report's share, since the server says nothing while it reads; the step names the file. The sheet is presented from My data itself, not from the section header, whose grey text, large font and icon-only labels it had inherited, and Photos is presented from the sheet's root: an inline picker row took the whole sheet down when a photo was picked (both seen in the simulator 2026-10-22). Checked by eye in the simulator, light mode, 2026-10-22; dark mode not checked.
- AC13c (wording, agreed with Brad 2026-10-22, written as the finished feature on his ruling; built 2026-10-22, with "A folder or ZIP" reading a picked folder and its folders, in name order, at most 200 files; Dropbox folders built 2026-10-23 and removed 2026-10-25 with the Dropbox list, AC11): the feature is "medical records". The button and sheet are "Add medical records", the sources' header "Where are your medical records?", and the explainer's sentence "Point the app at your medical records: a folder, a ZIP, or one PDF or photo. It reads the test results in your lab reports and clinic letters. You check each one before it's saved. Then: Claude reads them through Dr Brad's server, which keeps no copy. Your originals stay in your own cloud. (Never destroyed: Anthropic may keep it for a limited time for safety checks, as the consent screen says.) The reading screen says The server keeps no copy, no longer The report is not kept, since the original is kept in the person's own cloud (AC13d). Sources (since 2026-10-25, AC10): Files "A PDF, photo, ZIP or folder"; Photos "A photo of a paper report"; Scan "Use the camera, one page at a time". The web's sources are not changed by this.
- AC13d (clinic letters, as on the web; built 2026-10-22): a file the server reads as a letter, discharge summary or other document is filed as a document in the record, through the web's one save path, health-core's `saveDocuments` (US-14 AC5); there is no phone-only save code. The review shows the web's card: a keep tick, on unless the record already holds a live document from a file of that name (the web's `sourceFileName` dedup, said as "Already saved"); the title, editable (left empty, the model's is kept, as on the web); the date, editable, a past day or "Date unknown" (a month alone, a future day or none reads as unknown, and saves null); the classification as a read-only badge; the first 300 characters of the text. The screening-date tick the web offers for a document with `metadata.screeningType` is not on the phone (screening rules stay the web's for now). A metadata-only row holding the same bytes (a failed save, or the connector's; US-14 AC4) is read as the web's card reads it (`pendingRowsFor`): the card starts from the newest such row's title and date, an unknown date staying unknown, and its original is filed behind that row ("Save the original") even when the keep tick is off, as the web archives it. The review pins the record it opened on (`pinScreen`, as the sheets do): an erase that arrives before Save refuses the values and the document. While a save runs, Skip and Next wait. Saves run one after another in the engine, so two saves never take the same ref and overwrite each other's original. With a cloud record open, the original goes to the person's Dropbox or Google Drive first, under the web's folder (`buildDocumentRef`, by the opted-in shared adapters), then the rows are committed the way every cloud edit is: the phone's copy and its pending marker first, then `RecordSession.edit` with the erase the screen showed, refused if an erase arrived or the session closed during the upload. The phone fingerprints each original as it reads it (size and `sha256-<hex>`, the web's `sha256Blob` format, used as `contentHash`, so the same bytes are one original on both). A file picked in Files is kept as the file, not its bytes, and read again at Save under its access: a size or hash that no longer matches, or a file gone or unreadable, saves the row without the original, with the reviewed hash (US-14 AC4's metadata-only fallback), and the review says "The original changed or could not be read, so only its text was saved." A lab report's original is kept too, in the cloud only, as the web's hidden `pathology_report` row (`labArchivePayload`, shared by the web and the app), dated by the test day the review saved. With no cloud, as on the web off-cloud, a document is a text-only row (`fileRef`, `contentHash` and `mimeType` empty, the text kept), written to the phone's file only over the record the save began from, and a lab report's original is not kept. A provider that refuses the original leaves a metadata-only row with its hash, and the review says "The original file couldn't be stored; its details are saved." On Drive the originals go to the folder that holds the record (where the browser keeps its folder id and moves the record), not the first folder of that name (R4). Every stored `sourceFileName` is health-core's, one engine call per read (`fileNamesJson`): a ZIP member by `zipMemberName`, the web's rule and cap; any other file (a Files pick, a folder's `folder/sub/file`, a Dropbox file) on one line and cut to 255, as the connector stores one. A photo or a scan carries no original. Folders: a folder picked in Files is read, and since 2026-10-23 a Dropbox subfolder or a whole Dropbox folder (AC13c). Usage signal: none; the app sends no product events (D9), so filing is measured only by the web's events and by hand. Tests: `ios/engine/app-doors.test.ts` "US-52 AC13d" (the card, unknown dates, the dedup, no card for a lab report, held rows: a retry after an edited failed save, the connector's, not a lab archive; every stored file name); `ios/engine/cloud.test.ts` "documents from Add medical records" (cloud original first then the row through the session, dedup by hash, R1 two saves at once keep two refs and both originals, the lab-archive row, a refused original, a stale original, an upload behind a held row replaces it, an erase refused before any upload, R5 an erase or a close during the upload refuses the row, the phone's text-only row); `packages/health-core/src/drive-rest.test.ts` "US-52 AC13d (R4)"; iOS `CloudSyncTests.testALetterIsFiledInTheCloudWithItsOriginalAndTheWebsHash`, `testAnOriginalGoneBeforeSaveFilesOnlyTheText`, `testAnEraseAfterTheReviewOpensRefusesItsSave`, `RecordStoreTests.testALetterOnThePhoneAloneIsATextOnlyRow`, `testADocumentSaveNeverWritesOverAnEditMadeWhileItRan`, `AppChatLabTests.testALetterGetsTheWebsDocumentCard`, `testAReadFileKeepsItsOriginalBytes`, `testAZipMembersNameIsTheWebsZipMemberName`, `testAFoldersOriginalsAreStillReadableAfterTheRead` (and a changed or deleted file gives no bytes). Checked by eye in the simulator: not yet. **Which Drive folder (2026-10-23):** originals go into the folder that holds the record, found by the record's parent id, so a renamed app folder still gets them where the website reads them; the Drive root (a folder with no parent) never, nor a trashed folder or one this app may not see (404), which fall back to the app folder by name. A record with several parents takes the first that qualifies. Any other failure looking the folder up fails the save, so the next save retries rather than filing into a fallback folder (adversary and Codex R1). Tests: `drive-rest.test.ts` "a renamed app folder still holds the originals", "a failed look at the record's folder fails the save", "a record with several parents", and the root and stray-folder cases.
- AC14 (one lab-import path, 2026-10-23; Brad: "the only difference is that we want to use the user's openAI or claude or gemini etc rather than ours to do the processing. otherwise, share as much as possible and de-dup"; plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-23-mcp-dedup-plan.md`): after the file is read, the website, the iPhone app and the connector share one parse (`parseUnifiedResult`), one row shape (`BulkRow`), one value write (`bulkAppendValues` and its slot rule) and one document-row builder (`documentRow` in `document-rows.ts`, used by `saveDocuments` and the connector's commit; the lab report's archive row from `labArchiveFields` on all three). What differs stays per surface on purpose, named here so a later de-dup keeps it: who reads the file (our Claude on the website, the iPhone and the folder route; the person's own AI on `file_results`); edited values (the website's review edits a value and tags it `lab_import_edited`; the iPhone and the connector file what was read); previous-results columns (the website reads dated and undated ones, AC12 and AC14 of US-12; the iPhone files a value's own day or refuses the save; the connector's folder route drops a dated previous column until the MCP 1.0.2 review ends, the assistant route keeps its own day); same-day handling (the website shows one reading per slot and counts the loser; the connector offers both, marks the second `sameDayAs` and refuses a commit that picks both); replace rules (the website replaces when a ticked Replace meets `cell.existing`; the connector replaces a `held_different` slot only through `replace`, inside its 90-day rule, and refuses the commit when a slot moved; the iPhone does not replace yet). The six duplicate checks stay where they are, each with its reason, listed beside `saveDocuments` (`document-save.ts`): the website review's exact-name `isDocDuplicate`; the iPhone review's `alreadySaved`, the same rule; `saveDocuments`' hash rule, replacing a metadata-only row of its own kind (lab archive or shown document, US-14 AC4) behind and tombstoning it; the connector's `isAlreadyImported` (hash; else, for a hashless candidate, name and date with " (n)" stripped; else the name alone against a hashless live row whose date is unknown or equal); the connector's `folderNudge` name rule, comparing `dedupFileName` on both sides (" (n)" stripped); and the website archive step's by-hash and name sets with `pendingRowsFor`, which the iPhone's review-time held check uses too. Tests: `mcp-import-pins.test.ts` (16 connector cases, extract answer, pending JSON, receipt and rows byte for byte), `ios/engine/lab-rows-pins.test.ts` (`labRows` and its refusal words through `labImport` and `labSaveSummaryJson`), `ReviewTable.pins.test.tsx` and `UploadModal.pins.test.tsx` (the reviewed rows and the two store calls).
- Not yet: replacing a held value from the review (the web's "Replace"), chat proposing form edits, Apple's fraud-risk metric from the attestation receipt.
- Tests: ✅ `app/lib/app-attest.server.test.ts` (attestation and assertion verification against a test CA built with openssl, every refusal), `app/lib/app-routes.server.test.ts` (the gate, the key read before the body, the bypass refused in production and with NODE_ENV unset, limits incl. the per-IP failure budget, the chat pipeline called with the widget's shape and nothing stored, lab extraction reused), `ios/engine/app-doors.test.ts` (chat context, chat history through `ChatSession`, the lab review with the extractor's question, the save through `bulkAppendValues`), `ios/HealthRoadmapTests/AppChatLabTests.swift` (the same doors in JavaScriptCore, the NDJSON reader, the signed client data, PDF and ZIP reading), `ios/HealthRoadmapTests/AppServerE2ETests.swift` (opt-in: one real chat turn and one synthetic lab report against a local server, passed 2026-10-21). Owed: a real-device attestation and assertion (D8 Test vectors); the screens checked by hand (the simulator could not be driven in this session).

### US-54 · A new iPhone user reaches their plan in under a minute — **added 2026-10-22 (Brad approved the flow and the draft's recommendations; design: [ios/onboarding.md](../ios/onboarding.md))**
As a new app user, I answer four short questions, most filled in for me from Apple Health, and see my plan, without facing the full My data form.
- **Usage signal (Brad, 2026-10-22):** App Store Connect retention. The app still sends no product events (D9).
- AC1: a new user sees the welcome screen (US-25 AC10's words), then the flow once: Apple Health, sex, birth month and year, height, weight, then My plan (the questions Apple Health answered are skipped and listed on one last screen instead, AC3b). A record that already holds sex, birth year and height skips the flow (existing users and testers).
- AC2: the welcome screen also offers "I already use Health Roadmap". It runs Sync's own connect (US-25 AC11) and goes on only once the cloud record has opened; a sign-in whose record cannot be read says so and offers Try again, so the questions never start from the empty phone record (whose answers would win the merge over the website's). A record that then holds sex, birth year and height opens My plan; one that lacks any of them asks only for those, and its units are never changed.
- AC3: "Get started" shows one page of ours, "Use your Apple Health data", and no other page before Apple's sheet (Brad 2026-10-23: two pages were one too many). The page discloses what is read and written: the six things it reads (sex, birth date, height, weight, waist, blood pressure) as tiles that tick in one by one; under them one quiet line names US-56's five, read too but never in the record ("It also shows your heart rate, sleep, VO2 max and steps here, never in your record.", adversary R5, 2026-10-26; was "...here, never kept." until US-56 AC2 changed, Brad 2026-10-27); and a line that starts "So you type less." and says that the six (sex, birth date, height, weight, waist, blood pressure) go only into the record, on this iPhone or in the person's own cloud (named since 2026-10-27, adversary R2: US-56's five are now kept on the phone too, so "what it reads" was no longer true), and that values added here are saved back to Apple Health (it informs rather than urges, for App Review 5.1.1). Directly above "Connect Apple Health", the last thing read before the tap, a small callout with a tap symbol, in the app's accent green (Brad 2026-10-25: red read as something wrong), says what Apple asks next: "Next, Apple asks for access. Turn everything on, then tap **Allow**." (Brad 2026-10-23; words shortened 2026-10-25; made version-neutral 2026-10-26, because iOS 27's sheet says "Select All" where older ones say "Turn On All"). The page has no switch of its own: Apple's sheet is the system's, so no app can turn its switches on or press its buttons, and a toggle of ours would be a false control. VoiceOver reads the six as one list. Under Reduce Motion the tiles show ticked and still. "Connect Apple Health" runs the app's Apple Health connect (US-25 AC15), whose sheet also asks to read biological sex and date of birth. **One step (Brad 2026-10-26: "just ask for everything... just do it in one step"):** that one sheet also asks to read US-56's five types (heart rate, resting heart rate, sleep, VO2 max, steps), so the person answers Apple once. Every Health ask in the app is that one request (`HealthKitClient.requested`: the record's types to read and write, sex and date of birth, and `LiveHealthKitStore.readTypes`), so the sets cannot drift; on iOS 27 the sheet's "Select All" (older iOS: "Turn On All") is followed by its own "Continue", a choice of how much history to share, then "Allow". What Health gives is then handled by AC3b: sex (female or male) and birth month and year are saved at once (the day is never stored), height and weight come in with the connect, and those questions are skipped and listed on the summary. Sex "other" or "not set" gives nothing, so the question is asked. "Not now" goes on with nothing filled in; both buttons wait while the connect runs (adversary R8).
- AC3b (Health's answers are not asked again, **Brad 2026-10-26**: "if we are pulling that from Apple Health, we don't need to ask those questions. We should just automatically assume that the data is correct"; guards (a) and (b) by the orchestrator, the summary confirmed by Brad the same day: "sure"): after "Connect Apple Health", every question whose value Apple Health supplied is skipped, and only the rest are asked. Supplied means the record lacked it before the connect and has it from Health after: sex (female or male) and birth month and year from Health's characteristics, saved at once in one `profile` edit (`OnboardingSteps.healthEdit`, review E3; refused, both are asked); height and weight as the connect imported them (US-25 AC15, source Apple Health). Supplied is worked out from the record each time (`OnboardingSteps.supplied`): a step counts only while the record holds its answer. **(a)** A weight whose newest day is more than a year before today is not supplied: the weight question is asked, prefilled with it and labelled "From Apple Health" (`OnboardingSteps.supplied`). Continue on it untouched confirms it is current and saves it as today's weight (orchestrator 2026-10-26) as an Apple Health row (`source: apple_health`, `OnboardingSteps.confirmedWeight`) carrying the row's own SI value, never the rounded display (`OnboardingSteps.kilograms`), so it is never written back to Health; a weight typed over it is saved as usual. Once saved it is today's, so it counts as supplied: Back from the list skips it, and Continue never asks "Replace it?" again (adversary R1, Codex R2). **(b)** When anything was supplied, one last screen, "From Apple Health", lists each supplied answer on its own line ("Female", "Born March 1985", "170 cm", "68 kg", in the record's units) with an **Edit** button that opens that question, filled in, and returns to the list once answered; one **Continue** opens My plan. Back from the list, or from a question, skips the supplied steps. At accessibility text sizes each line stacks its answer over Edit, and VoiceOver reads each line by name, with height in words ("Height, 5 feet 10 inches"). So a person whose Health holds everything, with a weight from the last year, sees: Apple's sheet, the list, Continue. With nothing supplied there is no list. A run quit part way keeps both guards (adversary R2): which steps came from Health is kept as a setting by name only, never a value (`onboardingFromHealth`, cleared when the flow starts at Apple Health or finishes), supplied is worked out again from the record, and the run resumes at the first answer the record lacks, at a stale weight, or at the list. Tests: `OnboardingStepsTests` `testHealthsAnswersAreNotAskedAgain_AC3b`, `testAWeightOlderThanAYearIsAskedAgain_AC3b`, `testTheSummaryLinesSayWhatHealthGave_AC3b`, `testBackSkipsWhatHealthSupplied_AC3b`, `testBackToAConfirmedStaleWeightDoesNotLoop_AC3b`, `testARelaunchKeepsBothGuards_AC3b`, `testHealthsSexAndBirthAreOneEdit_AC3b`, `testTheSummaryHeightIsSpokenInWords_AC3b`; `AppleHealthSyncTests.testAConfirmedStaleHealthWeightIsNeverWrittenBack_US54_AC3b` and `testAConfirmedStaleWeightKeepsItsKilograms_US54_AC3b` (the row's SI value, 72.57 kg on a record shown in pounds); UI `OnboardingUITests.testAllowShowsOneSheetAskingForEverything_AC3_US56_AC4` (also checks the five-readings line). Checked by hand in the simulator with Health holding sex, date of birth, height and weight: the sheet, then the list, Edit and back, Continue to My plan.
- AC4: each question is one screen with a progress bar and Back. Every question must be answered (Brad 2026-10-23: weight is required, with no Skip). Sex has no Continue: tapping Female or Male saves it and moves on, with the step's short haptic; a sex from Apple Health is not asked (AC3b); opened from the summary's Edit, it shows selected and still takes that one tap. Birth month and year are two wheels with Continue: a wheel's starting value is not an answer until the person moves it, or it came from the record or Apple Health; one line says why age matters (which checks are due, like bowel and breast cancer screening and bone density scans) and that the day is never asked. Height and weight are typed into a large number box, focused when the screen opens, with Continue enabled once the box holds a number: centimetres or feet and inches (two boxes; empty inches are 0) for height, kilograms or pounds for weight. A value from Apple Health, opened from the summary or a stale weight, is labelled "From Apple Health".
- AC5: each answer (a sex tap, or Continue) writes through the engine's own edits (`profile` for sex, birth year and month and height; `feetInches` for a US height; `add` for weight, today), so a refused value shows the engine's words and nothing is written. Each answer is checked against the record its screen showed (US-25 AC11g); after a refusal the screen takes the current record. A weight equal to the record's latest writes nothing; a different weight on a day that already has one asks "Replace it?" first, and replacing is a FHIR correction.
- AC6: a new record takes its units from the phone's region (US: feet, inches and pounds), written as the record's unit choice; a record with values keeps its own. The record's units change only in My data › About you › Units. Beside the height and weight boxes a switch (cm or ft in, kg or lb) starts from the record's units (weight's own, US-25 AC17e) and is for entry only (review 2026-10-23: adversary R1, R2, Codex): it never writes the record's units. A box left alone shows the record's value again in the new units; a typed one is converted, by health-core's factors through the engine (`convertJson`). On Continue a typed value is converted once to the units the engine's edit reads and saved as before (feet and inches, a height, a weight added or corrected). A box filled from the record and not typed in saves nothing, in any unit: 70 kg shown as 154 lb and back adds no weight row.
- AC7: quitting part way keeps what was saved; the next launch resumes at the first unanswered question, weight included. Finishing opens My plan and never shows the flow again, until the record is erased: on the phone that erased it, once the erase's words are dismissed; on any other phone, when the higher erase count arrives through the cloud and the answers are gone. The questions start again on the empty record, not the welcome screen; the record keeps its units, and a connected cloud stays connected (Brad 2026-10-22).
- AC8: VoiceOver reads every screen; at accessibility text sizes Continue stays reachable.
- Tests: ✅ `OnboardingStepsTests.swift` (26 since AC3b, 2026-10-26; the first 14: which steps a record needs, start and resume, the full and only-missing orders, region units for a new record only, Health's sex and birth month and year with no day kept; AC6 through the real engine: a prefilled 70 or 70.5 kg switched to lb and back saves nothing, a weight typed in lb and a height in cm or ft in saved as the right value in the edit's units, a height switch leaving the weight alone); `ios/engine/convert.test.ts` (6: the `convertJson` door, and lb and ft in typed on a metric record, cm on a US record, saved right with the record's units unchanged); ✅ `HealthRoadmapUITests/OnboardingUITests.swift` (13 since US-57 and the one-step sheet; US-54's 7, simulator, each on a fresh install, run one at a time by `ios/scripts/ui-test.sh` (passed 2026-10-23): welcome to My plan with sex moving on at a tap, the wheel and Continue rules, focused height and weight boxes, no weight Skip, no return after finishing; quitting at weight resumes there with Continue still waiting; the unit switches are for entry only: a typed height converts, weight still opens in the record's units, a weight typed in the other unit is saved as the right weight and My data's Units are unchanged (AC6); every step reachable at the largest accessibility text size, the keyboard up, the size checked as applied (AC8); "Connect Apple Health" shows one Apple Health sheet asking to read everything, the record's types and US-56's five (AC3, 2026-10-26; it reads Apple's own `UIA.Health.*` ids, so a failure after an iOS update may be Apple's change); a plan edit on My data shows on return (US-25 AC6); "Delete all my data" brings the questions back and keeps the record's units (AC7)). `OnboardingStepsTests` also holds the erase-elsewhere rule; that path is not run on a second device. ✅ On Brad's iPhone 15 Pro Max (iOS 27.0.1, through iPhone Mirroring, 2026-10-22): "Allow" gave Apple's sheet (all topics, then iOS 27's new "how much history" step), and sex, birth month and year, height and weight each came preselected and labelled "From Apple Health"; Continue led to My plan, and My data showed the imported weight history and blood pressure. ### US-55 · Resting heart rate, VO2 max, steps and sleep come in from Apple Health — **replaced by US-56 (Brad 2026-10-23); was a draft of 2026-10-22, kept as history**
As an iPhone user whose watch already tracks my fitness, I see my resting heart rate, VO2 max, daily steps and sleep in my record and on the website, without typing them.
- **Usage signal:** App Store Connect retention (the app sends no product events, D9).
- AC1: Apple Health connect asks to read the four (resting heart rate, VO2 max, step count, sleep analysis). Turning them off leaves everything else working.
- AC2: each lands as its own metric in the shared record (`roadmap-file.ts` schema, the silent-data-loss checklist in CLAUDE.md), so the website shows and keeps it, and merge, export and erase treat it like weight.
- AC3: only finished days come in (yesterday and earlier), so a stored value never needs correcting as the day goes on; each day's value carries a stable `externalId` from its source and day, so a re-import adds nothing.
- AC4 (Brad 2026-10-22): one value per day for all four: steps the day's total, sleep the night's time asleep (dated the morning it ends), resting heart rate and VO2 max the day's value. Daily, because the charts are the point and Apple Health charts by day; the record's size cost is bounded by the engine reading the record once per change (ios/architecture.md D2).
- AC5: My data and the website show the four under a new "Fitness" group with Apple Health's colours (heart red, activity orange, sleep teal); each opens the metric page with its chart.
- AC6 (Brad 2026-10-22: "my algorithm doesn't factor in vo2max"): display only. No plan suggestion reads the four; the algorithm's general sleep card (7-9 hours, Cappuccio 2010) is unchanged and reads no one's sleep. A rule that uses them later is a clinical change under the three-file sync.
- Tests: none yet.
- **Replaced 2026-10-23 by US-56** (Brad: "sure"): the metrics are read live from Apple Health and never stored. Not to be built.

### US-56 · Heart rate, sleep, VO2 max and steps from Apple Health, shown in the app and never in the record — **approved 2026-10-23 (Brad: replaces US-55; every question below answered the same day); built 2026-10-25 (phases 1 and 2) on My data, review fixes the same day; AC8's bands built 2026-10-26; the cards' last readings kept on the phone (AC2, AC15) 2026-10-27, not yet reviewed or committed; the real-iPhone comparison waits**
As an iPhone user whose watch already tracks my heart, fitness and sleep, I see those numbers in Health Roadmap beside my vitals, so I don't have to open Apple Health to look.

Brad's ask (2026-10-23): "it would be great to have metrics like HR, VO2max, etc in our app. not necessarily to change the health plan. more so that users can view these metrics and not have to go into apple health."

**Why this replaces US-55 (Brad 2026-10-23: "sure").** US-55 stored the metrics in the record so the website could show them. That makes it a record change: a schema key per metric, the silent-data-loss checklist, merge, export and erase all touched, a daily row per metric for life, and the adversary plus Codex round for merge-class work. Reading live from Apple Health needs none of that, and Brad's ask is about viewing on the phone. What it costs is stated in AC3.

- **Usage signal (decided, Brad 2026-10-23: "do it"):** Clarity, masked as every screen is (D9). One new fixed screen name, "Apple Health metric", when a page from AC7 opens; the Turn On and Reconnect row's taps show in Clarity's masked tap data on My data. The weekly count of sessions reaching each is the signal; no value and no metric name is sent. The alternative, a `product_events` event, needs a D9 amendment and a new app-to-server path behind App Attest (D8), and would count no better: Clarity already sees the screens.
- AC1 (display only): these metrics never change the plan. They are not in `health-roadmap.json`, so no suggestion, screening, chat summary, export or merge can see them. The engine never reads them. AC8's bands come out of the engine as a table row; Swift applies them to the value at display time, and nothing it returns is stored. A rule that changes the plan from one of them later is a clinical change under the three-file sync and a record change under the silent-data-loss checklist; this story allows neither.
- AC2 (read live, the cards' last readings kept on the phone; **changed by Brad 2026-10-27, option A**): each time a card or a metric page shows, the app asks HealthKit for what it draws. It never writes a record row or a UserDefaults value. **Amended 2026-10-27 (Brad: "I'd prefer us to show everything, and just update the numbers as they come in. I don't want us to wait for anything."):** on a cold start My data drew the record, then 0.1 to 0.2 s later the cards arrived under blood pressure and pushed the blood tests down. So what the cards draw (`[LiveMetric: LiveCard]`: each card's latest value and date, the values behind its trend line, which are the past month's daily values or the last seven readings when there are fewer (AC14), the in-bed flag, and a version; nothing identifying; adversary R1) are kept in one file on this iPhone only, `Application Support/Apple Health/last-readings.json`, apart from the record's folder so no sync, export, chat summary, MCP, website or server reaches it. Its folder is left out of iCloud and computer backups (`isExcludedFromBackup`); the file is written atomically with `.completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication`, so a launch after the first unlock reads it. It is read once, when `LiveHealth` is made; a missing, damaged or other-version file is no file. A read that changes the cards replaces it; a read with no cards deletes it, so access turned off in Settings or an emptied Health clears it; a locked-phone or cancelled read changes nothing; access reset (Apple's sheet due again) deletes it; "Delete all my data" deletes it and empties the cards, and a read already under way when it runs keeps nothing (Codex R1, adversary R4). A page's longer history and its hourly and nightly detail are read fresh and never kept. Was (2026-10-23): "keeps nothing: no row, no cache file, no UserDefaults value". HealthKit's statistics queries do the daily maths: steps summed; heart rate as the day's lowest to highest; resting heart rate and VO2 max as the day's value; sleep as the night, dated the morning it ends. Today shows as it stands, partial, as Apple Health shows it. A card starts from the metric's newest reading however old, then reads the 30 days ending on it (sleep too, since 2026-10-26) for its trend (AC14), so a VO2 max from six weeks ago or a night from three weeks ago still has its card (Codex R2, 2026-10-25). **A page always shows its card's reading (Codex R2, adversary R7, 2026-10-25):** it reads 400 days (sleep: 200) or back to the reading when that is older, and opens with the reading in view; D scrolls across the last week, or back to the reading's day, and reads the hours of the day in view as the person moves between days (a 400-day hourly scroll took Swift Charts seconds to draw); the 400 days are read only once the range leaves D. A page with nothing to draw says "No VO2 max data in Apple Health for this time.", with the metric's own name. **An open page reads again** when the app becomes active, on unlock, at midnight and on a time zone change (Codex R1, N5); a D page on the day that was today moves to the new today. A read cancelled mid-flight is never kept as read and empty (N1). After Apple's sheet the app always reads again (N2); a read that finds the phone locked keeps what the page shows. Triggers within about 2 s of a running read are that read. Days, nights and labels use one calendar that follows the phone's time zone (`Calendar.autoupdatingCurrent`), given to both the reads and HealthKit's day anchor, so travel never mislabels a day (adversary R2). The app writes none of these types to Health.
- AC3 (what read-live costs): the website, the CLI, the MCP and the chatbot never see these metrics. They do not sync through Dropbox or Google Drive; on another iPhone signed in to the same Apple account, Health's own iCloud sync brings them, so the app shows them there too. A value deleted in Apple Health is gone from the app. The app shows nothing while Health has nothing (a new phone before Health restores). "Delete all my data" deletes the kept file (AC2) but never the readings in Apple Health: they are Apple Health's, not ours (adversary R5, 2026-10-27).
- AC4 (when access is asked; **changed by Brad 2026-10-26** to one step: "when users onboard and when they first connect to Apple Health, that's when we should just ask for everything"; it replaces his 2026-10-23 "agreed" to asking later, in context): the five types (heart rate, resting heart rate, sleep analysis, VO2 max, step count) are asked for in the same single request as US-54 AC3's types, by onboarding's "Connect Apple Health" and by My data's Apple Health row, the one way in after "Not now" (2026-10-26). HealthKit shows only the types not yet asked about, so a person who connected before 2026-10-26 sees just the five, once. The app uses `getRequestStatusForAuthorization` for the five to know whether the sheet would still show: if it would, Vitals shows AC5's row; if not, it shows the cards. A status check that fails keeps the answer it had, so the row never flashes over the cards (adversary R4); with no answer yet, neither shows. iOS never says whether a read was refused, so a metric with no data and a refused metric look the same; a footer says where to change access (Settings › Apps › Health › Data Access & Devices › Health Roadmap, the iOS 27 path, checked on the simulator 2026-10-25).
- AC5 (no access card, **Brad 2026-10-26**): the "Show from Apple Health" card and its separate five-type request are gone. After onboarding's "Connect Apple Health" the cards just appear when Health has readings. A person who skipped Apple Health connects from My data's Apple Health row, the one way in (review A2/A3); Vitals shows nothing for them. Only a person who connected Apple Health before 2026-10-26 (and whose connect has not failed), and so was never asked for the five, sees AC5b's calm row in Vitals with a **Turn On** button instead of Reconnect, with the same words. Turn On and My data's Apple Health row both run `AppleHealthSync.connect()`, which holds the app's `LiveHealth`: the full request (iOS shows only the types not yet asked), then the cards read as soon as the sheet is answered, with the record import running beside them, not before them (review E1). Turn On acts on the known answer; only Reconnect checks the status afresh, for the Settings fallback (`LiveReconnectRow.action`, review E2). It is a row in Vitals, never a pop-up or a badge, and it asks nothing until tapped. Tests: `LiveHealthTests` `testTurnOnShowsOnlyOnceConnectedUntilTheSheetIsDone_AC4_AC5`, `testConnectReadsTheCards_AC4` (the cards are read while the import is still held),  `testOneRequestAsksForEverything_US54_AC3_AC4`, `testTheRecordsTypesAndTheLiveTypesNeverOverlap_AC1_AC10`, and the advisory source scan `testOnlyHealthKitClientAsksForAccess_AC4` (the guarantee is that `LiveHealthStore` has no request); UI `OnboardingUITests.testAfterNotNowMyDataConnectAsksForEverythingInOneSheet_US56_AC4_AC5`.
- AC5b (after "Don't Allow", **Brad 2026-10-25**: "we need a way for users to reconnect"): once Apple's sheet is answered and nothing comes back, whether the person declined or Health holds none (iOS cannot tell them apart), Vitals shows one calm row in normal text, never an error or greyed line: "Heart rate, sleep, VO2 max and steps can show here from Apple Health.", a **Reconnect** button, and under it the path to turn the readings on (AC4's footer line). VoiceOver reads the words and the path as one element, then the button. Reconnect shows Apple's sheet again while iOS would still show it; once answered, iOS never shows it again, so Reconnect opens Settings (`UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`; on the iOS 27 simulator it opened at the top of Settings, and the app's own page there has no Health row, checked 2026-10-25), so the line names the path from the top of Settings. Back in the app, it reads again (`wake`), and the cards appear if data now comes back. Tests: `LiveHealthTests.testWhatEachPlaceShows_AC5b` (Turn On row, cards, Reconnect, nothing while unknown or unread, each place) and `testReconnectAsksAgainOrOpensSettings_AC5b`.
- AC6 (where they appear; **decided, Brad 2026-10-23**): heart rate, resting heart rate and sleep go in Vitals, under blood pressure. VO2 max and steps go under a new heading, "Fitness", below Vitals. Each is a card in the vitals card style (`MyDataView.swift` `vitals`, `ValueRow` with `card:`): name (no symbol, as the vitals cards since US-25 AC17; orchestrator 2026-10-25), the day or time of the latest value as Apple Health writes it ("Today", or the time for today's heart rate; "Yesterday"; then the short date; the vitals cards match, Brad 2026-10-25), the value large, the recent trend beside it, Apple Health's colours (heart red, sleep teal, activity orange; `softInDark` in dark mode). A metric with no data is left out, not shown empty; Fitness with neither is not shown. A footer under each says "From Apple Health. Kept on this iPhone only, so the cards show at once: not in your record or on the website." (AC2, Brad 2026-10-27; was "Shown here only: not saved to your record or the website.") Vitals' unit switch does not change them: each has one unit (bpm, mL/kg/min, steps, hours and minutes).
- AC7 (a metric's page): a tap opens the same pushed page as a vital (US-25 AC17, D11): range picker (D, W, M, 6M, Y, offered by the values' span), headline for the selected range, chart, scrub callout. It is read-only: no "+", no Show All Data list, no correction, no Unit menu. A line under the chart says "From Apple Health". Heart rate draws each day as a low-to-high bar, as Apple Health does; steps as daily bars; resting heart rate and VO2 max as daily points. The D range shows the day by hour (steps by hour, heart rate's samples). No target band or reference range on any of them (D11 drew none for the same reason), save AC8's VO2 max rating.
- AC8 (VO2 max fitness bands; **decided, Brad 2026-10-26: "do it. we want the bands"**, replacing the 2026-10-23 plan to copy Apple's table, which Apple does not publish): the VO2 max page shades four bands behind its chart, Low, Below Average, Above Average and High, for the person's age and sex, with a legend under the chart naming each band and its range in mL/kg/min. The bands are FRIEND percentiles (Kaminsky 2022, Mayo Clin Proc 97(2):285-293, doi:10.1016/j.mayocp.2021.08.020, Table 3, treadmill, RER ≥ 1.0): Low is below the 20th percentile from 20 to 59. **From 60, Low uses Apple's Low Cardio Fitness alert line (below 18 mL/kg/min for men, 15 for women; Brad 2026-10-27: "we want to do the same as Apple Health"):** the fixed lines of Apple's white paper (May 2021, "Using Apple Watch to Estimate Cardio Fitness with VO2 max"), which Apple ties to the fitness that independent living may need, so at older ages Low is a functional line rather than a percentile. Apple defines them only as its notification threshold. Apple's 20 to 59 line is the lowest fifth of FRIEND 2015, which publishes no 20th percentile, so there the bands keep FRIEND 2022's. Below Average runs from the Low line to below the 50th percentile, Above Average from the 50th to below the 80th, High the 80th and above. A band with no room is left out of the legend and the shading: for men 80 to 89, Apple's 18 is above FRIEND's median of 17.6, so below 18 is Low, 18 to below 21.4 Above Average, 21.4 and up High, and there is no Below Average. Each band includes its lower bound. A value is placed as it is shown, rounded to one decimal, so a reading never shows in one band and reads as another. Ages 20 to 89 by the table's decades; under 20, at 90 or over, or with no sex or birth year in the record, no band shows anywhere. Age is the record's (health-core's `calculateAge` rule: the birth month, else January), the person's age today, also for older readings. The words never claim the bands are Apple's, except the Low line from 60, which the legend's footer names as Apple's Low Cardio Fitness alert line. Under the legend, one line gives the source and one says Apple Watch estimates VO2 max while FRIEND's values come from lab treadmill tests. The VO2 max card adds the newest reading's band after the value ("Above Average"), in secondary text as the card's unit is. VoiceOver: the card's sentence ends with the band; each legend row reads as one element ("Above Average, 35.3 to 45.1 millilitres per kilogram per minute"); the audio graph's summary names the bands. A thin rule marks each cut-point on the chart, so the bands stay visible in dark mode. The legend's band labels are text in the primary colour, never colour alone, so they read in light and dark mode and at accessibility sizes. Display only (AC1): no suggestion, no plan change, nothing stored. **One table, served by the engine:** health-core's `vo2max-bands.ts` is the table the clinical files and tests pin; the engine serves the person's row on My data (`vo2Bands`, from the record's sex and `calculateAge`, as it serves the guides), and Swift only applies the cut-points to a value (`Vo2MaxBands.swift`). The served row's `p20` is the Low line: FRIEND's P20, or from 60 Apple's Low Cardio Fitness alert line (`APPLE_LOW_FROM_60` in `vo2max-bands.ts`), From 60 that line can exceed P50 (men 80 to 89), which an app before build 3 cannot draw, so the row and that meaning are in the bridge contract (`screenJson`'s returns): the bridge id moved to `2d467ff50c66c42d` (D3), an engine that serves the 60+ line reaches only build 3 or later, and an older build keeps its bundled engine (adversary R1, Codex R1). Later fixes to the row ship over the air within that bridge. No VO2 max enters the engine (AC1). A My data field; an older engine sends none, a malformed one reads as none, and then no bands show. The value is rounded once to one decimal (to even at a tie) and that one number is shown, plotted and placed. Three-file sync: the table and Apple's floors in `health_roadmap_algorithm.md`, its reason and references (FRIEND 2022 and Apple's white paper) in `evidence.ts` (`STAT_CARD_EVIDENCE['vo2max']`), and the sentence with its citations in `roadmap_text.html`.
- AC9 (sleep; **decided, Brad 2026-10-23: Apple's stages, "build it how Apple Health displays it"**): the sleep card shows the night's time asleep, as Apple Health's does. Its page is built the way Apple Health's Sleep page displays sleep, not a variant of the AC7 page: the night's stages (Awake, REM, Core, Deep) drawn over the night's clock times in Apple's stage colours, each stage's time beside it, and over longer ranges each night's time asleep with the stages' averages, in Apple's layout, ranges and wording. A source that records only "Asleep" or "In Bed" (an older watch, a third-party app) shows as Apple Health shows it, without stages; a night with only "In Bed" shows its time in bed, labelled "in bed" on the card and "Time in Bed" on the page, in every range (Codex R3, 2026-10-25). A night runs 6 pm to 6 pm by the local clock (a sample starting at 18:00 or later belongs to the next morning; the hour, not six hours of seconds, so a clock change at midnight, as in Santiago, moves nothing; adversary R5) and is dated the morning it ends. A night dated after today (a nap after 6 pm) is left out of the card and of the night D opens on; D's "Night after" can still reach it (adversary R3). When several apps record one night, the one with the most staged time draws it (Apple's source order is not readable). Both rules are to be checked against Apple Health on Brad's iPhone (orchestrator 2026-10-25). Every chart is matched against Apple Health's on Brad's iPhone during the build, side by side for the same nights.
- AC10 (only what is shown is read): the app asks to read exactly the five types it draws, and draws every type it asks for. No HRV (Brad 2026-10-23: "I don't want HRV"). The read purpose string (`NSHealthShareUsageDescription`; iOS allows one for all types, not one per type) names them and says they stay out of the record: "…and your heart rate, resting heart rate, sleep, VO2 max and steps, which it shows you and keeps only on this iPhone, never in your record." (AC2, Brad 2026-10-27; was "which it shows you and does not keep."). What it keeps is what the cards draw, each card's latest reading and its trend line's values (AC2). Its present words, "They go only into your record", stay true only of the six.
- AC11 (App Review): guideline 5.1.1 (collect only what the feature needs, say why) and 5.1.3 (Health data not used for advertising or data mining, not shared with third parties, not stored in iCloud by us) both hold: nothing leaves the phone, Clarity is masked (D9), and no value reaches any log. Guideline 2.5.1 asks a HealthKit app to show the integration plainly in its UI and its description: onboarding's Apple Health page, the Turn On and Reconnect row and the footers name Apple Health, and the App Store text and review notes say the app shows heart rate, sleep, VO2 max and steps from Apple Health. App Store Connect's privacy answers: these types are read on the device and never collected (Apple counts data as collected only when it leaves the device); the answer for the six is unchanged.
- AC12: VoiceOver reads each card as one sentence (name, value, day) and each chart through its audio graph (`accessibilityChartDescriptor`, as `MetricChart` does). The audio graph describes the bars or nights in view, not everything read (adversary R8). Sleep's audio graphs say "Time in bed" when the nights in view, or D's night, hold only time in bed (Codex R3). At accessibility text sizes a card stacks name over day (as the vitals do, review N7).
- AC13: with Health unavailable (an iPad without Health) neither the cards nor the Turn On row show. A locked phone's read error is not an error to the person: the cards and an open page keep what the last read drew while the app stays open, and read again on unlock.
- AC14 (recent data only in a card's trend, Brad 2026-10-25, as Apple Health; the record cards match, US-25 AC17f): a card's trend line shows the last 30 days' readings, today and the 29 days before it: a day's value (sleep: a night's time). With fewer than two readings in those 30 days it shows the last seven instead, however old, so a sparse VO2 max still draws a line. The card reads the 30 days ending on its newest reading (AC2). Only when those hold fewer than two readings in the last 30 days and fewer than seven in all does it read further back: a day metric 400 days before that window, sleep the 200 nights before today that a sleep page reads, or back to the first read's start when that is older (adversary R2, Codex R1, 2026-10-26). A read-back that fails or finds nothing more keeps the card the first read drew, heart rate's trend included (Codex R2). `LiveMaths.trend` and `LiveMaths.readsBack`, tested in `LiveMathsTests` `testACardsTrendIsTheLast30DaysOrTheLastSeven_AC14` and `LiveHealthTests` `testASparseMetricsTrendReadsBackForSevenReadings_AC14`, `testACardReadsBackOnlyWhenItsTrendNeedsOlderReadings_AC14`, `testAFailedReadBackKeepsTheFirstCard_AC14`.
- AC15 (no jump at launch; **Brad 2026-10-27, option A**): on a cold start the cards draw from the kept readings (AC2) in My data's first frame, so nothing is inserted under blood pressure a moment later; the first read then updates the numbers in place. While kept cards show and the first read has not landed, the place shows the cards, never the Turn On or Reconnect row. "Today", "Yesterday", times and VO2 max's band are worked out from the card's date and value when drawn, so a card kept for days says its date, not "Today". `LiveHealthTests.testTheKeptCardsDrawBeforeAnyRead_AC15`.
- **Gate check (Lane B):** AC8 is clinical (a threshold table shown to the person): three-file sync, adversary plus Codex. The rest is not clinical, not merge/FHIR (no record change), not a server change (no endpoint). It is a privacy surface, so the same adversary checks AC2, AC3, AC10 and AC11's claims.

### US-57 · After onboarding, a short tour shows a new iPhone user how to read My plan — **approved by Brad 2026-10-25 (tour, words, tile lines, usage signal, save rule); built 2026-10-25**
As a new app user who has just answered the four questions and landed on My plan, I see three one-line tips that show me what the tiles mean, why each step is there and how to make the plan more personal, and I can skip them. Brad: "This tour mustn't go on and on."

Continues US-54: onboarding ends on My plan, and the tour starts there. Design notes: [ios/onboarding.md](../ios/onboarding.md) § The tour.

- **Usage signal (decided, Brad 2026-10-25):** Clarity custom events (`ClaritySDK.sendCustomEvent`), sent only from `Analytics.swift`, from one enum (`Analytics.Event`), with no value and no tile name: "Tour started", "Tour tip closed 1/2/3", "Tour skipped 1/2/3", "Tile explainer opened", "Cloud prompt shown", "Cloud prompt back up", "Cloud prompt not now". D9 allows exactly these words. The weekly counts give how far people get through the tour and how many back up.
- AC1 (when): the tour starts once, when onboarding finishes and My plan opens (`RootView.finishOnboarding`, which "I already use Health Roadmap" with a full record also reaches). A phone that finished onboarding before this build never sees it. It uses Apple's TipKit; a tip closed, acted on or skipped never shows again, across launches.
- AC2 (order): exactly three tips, one at a time: the snapshot, the first Foundation step, then Blood tests on My data. Every tip ends on one row: "Skip tour" on the left, its counter ("1/3", "2/3", "3/3"; VoiceOver reads "Tip 1 of 3") centred, and "Next" on the right; tip 3's reads "Done" and ends the tour (Brad 2026-10-25). Tip 2's "Next" switches to My data, which scrolls Blood tests into view, and tip 3 shows there. No x: Next and a tap outside do its work (Brad 2026-10-25). The next tip shows only once the one before is closed: its Next, its action, or a tap outside it, which only dismisses a popover and so counts as closed (review R2a, decided 2026-10-25: Brad's "mustn't go on and on"; leaving the tab while a tip is up does the same). When tip 2 becomes due, My plan scrolls its card into view; when tip 3 is due and My data shows, it scrolls Blood tests into view. A tap outside tip 2 moves the tour on but stays on My plan: tip 3 then shows when the person next opens My data. A screen that cannot draw a tip's anchor (no tiles, no Foundation card) passes that step as closed, with its "Tour tip closed n" event, so the tour never stalls (review R4). The person's third own save ends a tour still running (review R2b), and a tour that ends offers the cloud prompt (AC8). Known trade-off (re-check N1, 2026-10-25): a tip also counts as closed whenever its popover leaves for any other reason (its anchor scrolled away or recycled, the plan reordered under it, a reminder switching tabs, a cover), so Clarity's "Tour tip closed n" reads as "passed n", not "read n"; kept because the tour must never stall.
- AC3 (skip): every tip carries "Skip tour", as plain text, not a filled button. It ends the tour: no later tip shows.
- AC4 (tip 1): one tip for the whole row of summary tiles, never one per tile (Brad 2026-10-25): "A snapshot of your health. Tap any tile to learn more." Then "Skip tour", "1/3", "Next".
- AC5 (tile explainers, for good): every tile is a button, before and after the tour. A tap opens a sheet with the tile's name, its "what it is" line and, under "The evidence", the existing why (guideline tags, reason, references). The ten lines (Brad approved them as drafted, 2026-10-25) live in health-core as `STAT_TILE_ABOUT` beside `statTiles`, which sets each tile's `about`; the engine serves them through `screenJson`. The web does not show them yet. A known minor's tile is a button too and shows the line alone, with no evidence (US-07 AC6 holds). The lines name no threshold and grade nothing. An eleventh line (Brad, 2026-10-25), `STAT_TILE_ABOUT_MINOR_BMI`, replaces the BMI line for a known minor only: "Body mass index: your weight in kilograms divided by your height in metres, squared. For under-18s the plan doesn't grade BMI, because children are compared with growth charts instead." Adults keep the waist line. Tests: `stat-tiles.test.ts` and `ios/engine/stat-tiles.test.ts`.
- AC6 (tip 2): anchored to the first card of the Foundation section: "Start here. Each step comes with the reason and the evidence." Then "Skip tour", "2/3", "Next"; Next opens tip 3 on My data (AC2).
- AC7 (tip 3): anchored to My data's Blood tests header: "The more data you add, the more personal your plan. You can upload lab reports to fill these in for you." (Brad 2026-10-25). ### US-58 · A metric page and each medicine question explain the measure, as Apple Health does — **added 2026-10-26 from Brad's six decisions on the draft (docs/drafts/metric-guides.md, 2026-10-25); built 2026-10-26, not yet reviewed or committed**

### US-27 · YouTube bot posting caps hold when the data layer fails — **added by sentry-fix 2026-08-27 (spec hole found via Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-64/65/66)**
As Brad, on whose channel the bot posts publicly, its safety caps (50 replies/day, 10/video lifetime) bind under ALL conditions — including when the Supabase reads behind them fail.
- AC1: A failed cap read (today's post count, per-video totals) fails distinguishably (throws, same convention as the tick's other pre-posting reads) — never a value indistinguishable from zero posts.
- AC2: With either cap unknown, the tick posts nothing (top-level or follow-up), logs the skip, and retries next tick.
- Tests: 🟡 `youtube-bot.server.test.ts` pins AC1 at the `readPostingCaps` gate (Supabase error on either read → rejects; success → both caps). AC2's tick half (catch → post nothing → log → retry) is review-verified only — `tick()` isn't exported; extracting it is a future testability task.
- Origin: from 2026-08-26 an intermittent Supabase-side PGRST303 ("JWT issued at future") made ~⅓ of cap reads error; each affected tick silently re-armed the full daily budget (error was mapped to count 0 / empty map).
- Status: shipped by sentry-fix's Tier 3 PR #30, deployed 2026-08-27; the PGRST303 class (JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-64/65/67) has been quiet since 2026-08-28T16:11Z (product-health W35, W36). Brad closed decision issue #32 as leave-to-Supabase.

### US-28 · Daily crons survive transient lock errors — **added by sentry-fix 2026-08-28 (spec hole found via Sentry JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-66/68)**
As Brad, whose server runs five daily jobs behind a cross-machine day lock (reminder emails, trending ×2, the YouTube ops summary, the chat-text purge), a transient database error while acquiring the lock delays that machine's attempt to the next hourly tick — it never silently cancels the job for the day.
- AC1: A transient DB error in `tryAcquireCronLock` (lock UPDATE or verify SELECT) fails distinguishably (throws, US-27 AC1's convention) — never the same `false` that means "another machine won". Permanent conditions (no admin client, missing seed row, malformed date) still return `false`: retrying cannot fix them.
- AC2: On such an error the caller leaves the day unmarked and retries next tick; a genuine `false` still ends its day. Because the day lock itself is the cross-machine gate, a retry can never double-run a job another machine already claimed.
- Tests: 🟡 `cron-lock.test.ts` pins AC1 (update error → rejects; verify error → rejects; won/lost/missing-seed/bad-date → boolean). `reminder-v2-cron.server.test.ts` pins AC2 for the reminder caller (rejection → re-attempt next tick then run; false → no re-attempt). The other two callers (trending, youtube-bot-summary) inherit AC2 through their existing tick catch — review-verified only (identical tick shape; exercising each would repeat the reminder test around modules that self-start on import — trending's starter is disabled under NODE_ENV=test, and the summary cron's missing test guard is flagged follow-up drift).
- Origin: the US-27 platform fault also hit `tryAcquireCronLock` (JAVASCRIPT-REMIX-66: 4 events 08-26/27; -68: reminder_v2_cron + trending_cron 08-28). Every caller mapped the error's `false` to "day done", so one transient error made that machine skip its daily job; whether the job ran at all then depended on the other machine winning the lock.
- **The chat digest is deleted (Brad, 2026-09-10).** One of the two ops summaries mailed every chat turn and reply of the past day to Brad — message BODIES, found by an audit of what a skeptical assistant reads out of this repo. Gone with it: the module, its admin trigger, its SIGTERM stop, its cron-lock name and its seed row; nothing imported it but itself. Brad: "I don't have time to read the responses anyway." The count stays five because `chat_text_purge` (US-15 AC7) took its place in the lock table, and the AC1/AC2 behaviour above is unchanged.
- Status: shipped by sentry-fix's Tier 3 PR #35, deployed 2026-08-28 — the day the first genuine reminder send came due inside the fault window (US-17). REMIX-66/68 quiet since; -68 marked resolved.

### US-51 · Brad's embedded-admin buttons run their action — **added 2026-10-21 (Sentry 7803370248, found live after the b625b92f deploy)**
As Brad, when I press a button in the embedded admin (run the trending cron, the reminders or YouTube summary trigger, create or stop an A/B test), the action runs on both Fly apps.
- AC1: a form POST from the embedded admin reaches its route's action. Fly terminates TLS and `react-router-serve` sets no `trust proxy`, so react-router builds `request.url` as `http://<app>.fly.dev` while the browser sends `Origin: https://<app>.fly.dev`; react-router's CSRF check (since 7.12) compared the two and answered every admin action 400 in 3 ms. `react-router.config.ts` `allowedActionOrigins` lists exactly the two app hosts, `health-tool-app.fly.dev` and `health-tool-edu.fly.dev`. The check matches the Origin's host only, so any other origin (another host, a lookalike suffix, `*.fly.dev`, `admin.shopify.com`, `null`, localhost) still gets 400 before the action. The check covers UI-route actions only, single-fetch (`.data`) and document POSTs alike; resource routes (`/api/*`, `/webhooks/*`, `/mcp`) are not checked by react-router and rely on their own auth. Besides the admin routes, the one UI-route action that now passes same-origin is `/auth/login`'s form POST (Shopify's `login()`, already capped by US-09 AC25). CORS is untouched. Residual, stated: each app also accepts an action POST whose Origin is the other app's host; both are ours. The list is static because the build runs once per app without `SHOPIFY_APP_URL`; a new app host must be added here.
- Tests: ✅ `app/routes/admin-action-origin.test.ts` (the real react-router request handler with the config's list: an https Origin to an http request.url runs the action on both hosts; no Origin runs it; six foreign origins get 400 and never reach the action; a document POST without `.data` behaves the same, allowed and refused).
